questions.question: You migrated your applications to Google Cloud Platform and kept your existing monitoring platform. You now find that your notification system is too slow for time critical problems.What should you do?

options.text: Replace your entire monitoring platform with Stackdriver.
Install the Stackdriver agents on your Compute Engine instances.
Use Stackdriver to capture and alert on logs, then ship them to your existing platform.
Migrate some traffic back to your old platform and perform AB testing on the two platforms concurrently.

questions.correct_text: Use Stackdriver to capture and alert on logs, then ship them to your existing platform.
questions.explanation: Because the team wants to keep its existing monitoring platform but needs faster alerting, the best approach is to use Cloud (Stackdriver) Monitoring/Logging to capture and alert on logs for time-critical issues and then forward those logs to the existing platform, giving fast native notifications without abandoning current tooling. Option A is excessive and unnecessary since a full platform replacement is not required to fix slow notifications. Option B only installs agents to collect metrics and does not by itself solve the slow notification problem. Option D introduces A/B testing of monitoring platforms, which adds risk and complexity without addressing alert speed. Capturing and alerting in Cloud Logging while shipping to the existing system delivers the needed speed with minimal disruption.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Como a equipe quer manter sua plataforma de monitoramento existente, mas precisa de alertas mais rápidos, a melhor abordagem é usar o Cloud (Stackdriver) Monitoring/Logging para capturar e alertar sobre logs de problemas críticos em relação ao tempo e, em seguida, encaminhar esses logs para a plataforma existente, oferecendo notificações nativas rápidas sem abandonar as ferramentas atuais. A opção A é excessiva e desnecessária, já que uma substituição completa da plataforma não é necessária para corrigir notificações lentas. A opção B apenas instala agentes para coletar métricas e, por si só, não resolve o problema de notificações lentas. A opção D introduz testes A/B de plataformas de monitoramento, o que adiciona risco e complexidade sem resolver a velocidade dos alertas. Capturar e alertar no Cloud Logging enquanto envia os dados ao sistema existente proporciona a velocidade necessária com mínima disrupção.

questions.question: You are planning to migrate a MySQL database to the managed Cloud SQL database for Google Cloud. You have Compute Engine virtual machine instances that will connect with this Cloud SQL instance. You do not want to whitelist IPs for the Compute Engine instances to be able to access Cloud SQL.What should you do?

options.text: Enable private IP for the Cloud SQL instance.
Whitelist a project to access Cloud SQL, and add Compute Engine instances in the whitelisted project.
Create a role in Cloud SQL that allows access to the database from external instances, and assign the Compute Engine instances to that role.
Create a CloudSQL instance on one project. Create Compute engine instances in a different project. Create a VPN between these two projects to allow internal access to CloudSQL.

questions.correct_text: Enable private IP for the Cloud SQL instance.
questions.explanation: Enabling private IP for the Cloud SQL instance lets Compute Engine instances in the same VPC connect over internal RFC 1918 addresses through private services access, eliminating the need to whitelist public IPs. Option B's project-based whitelisting is not how Cloud SQL authorized networks work, which operate on IP ranges, not projects. Option C is incorrect because Cloud SQL roles control database privileges, not network access from external instances. Option D adds an unnecessary cross-project VPN; private IP within a single VPC is simpler and avoids public exposure entirely. Thus enabling private IP is the correct, secure solution.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Habilitar o IP privado para a instância do Cloud SQL permite que instâncias do Compute Engine na mesma VPC se conectem por endereços internos RFC 1918 através do private services access, eliminando a necessidade de incluir IPs públicos em uma lista de permissões. O whitelisting baseado em projeto da opção B não é como funcionam as authorized networks do Cloud SQL, que operam com faixas de IP, não com projetos. A opção C está incorreta porque os papéis do Cloud SQL controlam privilégios de banco de dados, não o acesso de rede a partir de instâncias externas. A opção D adiciona uma VPN entre projetos desnecessária; o IP privado dentro de uma única VPC é mais simples e evita totalmente a exposição pública. Assim, habilitar o IP privado é a solução correta e segura.

questions.question: You have deployed an HTTP(s) Load Balancer with the gcloud commands shown below.Health checks to port 80 on the Compute Engine virtual machine instance are failing and no traffic is sent to your instances. You want to resolve the problem.Which commands should you run?

options.text: gcloud compute instances add-access-config ${NAME}-backend-instance-1
gcloud compute instances add-tags ${NAME}-backend-instance-1 --tags http-server
gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-lb --network load-balancer --allow tcp --source-ranges 130.211.0.0/22,35.191.0.0/16 --direction INGRESS
gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-lb --network load-balancer --allow tcp --destination-ranges 130.211.0.0/22,35.191.0.0/16 --direction EGRESS

questions.correct_text: gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-lb --network load-balancer --allow tcp --source-ranges 130.211.0.0/22,35.191.0.0/16 --direction INGRESS
questions.explanation: HTTP(S) Load Balancer health checks and traffic originate from Google's dedicated probe ranges 130.211.0.0/22 and 35.191.0.0/16, so an ingress firewall rule allowing TCP from those source ranges is required for health checks to pass and traffic to reach the instances. Option C creates exactly that ingress allow rule. Option A adds an external access config, which is unrelated to internal load balancer health probes. Option B adds an http-server tag but does nothing useful unless a matching firewall rule exists, and it does not open the probe ranges. Option D is wrong because it creates an EGRESS rule using destination-ranges, whereas the probes arrive as inbound traffic that must be permitted via ingress source ranges.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: As verificações de integridade (health checks) e o tráfego do HTTP(S) Load Balancer têm origem nas faixas de probe dedicadas do Google, 130.211.0.0/22 e 35.191.0.0/16, portanto é necessária uma regra de firewall de ingress permitindo TCP a partir dessas faixas de origem para que as verificações de integridade passem e o tráfego chegue às instâncias. A opção C cria exatamente essa regra de ingress allow. A opção A adiciona uma access config externa, o que não tem relação com as verificações de integridade internas do load balancer. A opção B adiciona uma tag http-server, mas não faz nada útil a menos que exista uma regra de firewall correspondente, e não abre as faixas de probe. A opção D está errada porque cria uma regra de EGRESS usando destination-ranges, enquanto os probes chegam como tráfego de entrada que deve ser permitido via faixas de origem de ingress.

questions.question: Your website is deployed on Compute Engine. Your marketing team wants to test conversion rates between 3 different website designs.Which approach should you use?

options.text: Deploy the website on App Engine and use traffic splitting.
Deploy the website on App Engine as three separate services.
Deploy the website on Cloud Functions and use traffic splitting.
Deploy the website on Cloud Functions as three separate functions.

questions.correct_text: Deploy the website on App Engine and use traffic splitting.
questions.explanation: App Engine supports native traffic splitting across multiple versions of a service, letting the marketing team route percentages of users to three different website designs to compare conversion rates, which is ideal for A/B testing. Option B deploying three separate services would not provide built-in percentage-based traffic distribution across a single endpoint for comparison. Options C and D rely on Cloud Functions, which is intended for event-driven backend logic rather than hosting a full website, and Cloud Functions does not offer the same versioned traffic-splitting feature for web front ends. Therefore deploying on App Engine and using traffic splitting is the correct approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: O App Engine oferece suporte nativo a divisão de tráfego (traffic splitting) entre várias versões de um serviço, permitindo que a equipe de marketing roteie porcentagens de usuários para três designs diferentes de site para comparar taxas de conversão, o que é ideal para testes A/B. A opção B, que implanta três serviços separados, não forneceria distribuição de tráfego baseada em porcentagem de forma integrada em um único endpoint para comparação. As opções C e D dependem do Cloud Functions, que é destinado a lógica de backend orientada a eventos em vez de hospedar um site completo, e o Cloud Functions não oferece o mesmo recurso de divisão de tráfego por versão para front ends web. Portanto, implantar no App Engine e usar a divisão de tráfego é a abordagem correta.

options.text: gsutil cp --project ג€my-gcp-projectג€ -r ~/local-scripts/ gcp-instance-name:~/server-scripts/ --zone ג€us-east1-bג€
gsutil cp --project ג€my-gcp-projectג€ -R ~/local-scripts/ gcp-instance-name:~/server-scripts/ --zone ג€us-east1-bג€
gcloud compute scp --project ג€my-gcp-projectג€ --recurse ~/local-scripts/ gcp-instance-name:~/server-scripts/ --zone ג€us-east1-bג€
gcloud compute mv --project ג€my-gcp-projectג€ --recurse ~/local-scripts/ gcp-instance-name:~/server-scripts/ --zone ג€us-east1-bג€

questions.correct_text: gcloud compute scp --project ג€my-gcp-projectג€ --recurse ~/local-scripts/ gcp-instance-name:~/server-scripts/ --zone ג€us-east1-bג€
questions.explanation: To copy a local directory and its contents to a Compute Engine VM you use gcloud compute scp with the --recurse flag, which securely transfers files over SSH to the instance. Option C is correct because gcloud compute scp is the supported tool for moving files between a workstation and a VM, and --recurse handles the directory tree. Options A and B use gsutil cp, which is for Cloud Storage buckets, not direct VM transfers, and gsutil does not accept a VM instance name as a destination. Option D uses gcloud compute mv, which is not a valid command. Therefore only C provides a correct, working recursive copy to the instance.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Para copiar um diretório local e seu conteúdo para uma VM do Compute Engine você usa gcloud compute scp com a flag --recurse, que transfere arquivos de forma segura via SSH para a instância. A opção C é correta porque gcloud compute scp é a ferramenta suportada para mover arquivos entre uma estação de trabalho e uma VM, e --recurse lida com a árvore de diretórios. As opções A e B usam gsutil cp, que é para buckets do Cloud Storage, não para transferências diretas para VMs, e o gsutil não aceita um nome de instância de VM como destino. A opção D usa gcloud compute mv, que não é um comando válido. Portanto, apenas C fornece uma cópia recursiva correta e funcional para a instância.

questions.question: You are deploying your application to a Compute Engine virtual machine instance with the Stackdriver Monitoring Agent installed. Your application is a unix process on the instance. You want to be alerted if the unix process has not run for at least 5 minutes. You are not able to change the application to generate metrics or logs.Which alert condition should you configure?

options.text: Uptime check
Process health
Metric absence
Metric threshold

questions.correct_text: Process health
questions.explanation: Because the Monitoring Agent collects process metrics, the running unix process generates a metric while it is alive, and that metric stops being written when the process dies. A Metric absence condition fires when no data points for the selected metric arrive within a chosen window (here 5 minutes), which precisely detects that the process has not run. Option C is therefore correct. Process health (B) is a concept rather than a standalone alert condition type that satisfies this requirement, and uptime checks (A) probe network endpoints, not arbitrary local unix processes. Metric threshold (D) needs the metric to still be reported to compare a value, but a stopped process emits no value, so absence is the right approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Como o Monitoring Agent coleta métricas de processo, o processo unix em execução gera uma métrica enquanto está ativo, e essa métrica deixa de ser registrada quando o processo morre. Uma condição de ausência de métrica (Metric absence) é acionada quando nenhum ponto de dados da métrica selecionada chega dentro de uma janela escolhida (aqui 5 minutos), o que detecta com precisão que o processo não foi executado. A opção C é, portanto, correta. Process health (B) é um conceito e não um tipo autônomo de condição de alerta que satisfaça esse requisito, e uptime checks (A) sondam endpoints de rede, não processos unix locais arbitrários. Metric threshold (D) precisa que a métrica continue sendo reportada para comparar um valor, mas um processo parado não emite nenhum valor, então a ausência é a abordagem correta.

questions.question: You have two tables in an ANSI-SQL compliant database with identical columns that you need to quickly combine into a single table, removing duplicate rows from the result set.What should you do?

options.text: Use the JOIN operator in SQL to combine the tables.
Use nested WITH statements to combine the tables.
Use the UNION operator in SQL to combine the tables.
Use the UNION ALL operator in SQL to combine the tables.

questions.correct_text: Use the UNION operator in SQL to combine the tables.
questions.explanation: The requirement is to combine two tables with identical columns into one result set while removing duplicate rows. In ANSI SQL the UNION operator concatenates the rows of two queries and, by default, eliminates duplicate rows, which is exactly what is needed, so option C is correct. UNION ALL (D) also concatenates but keeps all duplicates, so it fails the de-duplication requirement. JOIN (A) merges tables horizontally by matching keys across columns rather than stacking rows, and nested WITH statements (B) only define common table expressions and do not by themselves merge or de-duplicate data. Thus UNION is the appropriate set operator here.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O requisito é combinar duas tabelas com colunas idênticas em um único conjunto de resultados, removendo linhas duplicadas. No SQL ANSI, o operador UNION concatena as linhas de duas consultas e, por padrão, elimina linhas duplicadas, que é exatamente o necessário, então a opção C é correta. UNION ALL (D) também concatena, mas mantém todas as duplicatas, portanto falha no requisito de remoção de duplicatas. JOIN (A) mescla tabelas horizontalmente combinando chaves entre colunas em vez de empilhar linhas, e instruções WITH aninhadas (B) apenas definem common table expressions e por si só não mesclam nem removem duplicatas dos dados. Assim, UNION é o operador de conjunto apropriado aqui.

questions.question: You have an application deployed in production. When a new version is deployed, some issues don't arise until the application receives traffic from users in production. You want to reduce both the impact and the number of users affected.Which deployment strategy should you use?

options.text: Blue/green deployment
Canary deployment
Rolling deployment
Recreate deployment

questions.correct_text: Canary deployment
questions.explanation: A canary deployment releases the new version to a small subset of production traffic first, so problems that only surface under real user load are detected while affecting very few users, which directly minimizes both impact and the number of users affected. Option B is therefore correct. Blue/green (A) switches all traffic from the old to the new environment at once, exposing every user simultaneously if the new version is faulty. Rolling deployment (C) gradually replaces instances but typically routes normal traffic proportionally and offers less precise control over the exposed fraction than canary. Recreate (D) tears down the old version and starts the new one, causing downtime and full exposure, so it is the worst fit for limiting blast radius.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Uma implantação canary libera a nova versão primeiro para um pequeno subconjunto do tráfego de produção, de modo que problemas que só aparecem sob carga real de usuários sejam detectados afetando muito poucos usuários, o que minimiza diretamente tanto o impacto quanto o número de usuários afetados. A opção B é, portanto, correta. Blue/green (A) muda todo o tráfego do ambiente antigo para o novo de uma só vez, expondo todos os usuários simultaneamente se a nova versão estiver com falhas. A implantação rolling (C) substitui instâncias gradualmente, mas normalmente roteia o tráfego de forma proporcional e oferece controle menos preciso sobre a fração exposta do que o canary. Recreate (D) derruba a versão antiga e inicia a nova, causando indisponibilidade e exposição total, sendo a pior opção para limitar o raio de impacto.

questions.question: Your company wants to expand their users outside the United States for their popular application. The company wants to ensure 99.999% availability of the database for their application and also wants to minimize the read latency for their users across the globe.Which two actions should they take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a multi-regional Cloud Spanner instance with "nam-asia-eur1" configuration.
Create a multi-regional Cloud Spanner instance with "nam3" configuration.
Create a cluster with at least 3 Spanner nodes.
Create a cluster with at least 1 Spanner node.
Create a minimum of two Cloud Spanner instances in separate regions with at least one node.
Create a Cloud Dataflow pipeline to replicate data across different databases.

questions.correct_text: Create a multi-regional Cloud Spanner instance with "nam-asia-eur1" configuration. | Create a cluster with at least 3 Spanner nodes.
questions.explanation: To serve users globally with low read latency and 99.999% availability, a single multi-regional Cloud Spanner instance is required because multi-region configurations replicate data across continents and provide the five-nines SLA. Option A's nam-asia-eur1 configuration spans North America, Asia, and Europe, placing replicas close to worldwide users for low read latency, while option C's minimum of three nodes is recommended for production-grade capacity and resilience. The nam3 configuration (B) is a North-America-only multi-region, so it does not minimize latency for users outside the US. Option D (one node) is sub-production scale, option E (separate single-region instances) does not give a single globally consistent multi-region database, and option F (Dataflow replication) is a custom batch approach that does not deliver Spanner's synchronous global availability. Hence A and C are correct.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para atender usuários globalmente com baixa latência de leitura e disponibilidade de 99,999%, é necessária uma única instância multi-regional do Cloud Spanner, porque as configurações multi-region replicam os dados entre continentes e oferecem o SLA de cinco noves. A configuração nam-asia-eur1 da opção A abrange América do Norte, Ásia e Europa, posicionando réplicas próximas aos usuários do mundo todo para baixa latência de leitura, enquanto o mínimo de três nós da opção C é recomendado para capacidade e resiliência de nível de produção. A configuração nam3 (B) é uma multi-region apenas da América do Norte, portanto não minimiza a latência para usuários fora dos EUA. A opção D (um nó) está abaixo da escala de produção, a opção E (instâncias separadas de região única) não oferece um único banco de dados multi-region globalmente consistente, e a opção F (replicação via Dataflow) é uma abordagem de batch customizada que não entrega a disponibilidade global síncrona do Spanner. Por isso, A e C estão corretas.

questions.question: You need to migrate an internal file upload API with an enforced 500-MB file size limit to App Engine.What should you do?

options.text: Use FTP to upload files.
Use CPanel to upload files.
Use signed URLs to upload files.
Change the API to be a multipart file upload API.

questions.correct_text: Use signed URLs to upload files.
questions.explanation: App Engine has a request size limit of 32 MB, so a 500-MB file cannot be sent directly through the application. The correct approach is to use signed URLs to Cloud Storage, which let the client upload large files directly to a bucket without routing the payload through App Engine, bypassing the request size limit while still controlling who can upload. FTP and CPanel are not supported mechanisms in App Engine and are not relevant to modern cloud uploads. Converting to a multipart upload API does not help because the data would still pass through App Engine and remain subject to the 32-MB request limit.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O App Engine tem um limite de tamanho de requisição de 32 MB, então um arquivo de 500 MB não pode ser enviado diretamente através da aplicação. A abordagem correta é usar signed URLs para o Cloud Storage, que permitem ao cliente fazer upload de arquivos grandes diretamente para um bucket sem rotear o payload através do App Engine, contornando o limite de tamanho de requisição enquanto ainda controla quem pode fazer upload. FTP e CPanel não são mecanismos suportados no App Engine e não são relevantes para uploads modernos na nuvem. Converter para uma API de upload multipart não ajuda, porque os dados ainda passariam pelo App Engine e continuariam sujeitos ao limite de requisição de 32 MB.

questions.question: Your teammate has asked you to review the code below. Its purpose is to efficiently add a large number of small rows to a BigQuery table.Which improvement should you suggest your teammate make?

options.text: Include multiple rows with each request.
Perform the inserts in parallel by creating multiple threads.
Write each row to a Cloud Storage object, then load into BigQuery.
Write each row to a Cloud Storage object in parallel, then load into BigQuery.

questions.correct_text: Include multiple rows with each request.
questions.explanation: When inserting many small rows into BigQuery via streaming inserts (tabledata.insertAll), the most efficient improvement is to batch multiple rows into each request rather than sending one row per request, which reduces HTTP overhead and stays well within API quotas. Spawning many parallel threads of single-row inserts increases request count and can quickly hit streaming insert rate limits without improving efficiency. Writing each row to a separate Cloud Storage object and loading it is inefficient because it creates excessive tiny objects and load jobs, adding latency and quota pressure. Doing those writes in parallel has the same problems and adds complexity, so batching rows per request is the cleanest optimization.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Ao inserir muitas linhas pequenas no BigQuery via streaming inserts (tabledata.insertAll), a melhoria mais eficiente é agrupar várias linhas em cada requisição em vez de enviar uma linha por requisição, o que reduz o overhead de HTTP e mantém-se bem dentro das cotas da API. Disparar muitas threads paralelas de inserções de uma única linha aumenta a contagem de requisições e pode rapidamente atingir os limites de taxa dos streaming inserts sem melhorar a eficiência. Escrever cada linha em um objeto separado do Cloud Storage e carregá-lo é ineficiente, porque cria objetos minúsculos e jobs de load em excesso, adicionando latência e pressão sobre as cotas. Fazer essas escritas em paralelo tem os mesmos problemas e adiciona complexidade, então agrupar linhas por requisição é a otimização mais limpa.

questions.question: You are developing a JPEG image-resizing API hosted on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Callers of the service will exist within the same GKE cluster. You want clients to be able to get the IP address of the service.What should you do?

options.text: Define a GKE Service. Clients should use the name of the A record in Cloud DNS to find the service's cluster IP address.
Define a GKE Service. Clients should use the service name in the URL to connect to the service.
Define a GKE Endpoint. Clients should get the endpoint name from the appropriate environment variable in the client container.
Define a GKE Endpoint. Clients should get the endpoint name from Cloud DNS.

questions.correct_text: Define a GKE Service. Clients should use the service name in the URL to connect to the service.
questions.explanation: In GKE, a Service provides a stable virtual ClusterIP and an internal DNS name automatically created by kube-dns/CoreDNS, so in-cluster clients should simply connect using the service name in the URL, which resolves to the service's cluster IP. Cloud DNS is for external/managed DNS zones and is not how in-cluster service discovery works, so referencing an A record in Cloud DNS is incorrect. A GKE Endpoint object is not a discovery mechanism that clients query by name through environment variables or Cloud DNS for this purpose; Endpoints are managed by the Service controller and not consumed directly this way. Using the service name leverages built-in cluster DNS, which is the standard and simplest approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: No GKE, um Service fornece um ClusterIP virtual estável e um nome DNS interno criado automaticamente pelo kube-dns/CoreDNS, então clientes dentro do cluster devem simplesmente conectar-se usando o nome do service na URL, que resolve para o cluster IP do service. O Cloud DNS é para zonas DNS externas/gerenciadas e não é como funciona a descoberta de serviços dentro do cluster, então referenciar um registro A no Cloud DNS está incorreto. Um objeto Endpoint do GKE não é um mecanismo de descoberta que os clientes consultam por nome através de variáveis de ambiente ou Cloud DNS para esse propósito; os Endpoints são gerenciados pelo Service controller e não são consumidos diretamente dessa forma. Usar o nome do service aproveita o DNS interno do cluster, que é a abordagem padrão e mais simples.

questions.question: You are using Cloud Build to build and test application source code stored in Cloud Source Repositories. The build process requires a build tool not available in the Cloud Build environment.What should you do?

options.text: Download the binary from the internet during the build process.
Build a custom cloud builder image and reference the image in your build steps.
Include the binary in your Cloud Source Repositories repository and reference it in your build scripts.
Ask to have the binary added to the Cloud Build environment by filing a feature request against the Cloud Build public Issue Tracker.

questions.correct_text: Build a custom cloud builder image and reference the image in your build steps.
questions.explanation: Cloud Build runs each build step inside a container (a cloud builder), so the correct way to add a missing tool is to build a custom builder image that includes the tool and reference that image in your build steps. Downloading the binary from the internet during every build is slower, less reproducible, and introduces a dependency on external availability and integrity. Committing the binary into Cloud Source Repositories pollutes the source repo with platform-specific artifacts and is poor practice for build tooling. Filing a feature request to have the tool added to the Cloud Build environment is not a practical or timely solution, since custom builder images are the supported extension mechanism.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Build executa cada etapa de build dentro de um container (um cloud builder), então a forma correta de adicionar uma ferramenta ausente é construir uma imagem de builder customizada que inclua a ferramenta e referenciar essa imagem nas suas etapas de build. Baixar o binário da internet a cada build é mais lento, menos reproduzível e introduz uma dependência da disponibilidade e integridade de fontes externas. Fazer commit do binário no Cloud Source Repositories polui o repositório de código com artefatos específicos de plataforma e é uma prática ruim para ferramentas de build. Abrir uma solicitação de recurso para que a ferramenta seja adicionada ao ambiente do Cloud Build não é uma solução prática ou rápida, já que as imagens de builder customizadas são o mecanismo de extensão suportado.

questions.question: You are deploying your application to a Compute Engine virtual machine instance. Your application is configured to write its log files to disk. You want to view the logs in Stackdriver Logging without changing the application code.What should you do?

options.text: Install the Stackdriver Logging Agent and configure it to send the application logs.
Use a Stackdriver Logging Library to log directly from the application to Stackdriver Logging.
Provide the log file folder path in the metadata of the instance to configure it to send the application logs.
Change the application to log to /var/log so that its logs are automatically sent to Stackdriver Logging.

questions.correct_text: Install the Stackdriver Logging Agent and configure it to send the application logs.
questions.explanation: Because the application already writes logs to files on disk and you cannot change the code, the right solution is to install the Cloud Logging (Stackdriver) Logging Agent on the Compute Engine instance and configure it to tail and forward those log files to Cloud Logging. Using a logging library would require modifying the application code, which is explicitly disallowed. There is no instance metadata field that points to a log folder to automatically ship logs, so that option is invalid. Writing to /var/log does not automatically forward logs to Cloud Logging without an agent, and it would also require changing the application, so installing and configuring the agent is the correct choice.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Como a aplicação já grava logs em arquivos no disco e você não pode alterar o código, a solução correta é instalar o Logging Agent do Cloud Logging (Stackdriver) na instância do Compute Engine e configurá-lo para acompanhar (tail) e encaminhar esses arquivos de log para o Cloud Logging. Usar uma biblioteca de logging exigiria modificar o código da aplicação, o que é explicitamente proibido. Não existe nenhum campo de metadados da instância que aponte para uma pasta de logs para enviar os logs automaticamente, então essa opção é inválida. Gravar em /var/log não encaminha automaticamente os logs para o Cloud Logging sem um agente, e também exigiria alterar a aplicação, portanto instalar e configurar o agente é a escolha correta.

questions.question: Your service adds text to images that it reads from Cloud Storage. During busy times of the year, requests to Cloud Storage fail with an HTTP 429 "Too ManyRequests" status code.How should you handle this error?

options.text: Add a cache-control header to the objects.
Request a quota increase from the GCP Console.
Retry the request with a truncated exponential backoff strategy.
Change the storage class of the Cloud Storage bucket to Multi-regional.

questions.correct_text: Retry the request with a truncated exponential backoff strategy.
questions.explanation: An HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests' response from Cloud Storage indicates rate limiting because the request rate exceeded what the service or bucket can currently sustain. The recommended way to handle transient throttling errors (429 and 5xx) is to retry the failed request using a truncated exponential backoff strategy, which spaces out retries with increasing delays plus jitter to let the backend recover. Requesting a quota increase does not directly address per-bucket request-rate throttling, which is governed by ramp-up and auto-scaling rather than a console quota, and it ignores the transient nature of the error. A cache-control header only affects caching behavior of served objects, and changing the storage class to Multi-regional changes geographic redundancy, neither of which resolves request-rate throttling.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Uma resposta HTTP 429 'Too Many Requests' do Cloud Storage indica limitação de taxa (rate limiting), porque a taxa de requisições excedeu o que o serviço ou bucket consegue sustentar no momento. A forma recomendada de lidar com erros transitórios de throttling (429 e 5xx) é repetir a requisição que falhou usando uma estratégia de truncated exponential backoff, que espaça as tentativas com atrasos crescentes mais jitter para permitir que o backend se recupere. Solicitar um aumento de cota não resolve diretamente o throttling de taxa de requisições por bucket, que é governado por ramp-up e auto-scaling em vez de uma cota do console, e ignora a natureza transitória do erro. Um cabeçalho cache-control afeta apenas o comportamento de cache dos objetos servidos, e mudar a classe de armazenamento para Multi-regional altera a redundância geográfica; nenhuma dessas opções resolve o throttling de taxa de requisições.

questions.question: You are building an API that will be used by Android and iOS apps. The API must:* Support HTTPs* Minimize bandwidth cost* Integrate easily with mobile appsWhich API architecture should you use?

options.text: RESTful APIs
MQTT for APIs
gRPC-based APIs
SOAP-based APIs

questions.correct_text: gRPC-based APIs
questions.explanation: gRPC is the best fit when you need HTTPS support, minimized bandwidth, and easy mobile integration. gRPC uses HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers, a compact binary serialization format that significantly reduces payload size and bandwidth compared to text-based formats, and it provides generated client stubs for Android and iOS, making integration straightforward. RESTful APIs typically use verbose JSON over HTTP/1.1, which consumes more bandwidth than Protobuf binary messages. MQTT is a publish/subscribe messaging protocol designed for IoT telemetry, not a general application API, and SOAP relies on heavyweight XML envelopes that increase bandwidth and complexity, making both poor choices here.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: gRPC é a melhor opção quando você precisa de suporte a HTTPS, largura de banda minimizada e integração fácil com dispositivos móveis. O gRPC usa HTTP/2 e Protocol Buffers, um formato de serialização binária compacto que reduz significativamente o tamanho do payload e a largura de banda em comparação com formatos baseados em texto, e fornece client stubs gerados para Android e iOS, tornando a integração simples. APIs RESTful normalmente usam JSON verboso sobre HTTP/1.1, que consome mais largura de banda do que mensagens binárias em Protobuf. MQTT é um protocolo de mensagens publish/subscribe projetado para telemetria de IoT, não uma API de aplicação genérica, e SOAP depende de envelopes XML pesados que aumentam a largura de banda e a complexidade, tornando ambos escolhas ruins aqui.

questions.question: Your application takes an input from a user and publishes it to the user's contacts. This input is stored in a table in Cloud Spanner. Your application is more sensitive to latency and less sensitive to consistency.How should you perform reads from Cloud Spanner for this application?

options.text: Perform Read-Only transactions.
Perform stale reads using single-read methods.
Perform strong reads using single-read methods.
Perform stale reads using read-write transactions.

questions.correct_text: Perform stale reads using single-read methods.
questions.explanation: When an application prioritizes low latency over strong consistency, stale reads with single-read (single-use) methods are the correct approach in Cloud Spanner. A stale read reads data at a timestamp in the past (with a bounded or exact staleness), allowing Spanner to serve the read from the nearest available replica without waiting to confirm it has the absolute latest data, which lowers latency. Strong reads guarantee the most recent committed data but require coordination that increases latency, the opposite of what is wanted. Read-only transactions provide consistent reads across multiple statements but add overhead and are unnecessary for a single latency-sensitive read, and stale reads cannot be performed within read-write transactions, which always use strong consistency.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Quando uma aplicação prioriza baixa latência em vez de consistência forte, stale reads com métodos de leitura única (single-use) são a abordagem correta no Cloud Spanner. Uma stale read lê dados em um timestamp no passado (com staleness limitada ou exata), permitindo que o Spanner sirva a leitura a partir da réplica disponível mais próxima sem esperar para confirmar que possui os dados absolutamente mais recentes, o que reduz a latência. Strong reads garantem os dados mais recentemente confirmados (committed), mas exigem coordenação que aumenta a latência, o oposto do que se deseja. Read-only transactions fornecem leituras consistentes em múltiplas instruções, mas adicionam sobrecarga e são desnecessárias para uma única leitura sensível à latência, e stale reads não podem ser realizadas dentro de read-write transactions, que sempre usam consistência forte.

questions.question: Your application is deployed in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. When a new version of your application is released, your CI/CD tool updates the spec.template.spec.containers[0].image value to reference the Docker image of your new application version. When the Deployment object applies the change, you want to deploy at least 1 replica of the new version and maintain the previous replicas until the new replica is healthy.Which change should you make to the GKE Deployment object shown below?

options.text: Set the Deployment strategy to RollingUpdate with maxSurge set to 0, maxUnavailable set to 1.
Set the Deployment strategy to RollingUpdate with maxSurge set to 1, maxUnavailable set to 0.
Set the Deployment strategy to Recreate with maxSurge set to 0, maxUnavailable set to 1.
Set the Deployment strategy to Recreate with maxSurge set to 1, maxUnavailable set to 0.

questions.correct_text: Set the Deployment strategy to RollingUpdate with maxSurge set to 1, maxUnavailable set to 0.
questions.explanation: The requirement is to bring up at least one new replica and keep the old replicas running until the new one is healthy, which is exactly what a RollingUpdate strategy with maxSurge=1 and maxUnavailable=0 achieves. maxSurge=1 lets the Deployment create one extra Pod above the desired count for the new version, and maxUnavailable=0 ensures no existing Pods are removed until the new Pod passes its readiness checks, preserving full availability during the rollout. The Recreate strategy first terminates all old Pods before creating new ones, causing downtime and violating the requirement, and it does not honor maxSurge/maxUnavailable. Setting maxSurge=0 with maxUnavailable=1 would remove an old replica before adding the new one, reducing capacity rather than maintaining the previous replicas.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: O requisito é subir pelo menos uma nova réplica e manter as réplicas antigas em execução até que a nova esteja saudável, que é exatamente o que uma estratégia RollingUpdate com maxSurge=1 e maxUnavailable=0 alcança. maxSurge=1 permite que o Deployment crie um Pod extra acima da contagem desejada para a nova versão, e maxUnavailable=0 garante que nenhum Pod existente seja removido até que o novo Pod passe em suas verificações de readiness, preservando a disponibilidade total durante o rollout. A estratégia Recreate primeiro encerra todos os Pods antigos antes de criar os novos, causando indisponibilidade e violando o requisito, e não respeita maxSurge/maxUnavailable. Definir maxSurge=0 com maxUnavailable=1 removeria uma réplica antiga antes de adicionar a nova, reduzindo a capacidade em vez de manter as réplicas anteriores.

questions.question: You plan to make a simple HTML application available on the internet. This site keeps information about FAQs for your application. The application is static and contains images, HTML, CSS, and Javascript. You want to make this application available on the internet with as few steps as possible.What should you do?

options.text: Upload your application to Cloud Storage.
Upload your application to an App Engine environment.
Create a Compute Engine instance with Apache web server installed. Configure Apache web server to host the application.
Containerize your application first. Deploy this container to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and assign an external IP address to the GKE pod hosting the application.

questions.correct_text: Upload your application to Cloud Storage.
questions.explanation: For a purely static site consisting of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images, hosting the files in Cloud Storage is the simplest path to publish on the internet. Cloud Storage supports static website hosting directly: you upload the files to a bucket, make them publicly readable, and serve them, with no servers to provision or manage. Deploying to App Engine adds an application runtime and configuration that is unnecessary for static content. Creating a Compute Engine VM with Apache requires provisioning, patching, and managing the instance, and containerizing the app for GKE introduces even more operational overhead, so both involve far more steps than uploading to a bucket.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para um site puramente estático composto de HTML, CSS, JavaScript e imagens, hospedar os arquivos no Cloud Storage é o caminho mais simples para publicar na internet. O Cloud Storage oferece suporte direto à hospedagem de sites estáticos: você envia os arquivos para um bucket, os torna publicamente legíveis e os serve, sem servidores para provisionar ou gerenciar. Fazer o deploy no App Engine adiciona um runtime de aplicação e configurações que são desnecessários para conteúdo estático. Criar uma VM do Compute Engine com Apache exige provisionar, aplicar patches e gerenciar a instância, e conteinerizar a aplicação para o GKE introduz ainda mais sobrecarga operacional, de modo que ambos envolvem muito mais etapas do que enviar os arquivos para um bucket.

questions.question: Your company has deployed a new API to App Engine Standard environment. During testing, the API is not behaving as expected. You want to monitor the application over time to diagnose the problem within the application code without redeploying the application.Which tool should you use?

options.text: Stackdriver Trace
Stackdriver Monitoring
Stackdriver Debug Snapshots
Stackdriver Debug Logpoints

questions.correct_text: Stackdriver Debug Logpoints
questions.explanation: Stackdriver Debug Logpoints (now Cloud Debugger logpoints) let you inject log statements into a running application without redeploying or restarting it, so you can observe behavior over time and diagnose issues directly in the production code. Debug Snapshots (C) capture the application state at a single point in time, which is useful for a one-off inspection rather than continuous monitoring over time. Stackdriver Trace (A) measures request latency across distributed services but does not expose application-internal variable values for debugging logic. Stackdriver Monitoring (B) tracks infrastructure and custom metrics, not in-code diagnostics, so it cannot pinpoint problems within the application code itself.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Os Logpoints do Stackdriver Debug (agora logpoints do Cloud Debugger) permitem injetar instruções de log em uma aplicação em execução sem precisar refazer o deploy ou reiniciá-la, para que você possa observar o comportamento ao longo do tempo e diagnosticar problemas diretamente no código em produção. Os Debug Snapshots (C) capturam o estado da aplicação em um único ponto no tempo, o que é útil para uma inspeção pontual em vez de monitoramento contínuo ao longo do tempo. O Stackdriver Trace (A) mede a latência das requisições entre serviços distribuídos, mas não expõe os valores de variáveis internas da aplicação para depurar a lógica. O Stackdriver Monitoring (B) acompanha métricas de infraestrutura e métricas personalizadas, e não diagnósticos no código, então não consegue identificar problemas dentro do próprio código da aplicação.

questions.question: You want to use the Stackdriver Logging Agent to send an application's log file to Stackdriver from a Compute Engine virtual machine instance.After installing the Stackdriver Logging Agent, what should you do first?

options.text: Enable the Error Reporting API on the project.
Grant the instance full access to all Cloud APIs.
Configure the application log file as a custom source.
Create a Stackdriver Logs Export Sink with a filter that matches the application's log entries.

questions.correct_text: Configure the application log file as a custom source.
questions.explanation: By default the Stackdriver Logging Agent (based on fluentd) collects logs from a set of well-known system locations, but an application's custom log file is not included automatically. To ingest it you must configure the application log file as a custom source in the agent's fluentd configuration so the agent knows to tail and forward those entries. Enabling the Error Reporting API (A) is unrelated to log ingestion. Granting full access to all Cloud APIs (B) is an overly broad, insecure scope and is not required just to send logs. A Logs Export Sink (D) routes already-ingested logs to a destination like BigQuery or Cloud Storage, which happens only after the logs are first collected by the agent.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Por padrão, o Stackdriver Logging Agent (baseado no fluentd) coleta logs de um conjunto de locais conhecidos do sistema, mas o arquivo de log personalizado de uma aplicação não é incluído automaticamente. Para ingeri-lo, você precisa configurar o arquivo de log da aplicação como uma fonte personalizada na configuração do fluentd do agente, para que o agente saiba que deve acompanhar (tail) e encaminhar essas entradas. Habilitar a Error Reporting API (A) não tem relação com a ingestão de logs. Conceder acesso total a todas as Cloud APIs (B) é um escopo amplo demais e inseguro, e não é necessário apenas para enviar logs. Um Logs Export Sink (D) roteia logs já ingeridos para um destino como o BigQuery ou o Cloud Storage, o que só acontece depois que os logs são primeiro coletados pelo agente.

questions.question: Your company has a BigQuery data mart that provides analytics information to hundreds of employees. One user of wants to run jobs without interrupting important workloads. This user isn't concerned about the time it takes to run these jobs. You want to fulfill this request while minimizing cost to the company and the effort required on your part.What should you do?

options.text: Ask the user to run the jobs as batch jobs.
Create a separate project for the user to run jobs.
Add the user as a job.user role in the existing project.
Allow the user to run jobs when important workloads are not running.

questions.correct_text: Ask the user to run the jobs as batch jobs.
questions.explanation: Running BigQuery queries as batch jobs queues them and starts them when idle resources become available, so they do not consume the on-demand concurrent slot capacity needed by interactive workloads and will not interrupt important jobs. Because the user is unconcerned about completion time, batch priority is a perfect fit and requires no extra cost or administrative setup. Creating a separate project (B) adds significant management overhead and does not by itself isolate slot contention under on-demand pricing. The job.user role (C) only grants permission to run jobs and does nothing to deprioritize them. Manually scheduling around important workloads (D) requires ongoing human effort and is error-prone.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Executar consultas do BigQuery como jobs em batch as coloca em uma fila e as inicia quando recursos ociosos ficam disponíveis, de modo que elas não consomem a capacidade de slots concorrentes on-demand necessária para cargas de trabalho interativas e não interromperão jobs importantes. Como o usuário não se preocupa com o tempo de conclusão, a prioridade batch é uma escolha perfeita e não exige custo adicional nem configuração administrativa. Criar um projeto separado (B) adiciona uma sobrecarga significativa de gerenciamento e, por si só, não isola a contenção de slots no modelo de preços on-demand. O papel job.user (C) apenas concede permissão para executar jobs e não faz nada para reduzir a prioridade deles. Agendar manualmente em torno das cargas de trabalho importantes (D) exige esforço humano contínuo e é propenso a erros.

questions.question: You want to notify on-call engineers about a service degradation in production while minimizing development time.What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Function to monitor resources and raise alerts.
Use Cloud Pub/Sub to monitor resources and raise alerts.
Use Stackdriver Error Reporting to capture errors and raise alerts.
Use Stackdriver Monitoring to monitor resources and raise alerts.

questions.correct_text: Use Stackdriver Monitoring to monitor resources and raise alerts.
questions.explanation: Stackdriver (Cloud) Monitoring provides built-in alerting policies and notification channels, so you can detect a production service degradation through metrics and uptime checks and automatically page on-call engineers with virtually no custom code. Building a Cloud Function (A) to poll resources and raise alerts requires writing and maintaining custom logic, increasing development time. Pub/Sub (B) is a messaging service and does not monitor resources or generate alerts on its own. Error Reporting (C) aggregates application exceptions but is limited to code-level errors and is not the general-purpose tool for monitoring overall service health and triggering on-call notifications.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Stackdriver (Cloud) Monitoring fornece políticas de alerta e canais de notificação integrados, de modo que você pode detectar a degradação de um serviço em produção por meio de métricas e verificações de uptime e acionar automaticamente os engenheiros de plantão praticamente sem código personalizado. Construir uma Cloud Function (A) para consultar recursos e gerar alertas exige escrever e manter lógica personalizada, aumentando o tempo de desenvolvimento. O Pub/Sub (B) é um serviço de mensageria e não monitora recursos nem gera alertas por conta própria. O Error Reporting (C) agrega exceções da aplicação, mas se limita a erros no nível do código e não é a ferramenta de uso geral para monitorar a saúde geral do serviço e disparar notificações de plantão.

questions.question: You are writing a single-page web application with a user-interface that communicates with a third-party API for content using XMLHttpRequest. The data displayed on the UI by the API results is less critical than other data displayed on the same web page, so it is acceptable for some requests to not have the API data displayed in the UI. However, calls made to the API should not delay rendering of other parts of the user interface. You want your application to perform well when the API response is an error or a timeout.What should you do?

options.text: Set the asynchronous option for your requests to the API to false and omit the widget displaying the API results when a timeout or error is encountered.
Set the asynchronous option for your request to the API to true and omit the widget displaying the API results when a timeout or error is encountered.
Catch timeout or error exceptions from the API call and keep trying with exponential backoff until the API response is successful.
Catch timeout or error exceptions from the API call and display the error response in the UI widget.

questions.correct_text: Set the asynchronous option for your request to the API to true and omit the widget displaying the API results when a timeout or error is encountered.
questions.explanation: Setting the asynchronous option to true makes the XMLHttpRequest non-blocking, so the rest of the UI renders without waiting on the third-party API, and omitting the widget on a timeout or error gracefully degrades since that data is non-critical. A synchronous request (A) blocks the main thread and would delay rendering of other parts of the page, defeating the performance requirement. Retrying with exponential backoff (C) keeps consuming resources and delays resolution for data that is acceptable to skip, and can leave the user waiting. Displaying the raw error in the widget (D) provides a poor user experience for content that is supposed to fail silently.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Definir a opção assíncrona como true torna o XMLHttpRequest não bloqueante, de modo que o restante da UI é renderizado sem esperar pela API de terceiros, e omitir o widget em caso de timeout ou erro degrada de forma graciosa, já que esses dados não são críticos. Uma requisição síncrona (A) bloqueia a thread principal e atrasaria a renderização de outras partes da página, anulando o requisito de desempenho. Tentar novamente com exponential backoff (C) continua consumindo recursos e atrasa a resolução para dados que podem ser ignorados, além de poder deixar o usuário esperando. Exibir o erro bruto no widget (D) proporciona uma experiência ruim para um conteúdo que deveria falhar silenciosamente.

questions.question: You are creating a web application that runs in a Compute Engine instance and writes a file to any user's Google Drive. You need to configure the application to authenticate to the Google Drive API. What should you do?

options.text: Use an OAuth Client ID that uses the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file scope to obtain an access token for each user.
Use an OAuth Client ID with delegated domain-wide authority.
Use the App Engine service account and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file scope to generate a signed JSON Web Token (JWT).
Use the App Engine service account with delegated domain-wide authority.

questions.correct_text: Use an OAuth Client ID that uses the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file scope to obtain an access token for each user.
questions.explanation: Because the application writes files to any user's own Google Drive, you need to act on behalf of each individual user, which requires per-user consent through the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow. Using an OAuth Client ID with the drive.file scope lets the app obtain an access token for each authenticated user, granting it access only to files the app creates or opens, which is the least-privilege scope for this use case. Domain-wide delegation (B and D) is only appropriate for Google Workspace administrators impersonating users within a single Workspace domain, not for arbitrary external users. A service account (C and D) represents the application itself, not an end user, so it cannot write to a user's personal Drive without that user's OAuth consent, and a signed JWT flow is used for service account or 2-legged auth, not for accessing individual users' Drives.
