questions.explanation_pt: Como a aplicação grava arquivos no Google Drive de qualquer usuário, você precisa agir em nome de cada usuário individual, o que exige o consentimento por usuário através do fluxo de autorização OAuth 2.0. Usar um OAuth Client ID com o escopo drive.file permite que o app obtenha um access token para cada usuário autenticado, concedendo acesso apenas aos arquivos que o app cria ou abre, que é o escopo de menor privilégio para este caso de uso. Domain-wide delegation (B e D) só é apropriado para administradores do Google Workspace que personificam usuários dentro de um único domínio Workspace, não para usuários externos arbitrários. Uma service account (C e D) representa a própria aplicação, não um usuário final, portanto não pode gravar no Drive pessoal de um usuário sem o consentimento OAuth desse usuário, e um fluxo de JWT assinado é usado para autenticação de service account ou two-legged, não para acessar os Drives de usuários individuais.

questions.question: You are creating a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster and run this command:The command fails with the error:You want to resolve the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Request additional GKE quota in the GCP Console.
Request additional Compute Engine quota in the GCP Console.
Open a support case to request additional GKE quota.
Decouple services in the cluster, and rewrite new clusters to function with fewer cores.

questions.correct_text: Request additional Compute Engine quota in the GCP Console.
questions.explanation: GKE clusters are built on Compute Engine virtual machines, so the CPU cores consumed by cluster nodes count against your Compute Engine quota, not a separate GKE quota. A cluster-creation failure caused by exceeding available cores is therefore resolved by requesting additional Compute Engine quota in the Console (B). There is no distinct 'GKE quota' for node cores, which makes options A and C incorrect. Re-architecting services to use fewer cores (D) is unnecessary work when the straightforward fix is to raise the quota for the region where the cluster is being created.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Clusters GKE são construídos sobre máquinas virtuais do Compute Engine, então os núcleos de CPU consumidos pelos nós do cluster contam na sua cota do Compute Engine, e não em uma cota separada do GKE. Uma falha na criação do cluster causada por exceder os núcleos disponíveis é, portanto, resolvida solicitando cota adicional do Compute Engine no Console (B). Não existe uma 'cota do GKE' distinta para os núcleos dos nós, o que torna as opções A e C incorretas. Re-arquitetar os serviços para usar menos núcleos (D) é um trabalho desnecessário quando a correção direta é aumentar a cota para a região onde o cluster está sendo criado.

questions.question: You are parsing a log file that contains three columns: a timestamp, an account number (a string), and a transaction amount (a number). You want to calculate the sum of all transaction amounts for each unique account number efficiently.Which data structure should you use?

options.text: A linked list
A hash table
A two-dimensional array
A comma-delimited string

questions.correct_text: A hash table
questions.explanation: A hash table provides average O(1) lookup, insertion, and update by key, making it the ideal structure for aggregating values per unique account number: you key on the account string and accumulate the running sum for each. A linked list (A) requires O(n) traversal to find each account before updating, making aggregation O(n^2) overall. A two-dimensional array (C) offers no efficient way to look up an arbitrary string key, and a comma-delimited string (D) is a serialization format, not a structure suited for lookups or accumulation. Therefore the hash table is the most efficient choice.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Uma hash table fornece busca, inserção e atualização por chave em O(1) em média, tornando-a a estrutura ideal para agregar valores por número de conta único: você usa a string da conta como chave e acumula a soma corrente de cada uma. Uma linked list (A) exige travessia O(n) para encontrar cada conta antes de atualizar, tornando a agregação O(n^2) no total. Um array bidimensional (C) não oferece uma forma eficiente de buscar uma chave string arbitrária, e uma string delimitada por vírgulas (D) é um formato de serialização, não uma estrutura adequada para buscas ou acumulação. Portanto, a hash table é a escolha mais eficiente.

questions.question: Your company has a BigQuery dataset named "Master" that keeps information about employee travel and expenses. This information is organized by employee department. That means employees should only be able to view information for their department. You want to apply a security framework to enforce this requirement with the minimum number of steps.What should you do?

options.text: Create a separate dataset for each department. Create a view with an appropriate WHERE clause to select records from a particular dataset for the specific department. Authorize this view to access records from your Master dataset. Give employees the permission to this department-specific dataset.

Create a separate dataset for each department. Create a data pipeline for each department to copy appropriate information from the Master dataset to the specific dataset for the department. Give employees the permission to this department-specific dataset.
Create a dataset named Master dataset. Create a separate view for each department in the Master dataset. Give employees access to the specific view for their department.
Create a dataset named Master dataset. Create a separate table for each department in the Master dataset. Give employees access to the specific table for their department.

questions.correct_text: Create a dataset named Master dataset. Create a separate view for each department in the Master dataset. Give employees access to the specific view for their department.
questions.explanation: Authorized views in BigQuery let you expose a subset of data from a source dataset without granting users direct access to the underlying table. Keeping a single Master dataset and creating a per-department view with a filtering WHERE clause, then granting each group of employees access only to their view, enforces row-level isolation with minimal steps and no data duplication (C). Creating separate datasets and copying data via pipelines (B) or per-dataset views (A) duplicates data and adds maintenance overhead. Separate physical tables per department (D) likewise duplicates and fragments the data instead of leveraging views over the single source of truth.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: As authorized views no BigQuery permitem expor um subconjunto de dados de um dataset de origem sem conceder aos usuários acesso direto à tabela subjacente. Manter um único dataset Master e criar uma view por departamento com uma cláusula WHERE de filtragem, concedendo então a cada grupo de funcionários acesso apenas à sua view, impõe o isolamento em nível de linha com o mínimo de etapas e sem duplicação de dados (C). Criar datasets separados e copiar dados via pipelines (B) ou views por dataset (A) duplica os dados e adiciona sobrecarga de manutenção. Tabelas físicas separadas por departamento (D) igualmente duplicam e fragmentam os dados em vez de aproveitar as views sobre a única fonte de verdade.

questions.question: You have an application in production. It is deployed on Compute Engine virtual machine instances controlled by a managed instance group. Traffic is routed to the instances via a HTTP(s) load balancer. Your users are unable to access your application. You want to implement a monitoring technique to alert you when the application is unavailable.Which technique should you choose?

options.text: Smoke tests
Stackdriver uptime checks
Cloud Load Balancing - heath checks
Managed instance group - heath checks

questions.correct_text: Stackdriver uptime checks
questions.explanation: Stackdriver (Cloud Monitoring) uptime checks send requests to your application's public endpoint, such as the load balancer URL, from multiple global locations and can trigger an alert when the endpoint becomes unreachable, which is exactly what is needed to detect user-facing unavailability. Cloud Load Balancing and managed instance group health checks (C and D) determine whether individual backend instances are healthy so traffic can be routed away from failed VMs, but they do not alert you that the overall application is down from a user's perspective. Smoke tests (A) are run during deployment to validate a release, not for continuous production availability monitoring. Therefore uptime checks are the correct external monitoring technique.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: As uptime checks do Stackdriver (Cloud Monitoring) enviam requisições para o endpoint público da sua aplicação, como a URL do load balancer, a partir de múltiplas localidades globais e podem disparar um alerta quando o endpoint se torna inacessível, que é exatamente o que se precisa para detectar a indisponibilidade percebida pelo usuário. O Cloud Load Balancing e os health checks dos managed instance groups (C e D) determinam se instâncias de backend individuais estão saudáveis, para que o tráfego possa ser desviado das VMs com falha, mas eles não alertam você de que a aplicação como um todo está fora do ar sob a perspectiva do usuário. Smoke tests (A) são executados durante o deployment para validar um release, não para o monitoramento contínuo de disponibilidade em produção. Portanto, as uptime checks são a técnica correta de monitoramento externo.

questions.question: You are load testing your server application. During the first 30 seconds, you observe that a previously inactive Cloud Storage bucket is now servicing 2000 write requests per second and 7500 read requests per second. Your application is now receiving intermittent 5xx and 429 HTTP responses from the Cloud StorageJSON API as the demand escalates. You want to decrease the failed responses from the Cloud Storage API.What should you do?

options.text: Distribute the uploads across a large number of individual storage buckets.
Use the XML API instead of the JSON API for interfacing with Cloud Storage.
Pass the HTTP response codes back to clients that are invoking the uploads from your application.
Limit the upload rate from your application clients so that the dormant bucket's peak request rate is reached more gradually.

questions.correct_text: Limit the upload rate from your application clients so that the dormant bucket's peak request rate is reached more gradually.
questions.explanation: The 5xx and 429 responses indicate Cloud Storage is rate-limiting because a previously dormant bucket is being driven to a very high request rate too quickly. Cloud Storage auto-scales bucket throughput by gradually adapting to the request pattern, so the recommended fix is to ramp up the request rate gradually (roughly doubling it no faster than every 20 minutes) so the backend can scale, which is why D is correct. Option A (spreading across many buckets) adds operational complexity and is unnecessary since a single bucket can handle very high throughput once warmed up. Option B (switching to the XML API) does not change the underlying rate limits or auto-scaling behavior. Option C merely propagates the errors to clients instead of reducing the failures.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: As respostas 5xx e 429 indicam que o Cloud Storage está aplicando rate-limiting porque um bucket anteriormente inativo está sendo levado a uma taxa de requisições muito alta rápido demais. O Cloud Storage faz auto-scaling da vazão do bucket adaptando-se gradualmente ao padrão de requisições, então a correção recomendada é aumentar a taxa de requisições de forma gradual (aproximadamente dobrando-a não mais rápido do que a cada 20 minutos), para que o backend consiga escalar, e é por isso que D está correta. A opção A (distribuir entre muitos buckets) adiciona complexidade operacional e é desnecessária, já que um único bucket consegue lidar com vazão muito alta depois de aquecido. A opção B (mudar para a XML API) não altera os limites de taxa subjacentes nem o comportamento de auto-scaling. A opção C apenas propaga os erros para os clientes em vez de reduzir as falhas.

questions.question: Your application is controlled by a managed instance group. You want to share a large read-only data set between all the instances in the managed instance group. You want to ensure that each instance can start quickly and can access the data set via its filesystem with very low latency. You also want to minimize the total cost of the solution.What should you do?

options.text: Move the data to a Cloud Storage bucket, and mount the bucket on the filesystem using Cloud Storage FUSE.
Move the data to a Cloud Storage bucket, and copy the data to the boot disk of the instance via a startup script.
Move the data to a Compute Engine persistent disk, and attach the disk in read-only mode to multiple Compute Engine virtual machine instances.
Move the data to a Compute Engine persistent disk, take a snapshot, create multiple disks from the snapshot, and attach each disk to its own instance.

questions.correct_text: Move the data to a Compute Engine persistent disk, and attach the disk in read-only mode to multiple Compute Engine virtual machine instances.
questions.explanation: A Compute Engine persistent disk can be attached to many VM instances simultaneously in read-only mode, giving every instance fast, low-latency filesystem access to the shared data without duplicating storage, which minimizes cost and lets instances start quickly. This makes C correct. Option D creates a separate disk per instance from a snapshot, duplicating storage and increasing cost and startup time. Option B copies the entire dataset to each boot disk via a startup script, slowing startup and wasting storage. Option A using Cloud Storage FUSE provides filesystem-like access but with much higher latency than a local persistent disk, failing the very-low-latency requirement.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Um persistent disk do Compute Engine pode ser anexado a muitas instâncias de VM simultaneamente em modo somente leitura, dando a cada instância acesso rápido e de baixa latência ao sistema de arquivos com os dados compartilhados, sem duplicar o armazenamento, o que minimiza o custo e permite que as instâncias iniciem rapidamente. Isso torna C correta. A opção D cria um disco separado por instância a partir de um snapshot, duplicando o armazenamento e aumentando o custo e o tempo de inicialização. A opção B copia todo o dataset para cada boot disk por meio de um startup script, deixando a inicialização mais lenta e desperdiçando armazenamento. A opção A, usando Cloud Storage FUSE, fornece acesso semelhante a um sistema de arquivos, mas com latência muito maior do que um persistent disk local, não atendendo ao requisito de latência muito baixa.

questions.question: You are developing an HTTP API hosted on a Compute Engine virtual machine instance that needs to be invoked by multiple clients within the same VirtualPrivate Cloud (VPC). You want clients to be able to get the IP address of the service.What should you do?

options.text: Reserve a static external IP address and assign it to an HTTP(S) load balancing service's forwarding rule. Clients should use this IP address to connect to the service.

Reserve a static external IP address and assign it to an HTTP(S) load balancing service's forwarding rule. Then, define an A record in Cloud DNS. Clients should use the name of the A record to connect to the service.
Ensure that clients use Compute Engine internal DNS by connecting to the instance name with the url https://[INSTANCE_NAME].[ZONE].c. [PROJECT_ID].internal/.
Ensure that clients use Compute Engine internal DNS by connecting to the instance name with the url https://[API_NAME]/[API_VERSION]/.

questions.correct_text: Ensure that clients use Compute Engine internal DNS by connecting to the instance name with the url https://[INSTANCE_NAME].[ZONE].c. [PROJECT_ID].internal/.
questions.explanation: Because all clients are inside the same VPC, internal communication should use Compute Engine internal DNS, which automatically provides resolvable names in the form [INSTANCE_NAME].[ZONE].c.[PROJECT_ID].internal, so C is correct. This keeps traffic private and avoids exposing the service externally. Options A and B reserve external IP addresses and use an HTTP(S) load balancer, which routes internal traffic out to the public internet unnecessarily and adds cost and exposure for an internal-only API. Option D uses an invalid URL format that does not correspond to any real Compute Engine internal DNS name.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Como todos os clientes estão dentro da mesma VPC, a comunicação interna deve usar o DNS interno do Compute Engine, que fornece automaticamente nomes resolvíveis no formato [INSTANCE_NAME].[ZONE].c.[PROJECT_ID].internal, então C está correta. Isso mantém o tráfego privado e evita expor o serviço externamente. As opções A e B reservam endereços IP externos e usam um HTTP(S) load balancer, o que roteia o tráfego interno desnecessariamente para a internet pública e adiciona custo e exposição para uma API exclusivamente interna. A opção D usa um formato de URL inválido que não corresponde a nenhum nome real de DNS interno do Compute Engine.

questions.question: Your application is logging to Stackdriver. You want to get the count of all requests on all /api/alpha/* endpoints.What should you do?

options.text: Add a Stackdriver counter metric for path:/api/alpha/.
Add a Stackdriver counter metric for endpoint:/api/alpha/*.
Export the logs to Cloud Storage and count lines matching /api/alpha.
Export the logs to Cloud Pub/Sub and count lines matching /api/alpha.

questions.correct_text: Add a Stackdriver counter metric for path:/api/alpha/.
questions.explanation: To count requests matching a path pattern, you create a logs-based counter metric in Cloud Logging (Stackdriver) filtered on the relevant log entries, so A is the correct approach using a counter metric for the /api/alpha/ path. Logs-based metrics let you extract and count matching entries directly within the platform and chart or alert on them. Option B uses an invalid field/syntax (endpoint:...) that does not correspond to how logs-based metrics are defined. Options C and D export logs to Cloud Storage or Pub/Sub and then count lines externally, which is far more complex and unnecessary when a logs-based counter metric does this natively.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Para contar requisições que correspondem a um padrão de path, você cria uma logs-based counter metric no Cloud Logging (Stackdriver) filtrada nas entradas de log relevantes, então A é a abordagem correta usando uma counter metric para o path /api/alpha/. As logs-based metrics permitem extrair e contar entradas correspondentes diretamente dentro da plataforma e plotá-las em gráficos ou criar alertas. A opção B usa um campo/sintaxe inválido (endpoint:...) que não corresponde a como as logs-based metrics são definidas. As opções C e D exportam logs para o Cloud Storage ou Pub/Sub e então contam as linhas externamente, o que é muito mais complexo e desnecessário quando uma logs-based counter metric faz isso de forma nativa.

questions.question: You want to re-architect a monolithic application so that it follows a microservices model. You want to accomplish this efficiently while minimizing the impact of this change to the business.Which approach should you take?

options.text: Deploy the application to Compute Engine and turn on autoscaling.
Replace the application's features with appropriate microservices in phases.
Refactor the monolithic application with appropriate microservices in a single effort and deploy it.
Build a new application with the appropriate microservices separate from the monolith and replace it when it is complete.

questions.correct_text: Replace the application's features with appropriate microservices in phases.
questions.explanation: The recommended way to migrate a monolith to microservices with minimal business impact is the strangler pattern: incrementally replace the monolith's features with microservices in phases while the system keeps running, which is why B is correct. This lets you validate, roll back, and limit risk at each step. Option C, a single big-bang refactor and deploy, is high-risk and disruptive. Option D, building a fully separate new application and cutting over only when complete, delays value delivery and carries large all-at-once switchover risk. Option A simply scales the monolith with autoscaling and does not convert it to microservices at all.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: A forma recomendada de migrar um monolito para microsserviços com impacto mínimo ao negócio é o strangler pattern: substituir incrementalmente os recursos do monolito por microsserviços em fases enquanto o sistema continua em funcionamento, e por isso B está correta. Isso permite validar, reverter e limitar o risco em cada etapa. A opção C, uma única refatoração e implantação big-bang, é de alto risco e disruptiva. A opção D, construir um aplicativo novo totalmente separado e fazer a transição apenas quando estiver completo, atrasa a entrega de valor e carrega um grande risco de troca de uma só vez. A opção A simplesmente escala o monolito com autoscaling e não o converte em microsserviços de forma alguma.

questions.question: Your existing application keeps user state information in a single MySQL database. This state information is very user-specific and depends heavily on how long a user has been using an application. The MySQL database is causing challenges to maintain and enhance the schema for various users.Which storage option should you choose?

options.text: Cloud SQL
Cloud Storage
Cloud Spanner
Cloud Datastore/Firestore

questions.correct_text: Cloud Datastore/Firestore
questions.explanation: The data is user-specific state that varies in structure per user, and the rigid relational schema of MySQL is hard to maintain and evolve. Cloud Datastore/Firestore is a NoSQL document database with a flexible, schemaless model that lets different entities have different fields without costly schema migrations, making it ideal for evolving, per-user state. Cloud SQL (A) is itself a managed MySQL/PostgreSQL service and would carry the same schema-rigidity problem. Cloud Storage (B) is object storage, not suited for structured queryable state. Cloud Spanner (C) is a horizontally scalable relational database that still enforces a schema and is overkill and costly for this single-database, user-state use case.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Os dados são estado específico de cada usuário, que varia em estrutura por usuário, e o esquema relacional rígido do MySQL é difícil de manter e evoluir. O Cloud Datastore/Firestore é um banco de dados de documentos NoSQL com um modelo flexível e sem esquema (schemaless) que permite que diferentes entidades tenham diferentes campos sem migrações de esquema custosas, tornando-o ideal para estado por usuário em evolução. O Cloud SQL (A) é, ele próprio, um serviço gerenciado de MySQL/PostgreSQL e teria o mesmo problema de rigidez de esquema. O Cloud Storage (B) é armazenamento de objetos, não adequado para estado estruturado e consultável. O Cloud Spanner (C) é um banco de dados relacional escalável horizontalmente que ainda impõe um esquema e é exagerado e custoso para este caso de uso de banco de dados único e estado de usuário.

questions.question: You are building a new API. You want to minimize the cost of storing and reduce the latency of serving images.Which architecture should you use?

options.text: App Engine backed by Cloud Storage
Compute Engine backed by Persistent Disk
Transfer Appliance backed by Cloud Filestore
Cloud Content Delivery Network (CDN) backed by Cloud Storage

questions.correct_text: Cloud Content Delivery Network (CDN) backed by Cloud Storage
questions.explanation: To minimize storage cost and reduce serving latency for images, store the images cheaply in Cloud Storage and serve them through Cloud CDN, which caches content at Google's globally distributed edge points of presence close to users. Cloud Storage offers low-cost, durable object storage, and enabling Cloud CDN in front of it dramatically lowers latency for repeated requests. App Engine backed by Cloud Storage (A) serves dynamic content but does not provide edge caching for low latency. Compute Engine with Persistent Disk (B) is more expensive and lacks global caching. Transfer Appliance (C) is a hardware device for bulk data migration, not an image-serving architecture.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para minimizar o custo de armazenamento e reduzir a latência de entrega de imagens, armazene as imagens de forma barata no Cloud Storage e sirva-as através do Cloud CDN, que faz cache do conteúdo nos pontos de presença de borda distribuídos globalmente da Google, próximos aos usuários. O Cloud Storage oferece armazenamento de objetos durável e de baixo custo, e habilitar o Cloud CDN na frente dele reduz drasticamente a latência para requisições repetidas. O App Engine com backend no Cloud Storage (A) serve conteúdo dinâmico, mas não fornece cache de borda para baixa latência. O Compute Engine com Persistent Disk (B) é mais caro e não tem cache global. O Transfer Appliance (C) é um dispositivo de hardware para migração de dados em massa, não uma arquitetura de entrega de imagens.

questions.question: Your company's development teams want to use Cloud Build in their projects to build and push Docker images to Container Registry. The operations team requires all Docker images to be published to a centralized, securely managed Docker registry that the operations team manages.What should you do?

options.text: Use Container Registry to create a registry in each development team's project. Configure the Cloud Build build to push the Docker image to the project's registry. Grant the operations team access to each development team's registry.

Create a separate project for the operations team that has Container Registry configured. Assign appropriate permissions to the Cloud Build service account in each developer team's project to allow access to the operation team's registry.

Create a separate project for the operations team that has Container Registry configured. Create a Service Account for each development team and assign the appropriate permissions to allow it access to the operations team's registry. Store the service account key file in the source code repository and use it to authenticate against the operations team's registry.

Create a separate project for the operations team that has the open source Docker Registry deployed on a Compute Engine virtual machine instance. Create a username and password for each development team. Store the username and password in the source code repository and use it to authenticate against the operations team's Docker registry.

questions.correct_text: Create a separate project for the operations team that has Container Registry configured. Assign appropriate permissions to the Cloud Build service account in each developer team's project to allow access to the operation team's registry.
questions.explanation: The cleanest, most secure approach is to centralize the registry in a dedicated operations-team project and grant each development team's Cloud Build service account the appropriate IAM permissions (such as Artifact/Container Registry writer) on that registry. This uses Google-managed service account identities and IAM, avoiding any long-lived credentials. Option A scatters registries across projects, the opposite of centralization. Option C stores a service account key file in source control, a serious security anti-pattern that risks credential leakage. Option D runs an unmanaged open-source Docker registry on a VM with static username/password stored in source code, which is insecure and operationally burdensome compared to a managed registry with IAM.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: A abordagem mais limpa e segura é centralizar o registry em um projeto dedicado da equipe de operações e conceder à service account do Cloud Build de cada equipe de desenvolvimento as permissões de IAM apropriadas (como writer do Artifact/Container Registry) nesse registry. Isso usa identidades de service account gerenciadas pela Google e o IAM, evitando quaisquer credenciais de longa duração. A opção A espalha registries por vários projetos, o oposto da centralização. A opção C armazena um arquivo de chave de service account no controle de código-fonte, um sério anti-padrão de segurança que arrisca vazamento de credenciais. A opção D executa um registry Docker open-source não gerenciado em uma VM com usuário/senha estáticos armazenados no código-fonte, o que é inseguro e operacionalmente oneroso em comparação com um registry gerenciado com IAM.

questions.question: You are planning to deploy your application in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. Your application can scale horizontally, and each instance of your application needs to have a stable network identity and its own persistent disk.Which GKE object should you use?

options.text: Deployment
StatefulSet
ReplicaSet
ReplicaController

questions.correct_text: StatefulSet
questions.explanation: A StatefulSet is the correct GKE/Kubernetes object when each replica needs a stable, unique network identity and its own dedicated persistent storage. StatefulSets assign stable ordinal pod names and per-pod PersistentVolumeClaims, preserving identity and data across rescheduling. A Deployment (A) and ReplicaSet (C) create interchangeable, stateless pods with random names and no per-pod stable storage. ReplicationController (D) is the legacy predecessor of ReplicaSet and likewise provides no stable identity or per-instance persistent disk.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Um StatefulSet é o objeto correto do GKE/Kubernetes quando cada réplica precisa de uma identidade de rede estável e única e de seu próprio armazenamento persistente dedicado. StatefulSets atribuem nomes de pod ordinais estáveis e PersistentVolumeClaims por pod, preservando a identidade e os dados ao longo de reagendamentos. Um Deployment (A) e um ReplicaSet (C) criam pods intercambiáveis e stateless com nomes aleatórios e sem armazenamento estável por pod. O ReplicationController (D) é o predecessor legado do ReplicaSet e, da mesma forma, não fornece identidade estável nem disco persistente por instância.

questions.question: You are using Cloud Build to build a Docker image. You need to modify the build to execute unit and run integration tests. When there is a failure, you want the build history to clearly display the stage at which the build failed.What should you do?

options.text: Add RUN commands in the Dockerfile to execute unit and integration tests.
Create a Cloud Build build config file with a single build step to compile unit and integration tests.
Create a Cloud Build build config file that will spawn a separate cloud build pipeline for unit and integration tests.
Create a Cloud Build build config file with separate cloud builder steps to compile and execute unit and integration tests.

questions.correct_text: Create a Cloud Build build config file with separate cloud builder steps to compile and execute unit and integration tests.
questions.explanation: Defining a Cloud Build config file (cloudbuild.yaml) with separate build steps for compiling, running unit tests, and running integration tests gives each phase its own discrete step, so a failure is clearly attributed to the specific stage in the build history. Each step appears individually with its own status and logs. Adding RUN commands in the Dockerfile (A) buries testing inside the image build and obscures which phase failed. A single build step (B) lumps everything together, so the build history cannot distinguish the failing stage. Spawning a separate pipeline (C) fragments the build and complicates tracking the failure within one cohesive history.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Definir um arquivo de configuração do Cloud Build (cloudbuild.yaml) com etapas de build separadas para compilar, executar testes unitários e executar testes de integração dá a cada fase sua própria etapa discreta, de modo que uma falha é claramente atribuída ao estágio específico no histórico do build. Cada etapa aparece individualmente, com seu próprio status e logs. Adicionar comandos RUN no Dockerfile (A) enterra os testes dentro do build da imagem e obscurece qual fase falhou. Uma única etapa de build (B) agrupa tudo, de modo que o histórico do build não consegue distinguir o estágio que falhou. Criar um pipeline separado (C) fragmenta o build e complica o rastreamento da falha dentro de um único histórico coeso.

questions.question: Your code is running on Cloud Functions in project A. It is supposed to write an object in a Cloud Storage bucket owned by project B. However, the write call is failing with the error "403 Forbidden".What should you do to correct the problem?

options.text: Grant your user account the roles/storage.objectCreator role for the Cloud Storage bucket.
Grant your user account the roles/iam.serviceAccountUser role for the [email protected] service account.
Grant the [email protected] service account the roles/storage.objectCreator role for the Cloud Storage bucket.
Enable the Cloud Storage API in project B.

questions.correct_text: Grant the [email protected] service account the roles/storage.objectCreator role for the Cloud Storage bucket.
questions.explanation: Cloud Functions execute under the identity of a service account, not your user account, so the IAM permissions that matter are those granted to the function's runtime service account. Because the function runs in project A but writes to a bucket in project B, the function's service account must be granted roles/storage.objectCreator on the project B bucket, which is exactly what option C does. Option A grants the role to your user account, which is irrelevant since the function does not run as you. Option B (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser) governs impersonation of a service account, not access to Storage objects. Option D is wrong because the Cloud Storage API is enabled in project A (where the calling code runs), and the 403 indicates an authorization failure rather than a disabled API.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: As Cloud Functions executam sob a identidade de uma service account, e não da sua conta de usuário, portanto as permissões de IAM que importam são aquelas concedidas à service account de runtime da função. Como a função executa no project A mas grava em um bucket no project B, a service account da função precisa receber o papel roles/storage.objectCreator no bucket do project B, que é exatamente o que a opção C faz. A opção A concede o papel à sua conta de usuário, o que é irrelevante, já que a função não executa como você. A opção B (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser) governa a impersonação de uma service account, e não o acesso a objetos do Storage. A opção D está incorreta porque a Cloud Storage API está habilitada no project A (onde o código chamador é executado), e o erro 403 indica uma falha de autorização, e não uma API desabilitada.

When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.Company Overview -HipLocal is a community application designed to facilitate communication between people in close proximity. It is used for event planning and organizing sporting events, and for businesses to connect with their local communities. HipLocal launched recently in a few neighborhoods in Dallas and is rapidly growing into a global phenomenon. Its unique style of hyper-local community communication and business outreach is in demand around the world.Executive Statement -We are the number one local community app; it's time to take our local community services global. Our venture capital investors want to see rapid growth and the same great experience for new local and virtual communities that come online, whether their members are 10 or 10000 miles away from each other.Solution Concept -HipLocal wants to expand their existing service, with updated functionality, in new regions to better serve their global customers. They want to hire and train a new team to support these regions in their time zones. They will need to ensure that the application scales smoothly and provides clear uptime data.Existing Technical Environment -HipLocal's environment is a mix of on-premises hardware and infrastructure running in Google Cloud Platform. The HipLocal team understands their application well, but has limited experience in global scale applications. Their existing technical environment is as follows:* Existing APIs run on Compute Engine virtual machine instances hosted in GCP.* State is stored in a single instance MySQL database in GCP.* Data is exported to an on-premises Teradata/Vertica data warehouse.* Data analytics is performed in an on-premises Hadoop environment.* The application has no logging.* There are basic indicators of uptime; alerts are frequently fired when the APIs are unresponsive.Business Requirements -HipLocal's investors want to expand their footprint and support the increase in demand they are seeing. Their requirements are:* Expand availability of the application to new regions.* Increase the number of concurrent users that can be supported.* Ensure a consistent experience for users when they travel to different regions.* Obtain user activity metrics to better understand how to monetize their product.* Ensure compliance with regulations in the new regions (for example, GDPR).* Reduce infrastructure management time and cost.* Adopt the Google-recommended practices for cloud computing.Technical Requirements -* The application and backend must provide usage metrics and monitoring.* APIs require strong authentication and authorization.* Logging must be increased, and data should be stored in a cloud analytics platform.* Move to serverless architecture to facilitate elastic scaling.* Provide authorized access to internal apps in a secure manner.HipLocal's .net-based auth service fails under intermittent load.What should they do?

options.text: Use App Engine for autoscaling.
Use Cloud Functions for autoscaling.
Use a Compute Engine cluster for the service.
Use a dedicated Compute Engine virtual machine instance for the service.

questions.correct_text: Use App Engine for autoscaling.
questions.explanation: The auth service fails under intermittent load because it cannot scale horizontally to absorb traffic spikes, and HipLocal's technical requirements call for a serverless architecture with elastic scaling. App Engine provides automatic, rapid autoscaling of stateless HTTP services (including .NET via the flexible environment) without managing instances, making option A the best fit. Cloud Functions (option B) are intended for event-driven, single-purpose functions rather than hosting a full auth service, and adapting an existing .NET service to it is awkward. A Compute Engine cluster (option C) can scale via managed instance groups but requires significant infrastructure management, conflicting with the requirement to reduce management overhead. A single dedicated VM (option D) does not autoscale at all and would still fail under load.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O serviço de autenticação falha sob carga intermitente porque não consegue escalar horizontalmente para absorver picos de tráfego, e os requisitos técnicos da HipLocal exigem uma arquitetura serverless com escalonamento elástico. O App Engine fornece autoescalonamento automático e rápido de serviços HTTP stateless (incluindo .NET via flexible environment) sem gerenciar instâncias, tornando a opção A a mais adequada. As Cloud Functions (opção B) destinam-se a funções orientadas a eventos e de propósito único, e não a hospedar um serviço de autenticação completo, e adaptar um serviço .NET existente a elas é desajeitado. Um cluster do Compute Engine (opção C) pode escalar via managed instance groups, mas exige gerenciamento significativo de infraestrutura, conflitando com o requisito de reduzir a sobrecarga de gerenciamento. Uma única VM dedicada (opção D) não faz autoescalonamento algum e ainda falharia sob carga.

They want to collect application information specifically to troubleshoot the issue. What should they do?

options.text: Take frequent snapshots of the virtual machines.
Install the Cloud Logging agent on the virtual machines.
Install the Cloud Monitoring agent on the virtual machines.
Use Cloud Trace to look for performance bottlenecks.

questions.correct_text: Install the Cloud Logging agent on the virtual machines.
questions.explanation: The goal is to collect application-level information to troubleshoot occasional failures, and the existing application has no logging. Installing the Cloud Logging (Ops) agent on the VMs (option B) ingests application and system logs into Cloud Logging, giving the detailed records needed to diagnose intermittent errors. Snapshots (option A) capture disk state for backup/recovery and reveal nothing about runtime failures. The Cloud Monitoring agent (option C) gathers metrics such as CPU and memory, which indicate health trends but do not contain the diagnostic log detail required to troubleshoot specific failures. Cloud Trace (option D) measures request latency and bottlenecks but is for performance analysis, not capturing failure logs.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O objetivo é coletar informações em nível de aplicação para solucionar falhas ocasionais, e a aplicação existente não tem logging. Instalar o agente do Cloud Logging (Ops) nas VMs (opção B) ingere logs de aplicação e de sistema no Cloud Logging, fornecendo os registros detalhados necessários para diagnosticar erros intermitentes. Snapshots (opção A) capturam o estado do disco para backup/recuperação e não revelam nada sobre falhas em tempo de execução. O agente do Cloud Monitoring (opção C) coleta métricas como CPU e memória, que indicam tendências de saúde mas não contêm o detalhe de log diagnóstico necessário para solucionar falhas específicas. O Cloud Trace (opção D) mede a latência de requisições e gargalos, mas é para análise de desempenho, não para capturar logs de falha.

options.text: Create manual subnets.
Create an auto mode subnet.
Create multiple peered VPCs.
Provision a single instance for NAT.

questions.correct_text: Create manual subnets.
questions.explanation: When connecting on-premises infrastructure to Google Cloud over Cloud Interconnect, the on-premises and VPC IP ranges must not overlap, and you need predictable, controllable CIDR blocks for routing. Creating manual (custom mode) subnets (option A) lets HipLocal define exact, non-overlapping IP ranges per region, which is the Google-recommended approach for hybrid connectivity. Auto mode subnets (option B) assign predefined ranges automatically and risk overlapping with the on-premises network, making them unsuitable for Interconnect. Multiple peered VPCs (option C) address inter-VPC connectivity, not on-premises IP planning. Provisioning a NAT instance (option D) is for outbound internet egress from private VMs and is irrelevant to private Interconnect-based access.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Ao conectar a infraestrutura on-premises ao Google Cloud por meio do Cloud Interconnect, os intervalos de IP on-premises e da VPC não podem se sobrepor, e você precisa de blocos CIDR previsíveis e controláveis para o roteamento. Criar subnets manuais (modo custom) (opção A) permite que a HipLocal defina intervalos de IP exatos e não sobrepostos por região, que é a abordagem recomendada pelo Google para conectividade híbrida. Subnets em modo auto (opção B) atribuem intervalos predefinidos automaticamente e correm o risco de se sobrepor à rede on-premises, tornando-as inadequadas para o Interconnect. Múltiplas VPCs em peering (opção C) tratam da conectividade entre VPCs, e não do planejamento de IP on-premises. Provisionar uma instância NAT (opção D) serve para a saída de tráfego de saída à internet a partir de VMs privadas e é irrelevante para o acesso privado baseado em Interconnect.

options.text: Cloud VPN
Cloud Armor
Virtual Private Cloud
Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy

questions.correct_text: Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy
questions.explanation: HipLocal needs to provide authorized, identity-based access to internal applications in a secure manner. Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (option D) enforces per-request authentication and authorization at the application layer, allowing only verified users with the right IAM permissions to reach internal apps without a VPN, which directly satisfies the requirement. Cloud VPN (option A) creates an encrypted network tunnel but grants broad network-level access rather than fine-grained per-app identity authorization. Cloud Armor (option B) provides WAF and DDoS protection for public-facing services, not identity-based internal access control. Virtual Private Cloud (option C) is the underlying network and does not by itself authenticate or authorize users to applications.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: A HipLocal precisa fornecer acesso autorizado e baseado em identidade a aplicações internas de forma segura. O Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (opção D) impõe autenticação e autorização por requisição na camada de aplicação, permitindo que apenas usuários verificados com as permissões IAM corretas alcancem as aplicações internas sem uma VPN, o que satisfaz diretamente o requisito. O Cloud VPN (opção A) cria um túnel de rede criptografado, mas concede acesso amplo no nível de rede em vez de autorização de identidade granular por aplicação. O Cloud Armor (opção B) fornece proteção WAF e contra DDoS para serviços expostos publicamente, e não controle de acesso interno baseado em identidade. A Virtual Private Cloud (opção C) é a rede subjacente e, por si só, não autentica nem autoriza usuários às aplicações.

Cloud Functions
Cloud Endpoints
Shielded Virtual Machines

questions.correct_text: Cloud Endpoints
questions.explanation: The technical requirements state that APIs require strong authentication and authorization plus usage metrics and monitoring, which is exactly what an API management layer provides. topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Os requisitos técnicos afirmam que as APIs exigem autenticação e autorização fortes, além de métricas de uso e monitoramento, que é exatamente o que uma camada de gerenciamento de API fornece. O Cloud Armor (A) é um serviço de proteção WAF e contra DDoS, não um produto de gerenciamento de API. options.text: Use the current single instance MySQL on Compute Engine and several read-only MySQL servers on Compute Engine.
Use the current single instance MySQL on Compute Engine, and replicate the data to Cloud SQL in an external master configuration.
Replace the current single instance MySQL instance with Cloud SQL, and configure high availability.
Replace the current single instance MySQL instance with Cloud SQL, and Google provides redundancy without further configuration.

questions.correct_text: Replace the current single instance MySQL instance with Cloud SQL, and configure high availability.
questions.explanation: To improve resilience while reducing infrastructure management, HipLocal should migrate from self-managed MySQL on Compute Engine to the managed Cloud SQL service and explicitly enable its high availability configuration. Answer C is correct because Cloud SQL HA uses a regional, synchronously replicated standby in a different zone with automatic failover, which addresses resilience and the goal of reducing operational overhead. Options A and B keep the self-managed single-instance MySQL on Compute Engine, retaining the management burden and single point of failure that the requirements aim to eliminate. Option D is wrong because Cloud SQL does not provide HA automatically; high availability is an opt-in configuration the user must enable.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para melhorar a resiliência e ao mesmo tempo reduzir o gerenciamento de infraestrutura, a HipLocal deve migrar do MySQL autogerenciado no Compute Engine para o serviço gerenciado Cloud SQL e habilitar explicitamente sua configuração de alta disponibilidade. A resposta C está correta porque o Cloud SQL HA usa um standby regional, replicado de forma síncrona em uma zona diferente, com failover automático, o que atende à resiliência e à meta de reduzir a sobrecarga operacional. As opções A e B mantêm o MySQL autogerenciado de instância única no Compute Engine, retendo a carga de gerenciamento e o ponto único de falha que os requisitos visam eliminar. A opção D está incorreta porque o Cloud SQL não fornece HA automaticamente; a alta disponibilidade é uma configuração opcional que o usuário precisa habilitar.

questions.question: Your application is running in multiple Google Kubernetes Engine clusters. It is managed by a Deployment in each cluster. The Deployment has created multiple replicas of your Pod in each cluster. You want to view the logs sent to stdout for all of the replicas in your Deployment in all clusters.Which command should you use?

options.text: kubectl logs [PARAM]
gcloud logging read [PARAM]
kubectl exec ג€"it [PARAM] journalctl
gcloud compute ssh [PARAM] ג€"-command= ג€sudo journalctlג€

questions.correct_text: gcloud logging read [PARAM]
questions.explanation: GKE automatically sends container stdout/stderr to Cloud Logging when Cloud Operations logging is enabled, so logs from all replicas across multiple clusters are centralized there. Using 'gcloud logging read' with an appropriate filter (B) lets you query and aggregate those logs across every cluster from one place. 'kubectl logs' (A) only targets a single cluster's context (the one in your current kubeconfig) and typically one Pod or Deployment, so it cannot span multiple clusters. 'kubectl exec ... journalctl' (C) and 'gcloud compute ssh ... journalctl' (D) inspect node-level systemd journals on individual machines, which is not how application stdout is collected and does not give a unified cross-cluster view.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O GKE envia automaticamente o stdout/stderr dos containers para o Cloud Logging quando o logging do Cloud Operations está habilitado, então os logs de todas as réplicas em múltiplos clusters ficam centralizados ali. Usar 'gcloud logging read' com um filtro apropriado (B) permite consultar e agregar esses logs de todos os clusters a partir de um único lugar. O 'kubectl logs' (A) só atinge o contexto de um único cluster (aquele no seu kubeconfig atual) e tipicamente um único Pod ou Deployment, portanto não consegue abranger múltiplos clusters. O 'kubectl exec ... journalctl' (C) e o 'gcloud compute ssh ... journalctl' (D) inspecionam os journals systemd a nível de nó em máquinas individuais, o que não é a forma como o stdout da aplicação é coletado e não oferece uma visão unificada entre clusters.

questions.question: You are using Cloud Build to create a new Docker image on each source code commit to a Cloud Source Repositories repository. Your application is built on every commit to the master branch. You want to release specific commits made to the master branch in an automated method.What should you do?

options.text: Manually trigger the build for new releases.
Create a build trigger on a Git tag pattern. Use a Git tag convention for new releases.
Create a build trigger on a Git branch name pattern. Use a Git branch naming convention for new releases.
Commit your source code to a second Cloud Source Repositories repository with a second Cloud Build trigger. Use this repository for new releases only.

questions.correct_text: Create a build trigger on a Git tag pattern. Use a Git tag convention for new releases.
questions.explanation: Creating a Cloud Build trigger that fires on a Git tag pattern lets you release specific commits automatically by tagging them with a release convention (for example, v1.2.0), making releases deterministic and decoupled from every master commit. Tags point to exact commits, which is the standard way to mark releases. Option A relies on manual triggering, which is not automated. Option C uses branch name patterns, but you want to release particular commits on master, not separate branches, so this does not target individual commits. Option D adds an unnecessary second repository and duplicates source, which complicates the workflow without solving the requirement.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Criar um trigger do Cloud Build que dispara em um padrão de tag do Git permite lançar commits específicos automaticamente ao marcá-los com uma convenção de release (por exemplo, v1.2.0), tornando os lançamentos determinísticos e desacoplados de cada commit na master. As tags apontam para commits exatos, que é a forma padrão de marcar releases. A opção A depende de acionamento manual, que não é automatizado. A opção C usa padrões de nome de branch, mas você quer lançar commits específicos na master, não branches separadas, então isso não direciona commits individuais. A opção D adiciona um segundo repositório desnecessário e duplica o código-fonte, o que complica o fluxo de trabalho sem resolver o requisito.

questions.question: You are designing a schema for a table that will be moved from MySQL to Cloud Bigtable. The MySQL table is as follows:How should you design a row key for Cloud Bigtable for this table?

options.text: Set Account_id as a key.
Set Account_id_Event_timestamp as a key.
Set Event_timestamp_Account_id as a key.
Set Event_timestamp as a key.

questions.correct_text: Set Account_id_Event_timestamp as a key.
questions.explanation: In Cloud Bigtable, the row key determines data locality and query patterns, and a well-designed key both avoids hotspotting and supports the access pattern. Using Account_id as the leading portion distributes rows across accounts, while appending Event_timestamp lets you store and efficiently scan time-ordered events for a given account. Option A (Account_id alone) cannot uniquely identify multiple events per account. Option D (timestamp alone) and Option C (timestamp first) place the monotonically increasing timestamp at the start of the key, causing all writes to hit the same tablet and creating a severe hotspot. Therefore Account_id_Event_timestamp is the correct composite key.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: No Cloud Bigtable, a row key determina a localidade dos dados e os padrões de consulta, e uma chave bem projetada evita hotspotting e dá suporte ao padrão de acesso. Usar o Account_id como a parte inicial distribui as linhas entre as contas, enquanto anexar o Event_timestamp permite armazenar e escanear eficientemente eventos ordenados por tempo para uma determinada conta. A opção A (Account_id sozinho) não consegue identificar de forma única múltiplos eventos por conta. A opção D (timestamp sozinho) e a opção C (timestamp primeiro) colocam o timestamp monotonicamente crescente no início da chave, fazendo com que todas as escritas atinjam o mesmo tablet e criando um hotspot severo. Portanto, Account_id_Event_timestamp é a chave composta correta.

questions.question: You want to view the memory usage of your application deployed on Compute Engine.What should you do?

options.text: Install the Stackdriver Client Library.
Install the Stackdriver Monitoring Agent.
Use the Stackdriver Metrics Explorer.
Use the Google Cloud Platform Console.

questions.correct_text: Install the Stackdriver Monitoring Agent.
questions.explanation: By default, Compute Engine exposes CPU, disk, and network metrics, but memory utilization is a guest-OS metric that is not collected without an agent. Installing the Cloud Monitoring (Stackdriver Monitoring) Agent on the VM gathers in-guest metrics such as memory usage and reports them to Cloud Monitoring where you can view them. Option A, the client library, is for instrumenting custom application metrics, not standard system memory. Options C and D let you view metrics that already exist, but without the agent installed there is no memory metric to plot or display, so they do not solve the underlying collection gap.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Por padrão, o Compute Engine expõe métricas de CPU, disco e rede, mas a utilização de memória é uma métrica do guest OS que não é coletada sem um agente. Instalar o Cloud Monitoring (Stackdriver Monitoring) Agent na VM coleta métricas de dentro do guest, como o uso de memória, e as reporta ao Cloud Monitoring, onde você pode visualizá-las. A opção A, a client library, serve para instrumentar métricas customizadas da aplicação, não a memória padrão do sistema. As opções C e D permitem visualizar métricas que já existem, mas sem o agente instalado não há métrica de memória para plotar ou exibir, então elas não resolvem a lacuna de coleta subjacente.

questions.question: You have an analytics application that runs hundreds of queries on BigQuery every few minutes using BigQuery API. You want to find out how much time these queries take to execute.What should you do?

options.text: Use Stackdriver Monitoring to plot slot usage.
Use Stackdriver Trace to plot API execution time.
Use Stackdriver Trace to plot query execution time.
Use Stackdriver Monitoring to plot query execution times.

questions.correct_text: Use Stackdriver Monitoring to plot query execution times.
questions.explanation: BigQuery emits built-in metrics to Cloud Monitoring (Stackdriver Monitoring), including query execution time, which you can chart to understand how long your frequent queries take. Using Cloud Monitoring to plot query execution times directly answers the question. Option A plots slot usage, which measures resource consumption rather than elapsed query time. Options B and C use Cloud Trace, which is designed for distributed request latency tracing across application services and is not the tool that surfaces BigQuery query execution time; Trace would not capture this without custom instrumentation, and plotting metrics is the native fit.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O BigQuery emite métricas integradas para o Cloud Monitoring (Stackdriver Monitoring), incluindo o tempo de execução de consultas, que você pode plotar em gráficos para entender quanto tempo suas consultas frequentes levam. Usar o Cloud Monitoring para plotar os tempos de execução das consultas responde diretamente à pergunta. A opção A plota o uso de slots, que mede o consumo de recursos em vez do tempo decorrido da consulta. As opções B e C usam o Cloud Trace, que é projetado para rastreamento de latência de requisições distribuídas entre serviços de aplicação e não é a ferramenta que expõe o tempo de execução de consultas do BigQuery; o Trace não capturaria isso sem instrumentação customizada, e plotar métricas é o ajuste nativo.

questions.question: You are designing a schema for a Cloud Spanner customer database. You want to store a phone number array field in a customer table. You also want to allow users to search customers by phone number.How should you design this schema?

options.text: Create a table named Customers. Add an Array field in a table that will hold phone numbers for the customer.
Create a table named Customers. Create a table named Phones. Add a CustomerId field in the Phones table to find the CustomerId from a phone number.
Create a table named Customers. Add an Array field in a table that will hold phone numbers for the customer. Create a secondary index on the Array field.
Create a table named Customers as a parent table. Create a table named Phones, and interleave this table into the Customer table. Create an index on the phone number field in the Phones table.

questions.correct_text: Create a table named Customers as a parent table. Create a table named Phones, and interleave this table into the Customer table. Create an index on the phone number field in the Phones table.
questions.explanation: Cloud Spanner does not support indexing array fields directly, so to make phone numbers searchable you should store them in a separate Phones table and index the phone number column. Interleaving the Phones table into the parent Customers table physically co-locates each customer's phone rows with the parent row, improving locality and join performance, while an index on the phone number column enables efficient lookups by phone. Options A and C use an Array field; Spanner cannot create a usable secondary index on an array element to support phone-number search, so C is invalid and A offers no search path. Option B creates a non-interleaved Phones table without leveraging interleaving for locality and omits indexing guidance, making D the best schema.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Spanner não suporta indexação direta de campos de array, então, para tornar números de telefone pesquisáveis, você deve armazená-los em uma tabela Phones separada e indexar a coluna do número de telefone. Fazer o interleaving da tabela Phones na tabela pai Customers co-localiza fisicamente as linhas de telefone de cada cliente com a linha pai, melhorando a localidade e o desempenho de joins, enquanto um índice na coluna do número de telefone permite buscas eficientes por telefone. As opções A e C usam um campo Array; o Spanner não consegue criar um índice secundário utilizável em um elemento de array para suportar a busca por número de telefone, então C é inválida e A não oferece caminho de busca. A opção B cria uma tabela Phones sem interleaving, sem aproveitar o interleaving para localidade e omite orientações de indexação, tornando D o melhor esquema.

questions.question: You are deploying a single website on App Engine that needs to be accessible via the URL http://www.altostrat.com/.What should you do?

options.text: Verify domain ownership with Webmaster Central. Create a DNS CNAME record to point to the App Engine canonical name ghs.googlehosted.com.
Verify domain ownership with Webmaster Central. Define an A record pointing to the single global App Engine IP address.
Define a mapping in dispatch.yaml to point the domain www.altostrat.com to your App Engine service. Create a DNS CNAME record to point to the App Engine canonical name ghs.googlehosted.com.
Define a mapping in dispatch.yaml to point the domain www.altostrat.com to your App Engine service. Define an A record pointing to the single global App Engine IP address.

questions.correct_text: Verify domain ownership with Webmaster Central. Create a DNS CNAME record to point to the App Engine canonical name ghs.googlehosted.com.
questions.explanation: To serve an App Engine app on a custom domain like www.altostrat.com, you first verify ownership of the domain, then map the subdomain to a DNS CNAME record pointing to ghs.googlehosted.com, which is App Engine's canonical host. A CNAME is the correct record type for a subdomain (www) and lets Google route and serve traffic with managed SSL. Defining an A record to a single global IP (B) is not how App Engine custom domains work for subdomains, and there is no single fixed global App Engine IP suited to this. dispatch.yaml (C, D) routes incoming requests to different services within an app based on URL paths/hosts; it does not establish external domain ownership or DNS mapping, so it is not the mechanism for attaching a custom domain.

questions.explanation_pt: Para servir um app do App Engine em um domínio personalizado como www.altostrat.com, você primeiro verifica a propriedade do domínio e, em seguida, mapeia o subdomínio para um registro CNAME do DNS apontando para ghs.googlehosted.com, que é o host canônico do App Engine. Um CNAME é o tipo de registro correto para um subdomínio (www) e permite que o Google roteie e sirva o tráfego com SSL gerenciado. Definir um registro A para um único IP global (B) não é como funcionam os domínios personalizados do App Engine para subdomínios, e não há um único IP global fixo do App Engine adequado para isso. O dispatch.yaml (C, D) roteia requisições recebidas para diferentes serviços dentro de um app com base em caminhos/hosts da URL; ele não estabelece propriedade de domínio externo nem mapeamento de DNS, portanto não é o mecanismo para anexar um domínio personalizado.

questions.question: You are running an application on App Engine that you inherited. You want to find out whether the application is using insecure binaries or is vulnerable to XSS attacks.Which service should you use?

options.text: Cloud Amor
Stackdriver Debugger
Cloud Security Scanner
Stackdriver Error Reporting

questions.correct_text: Cloud Security Scanner
questions.explanation: Cloud Security Scanner (Web Security Scanner) crawls a deployed App Engine, Compute Engine, or GKE web app and probes for common vulnerabilities such as cross-site scripting (XSS), Flash injection, mixed content, and use of insecure or outdated/vulnerable libraries and binaries. This directly matches the requirement to detect insecure binaries and XSS exposure. Cloud Armor (A) is a WAF/DDoS protection service that blocks malicious traffic at runtime but does not scan an app for vulnerabilities. Stackdriver Debugger (B) inspects live application state during execution, and Stackdriver Error Reporting (D) aggregates runtime exceptions; neither performs security vulnerability scanning.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Security Scanner (Web Security Scanner) rastreia um app web implantado no App Engine, Compute Engine ou GKE e sonda em busca de vulnerabilidades comuns, como cross-site scripting (XSS), injeção de Flash, conteúdo misto (mixed content) e uso de bibliotecas e binários inseguros ou desatualizados/vulneráveis. Isso atende diretamente ao requisito de detectar binários inseguros e exposição a XSS. O Cloud Armor (A) é um serviço de WAF/proteção contra DDoS que bloqueia tráfego malicioso em tempo de execução, mas não escaneia um app em busca de vulnerabilidades. O Stackdriver Debugger (B) inspeciona o estado da aplicação em tempo real durante a execução, e o Stackdriver Error Reporting (D) agrega exceções de runtime; nenhum deles realiza varredura de vulnerabilidades de segurança.

questions.question: You are working on a social media application. You plan to add a feature that allows users to upload images. These images will be 2 MB `" 1 GB in size. You want to minimize their infrastructure operations overhead for this feature.What should you do?

options.text: Change the application to accept images directly and store them in the database that stores other user information.
Change the application to create signed URLs for Cloud Storage. Transfer these signed URLs to the client application to upload images to Cloud Storage.
Set up a web server on GCP to accept user images and create a file store to keep uploaded files. Change the application to retrieve images from the file store.

Create a separate bucket for each user in Cloud Storage. Assign a separate service account to allow write access on each bucket. Transfer service account credentials to the client application based on user information. The application uses this service account to upload images to Cloud Storage.

questions.correct_text: Change the application to create signed URLs for Cloud Storage. Transfer these signed URLs to the client application to upload images to Cloud Storage.
questions.explanation: For large user-uploaded objects (2 MB to 1 GB), Cloud Storage is the appropriate, fully managed store, and generating signed URLs lets clients upload directly to a bucket without routing bytes through your application servers, minimizing operational overhead. This avoids running and scaling your own upload infrastructure and keeps your service accounts and credentials off the client. Storing binary images in the user database (A) bloats the database and is poorly suited to large blobs. Running your own web server and file store (C) maximizes operations overhead, the opposite of the goal. Creating a bucket and service account per user and shipping credentials to clients (D) is an unscalable, insecure anti-pattern that exposes long-lived credentials.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Para objetos grandes enviados pelos usuários (de 2 MB a 1 GB), o Cloud Storage é o armazenamento apropriado e totalmente gerenciado, e gerar signed URLs permite que os clientes façam upload diretamente para um bucket sem encaminhar os bytes pelos seus servidores de aplicação, minimizando o overhead operacional. Isso evita executar e escalar sua própria infraestrutura de upload e mantém suas service accounts e credenciais fora do cliente. Armazenar imagens binárias no banco de dados de usuários (A) incha o banco de dados e é mal adaptado para blobs grandes. Executar seu próprio servidor web e armazenamento de arquivos (C) maximiza o overhead operacional, o oposto do objetivo. Criar um bucket e uma service account por usuário e enviar credenciais para os clientes (D) é um antipadrão inseguro e não escalável que expõe credenciais de longa duração.

questions.question: Your application is built as a custom machine image. You have multiple unique deployments of the machine image. Each deployment is a separate managed instance group with its own template. Each deployment requires a unique set of configuration values. You want to provide these unique values to each deployment but use the same custom machine image in all deployments. You want to use out-of-the-box features of Compute Engine.What should you do?

options.text: Place the unique configuration values in the persistent disk.
Place the unique configuration values in a Cloud Bigtable table.
Place the unique configuration values in the instance template startup script.
Place the unique configuration values in the instance template instance metadata.

questions.correct_text: Place the unique configuration values in the instance template instance metadata.
questions.explanation: Instance metadata is the out-of-the-box Compute Engine mechanism for passing per-deployment configuration values to instances while reusing the same custom image; each instance template can define its own metadata key/value pairs (or metadata-driven startup script behavior), and instances read them via the metadata server. This cleanly separates configuration from the immutable image. Putting values on a persistent disk (A) adds storage management overhead and is not the standard config-injection path. Cloud Bigtable (B) is a heavyweight NoSQL database, vastly over-engineered for a handful of config values. Hardcoding values into the startup script (C) is less flexible than metadata; the recommended pattern is to store values in metadata and have the startup script read them, making metadata the best answer.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Os metadados de instância são o mecanismo nativo do Compute Engine para passar valores de configuração por implantação às instâncias enquanto se reutiliza a mesma imagem personalizada; cada instance template pode definir seus próprios pares de chave/valor de metadados (ou comportamento de startup script baseado em metadados), e as instâncias os leem via o servidor de metadados. Isso separa de forma limpa a configuração da imagem imutável. Colocar valores em um disco persistente (A) adiciona overhead de gerenciamento de armazenamento e não é o caminho padrão de injeção de configuração. O Cloud Bigtable (B) é um banco de dados NoSQL pesado, amplamente superdimensionado para um punhado de valores de configuração. Fixar (hardcode) valores no startup script (C) é menos flexível do que metadados; o padrão recomendado é armazenar os valores nos metadados e fazer o startup script lê-los, tornando os metadados a melhor resposta.

questions.question: Your application performs well when tested locally, but it runs significantly slower after you deploy it to a Compute Engine instance. You need to diagnose the problem. What should you do?What should you do?

options.text: File a ticket with Cloud Support indicating that the application performs faster locally.
Use Cloud Debugger snapshots to look at a point-in-time execution of the application.
Use Cloud Profiler to determine which functions within the application take the longest amount of time.
Add logging commands to the application and use Cloud Logging to check where the latency problem occurs.

questions.correct_text: Use Cloud Profiler to determine which functions within the application take the longest amount of time.
questions.explanation: Cloud Profiler continuously samples CPU and memory (heap) usage across an application's functions with low overhead, making it the right tool to pinpoint which functions consume the most time and explain why performance degrades when deployed. Filing a support ticket (A) does not diagnose the code. Cloud Debugger snapshots (B) capture variable state at a point in execution but do not measure where time is spent across the call stack. Adding ad-hoc logging and inspecting Cloud Logging (D) is laborious, imprecise, and changes the code; Profiler gives aggregated, statistical performance insight without that instrumentation effort.
