questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Profiler amostra continuamente o uso de CPU e memória (heap) entre as funções de uma aplicação com baixo overhead, tornando-o a ferramenta certa para identificar quais funções consomem mais tempo e explicar por que o desempenho degrada quando implantado. Abrir um ticket de suporte (A) não diagnostica o código. Os snapshots do Cloud Debugger (B) capturam o estado das variáveis em um ponto da execução, mas não medem onde o tempo é gasto ao longo da pilha de chamadas. Adicionar logs ad-hoc e inspecionar o Cloud Logging (D) é trabalhoso, impreciso e altera o código; o Profiler fornece insights de desempenho agregados e estatísticos sem esse esforço de instrumentação.

questions.question: You have an application running in App Engine. Your application is instrumented with Stackdriver Trace. The /product-details request reports details about four known unique products at /sku-details as shown below. You want to reduce the time it takes for the request to complete.What should you do?

options.text: Increase the size of the instance class.
Change the Persistent Disk type to SSD.
Change /product-details to perform the requests in parallel.
Store the /sku-details information in a database, and replace the webservice call with a database query.

questions.correct_text: Change /product-details to perform the requests in parallel.
questions.explanation: The Cloud Trace data shows the /product-details request making four sequential calls to /sku-details for four unique products. Because these calls are independent of one another, the latency accumulates as the sum of all four. Executing the requests in parallel (option C) allows them to run concurrently, so the total time approaches that of the single slowest call rather than the sum, directly reducing request completion time. Increasing the instance class (A) or switching to SSD persistent disk (B) addresses CPU/memory or disk I/O, neither of which is the bottleneck in serial network calls. Storing the data in a database and replacing the webservice call (D) is a larger architectural change that is not needed when the four products are known and can simply be fetched concurrently.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Os dados do Cloud Trace mostram a requisição /product-details fazendo quatro chamadas sequenciais para /sku-details para quatro produtos distintos. Como essas chamadas são independentes entre si, a latência se acumula como a soma das quatro. Executar as requisições em paralelo (opção C) permite que rodem simultaneamente, de modo que o tempo total se aproxima do da única chamada mais lenta, em vez da soma, reduzindo diretamente o tempo de conclusão da requisição. Aumentar a classe da instância (A) ou mudar para SSD persistent disk (B) trata de CPU/memória ou I/O de disco, sendo que nenhum é o gargalo em chamadas de rede seriais. Armazenar os dados em um banco de dados e substituir a chamada ao webservice (D) é uma mudança arquitetural maior que não é necessária quando os quatro produtos são conhecidos e podem simplesmente ser buscados concorrentemente.

questions.question: Your company has a data warehouse that keeps your application information in BigQuery. The BigQuery data warehouse keeps 2 PBs of user data. Recently, your company expanded your user base to include EU users and needs to comply with these requirements:✑ Your company must be able to delete all user account information upon user request.✑ All EU user data must be stored in a single region specifically for EU users.Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use BigQuery federated queries to query data from Cloud Storage.
Create a dataset in the EU region that will keep information about EU users only.
Create a Cloud Storage bucket in the EU region to store information for EU users only.
Re-upload your data using to a Cloud Dataflow pipeline by filtering your user records out.
Use DML statements in BigQuery to update/delete user records based on their requests.

questions.correct_text: Create a dataset in the EU region that will keep information about EU users only. | Use DML statements in BigQuery to update/delete user records based on their requests.
questions.explanation: To meet data residency, creating a dataset in the EU region dedicated to EU users (B) ensures that BigQuery physically stores their data in a single EU location, since dataset location is fixed at creation. To honor deletion requests, using DML statements such as DELETE in BigQuery (E) lets you remove specific user records on demand. Federated queries over Cloud Storage (A) do not control where the warehouse data resides nor satisfy deletion. Creating a Cloud Storage bucket for EU users (C) moves data out of the warehouse and doesn't address querying the existing BigQuery data. Re-uploading via a Dataflow pipeline that filters records out (D) is an expensive, recurring batch process for what targeted DML deletes handle natively.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para atender à residência de dados, criar um dataset na região EU dedicado aos usuários da UE (B) garante que o BigQuery armazene fisicamente os dados deles em um único local na UE, já que a localização do dataset é fixada na criação. Para honrar solicitações de exclusão, usar instruções DML como DELETE no BigQuery (E) permite remover registros específicos de usuários sob demanda. Consultas federadas sobre o Cloud Storage (A) não controlam onde os dados do data warehouse residem nem satisfazem a exclusão. Criar um bucket do Cloud Storage para usuários da UE (C) move os dados para fora do data warehouse e não resolve a consulta dos dados existentes no BigQuery. Reenviar via um pipeline do Dataflow que filtra os registros (D) é um processo em lote recorrente e caro para algo que os DELETEs DML direcionados tratam nativamente.

questions.question: Your App Engine standard configuration is as follows:service: productioninstance_class: B1You want to limit the application to 5 instances.Which code snippet should you include in your configuration?

options.text: manual_scaling: instances: 5 min_pending_latency: 30ms
manual_scaling: max_instances: 5 idle_timeout: 10m
basic_scaling: instances: 5 min_pending_latency: 30ms
basic_scaling: max_instances: 5 idle_timeout: 10m

questions.correct_text: basic_scaling: max_instances: 5 idle_timeout: 10m
questions.explanation: App Engine standard supports automatic, basic, and manual scaling. Basic scaling creates instances when requests arrive and shuts them down when idle, and it uses the max_instances parameter to cap the number of instances plus idle_timeout to control shutdown, which matches option D for limiting the app to 5 instances. Manual scaling (A and B) uses a fixed instances count and does not support max_instances or idle_timeout, so those snippets are invalid. Option C is wrong because basic_scaling uses max_instances rather than instances and does not use min_pending_latency (that belongs to automatic scaling). Therefore D is the only syntactically and semantically correct configuration.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: O App Engine standard suporta escalonamento automatic, basic e manual. O basic scaling cria instâncias quando as requisições chegam e as desliga quando ociosas, e usa o parâmetro max_instances para limitar o número de instâncias, além do idle_timeout para controlar o desligamento, o que corresponde à opção D para limitar a aplicação a 5 instâncias. O manual scaling (A e B) usa uma contagem fixa de instances e não suporta max_instances nem idle_timeout, então esses trechos são inválidos. A opção C está errada porque o basic_scaling usa max_instances em vez de instances e não usa min_pending_latency (que pertence ao automatic scaling). Portanto, D é a única configuração sintática e semanticamente correta.

questions.question: Your analytics system executes queries against a BigQuery dataset. The SQL query is executed in batch and passes the contents of a SQL file to the BigQueryCLI. Then it redirects the BigQuery CLI output to another process. However, you are getting a permission error from the BigQuery CLI when the queries are executed.You want to resolve the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the service account BigQuery Data Viewer and BigQuery Job User roles.
Grant the service account BigQuery Data Editor and BigQuery Data Viewer roles.
Create a view in BigQuery from the SQL query and SELECT* from the view in the CLI.
Create a new dataset in BigQuery, and copy the source table to the new dataset Query the new dataset and table from the CLI.

questions.correct_text: Grant the service account BigQuery Data Viewer and BigQuery Job User roles.
questions.explanation: Running a query through the BigQuery CLI requires two distinct permissions: the ability to run query jobs and the ability to read the underlying data. The BigQuery Job User role grants permission to create and run jobs (including queries), while BigQuery Data Viewer grants read access to the dataset, so granting both (A) resolves the permission error for read-only batch queries. Data Editor plus Data Viewer (B) provides data read/write but lacks the bigquery.jobs.create permission needed to launch the query job, so the error persists. Creating a view (C) or copying tables to a new dataset (D) does not address the missing job-execution permission and still requires the same underlying roles.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Executar uma consulta pela CLI do BigQuery requer duas permissões distintas: a capacidade de executar query jobs e a capacidade de ler os dados subjacentes. O papel BigQuery Job User concede permissão para criar e executar jobs (incluindo consultas), enquanto o BigQuery Data Viewer concede acesso de leitura ao dataset, portanto conceder ambos (A) resolve o erro de permissão para consultas em lote somente leitura. Data Editor mais Data Viewer (B) fornece leitura/escrita de dados, mas não tem a permissão bigquery.jobs.create necessária para iniciar o query job, então o erro persiste. Criar uma view (C) ou copiar tabelas para um novo dataset (D) não resolve a permissão de execução de job ausente e ainda requer os mesmos papéis subjacentes.

questions.question: Your application is running on Compute Engine and is showing sustained failures for a small number of requests. You have narrowed the cause down to a singleCompute Engine instance, but the instance is unresponsive to SSH.What should you do next?

options.text: Reboot the machine.
Enable and check the serial port output.
Delete the machine and create a new one.
Take a snapshot of the disk and attach it to a new machine.

questions.correct_text: Enable and check the serial port output.
questions.explanation: When a Compute Engine instance is unresponsive to SSH but still serving some requests, the priority is to diagnose the root cause without destroying evidence. Enabling and checking the serial port (console) output (B) lets you view boot messages, kernel panics, full disk conditions, or networking failures that explain why SSH is unavailable, making it the correct next diagnostic step. Rebooting (A) may clear the issue but discards the in-memory state and logs needed to understand it. Deleting and recreating the instance (C) destroys all diagnostic information. Taking a disk snapshot and attaching it to a new machine (D) is a heavier forensic step that is unnecessary before simply reading the serial output.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Quando uma instância do Compute Engine está sem resposta ao SSH, mas ainda atende a algumas requisições, a prioridade é diagnosticar a causa raiz sem destruir evidências. Ativar e verificar a saída da porta serial (console) (B) permite visualizar mensagens de boot, kernel panics, condições de disco cheio ou falhas de rede que explicam por que o SSH está indisponível, tornando esse o próximo passo de diagnóstico correto. Reiniciar (A) pode resolver o problema, mas descarta o estado em memória e os logs necessários para entendê-lo. Excluir e recriar a instância (C) destrói todas as informações de diagnóstico. Tirar um snapshot do disco e anexá-lo a uma nova máquina (D) é um passo forense mais pesado, desnecessário antes de simplesmente ler a saída serial.

questions.question: You configured your Compute Engine instance group to scale automatically according to overall CPU usage. However, your application's response latency increases sharply before the cluster has finished adding up instances. You want to provide a more consistent latency experience for your end users by changing the configuration of the instance group autoscaler.Which two configuration changes should you make? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add the label ג€AUTOSCALEג€ to the instance group template.
Decrease the cool-down period for instances added to the group.
Increase the target CPU usage for the instance group autoscaler.
Decrease the target CPU usage for the instance group autoscaler.
Remove the health-check for individual VMs in the instance group.

questions.correct_text: Decrease the cool-down period for instances added to the group. | Decrease the target CPU usage for the instance group autoscaler.
questions.explanation: To smooth out latency spikes during scale-up, the autoscaler must react sooner and bring instances into service faster. Decreasing the target CPU utilization (D) causes the autoscaler to add instances earlier, before CPU pressure becomes severe, giving more headroom. Decreasing the cool-down (initialization) period (B) means newly added instances are considered ready and counted toward capacity sooner, so the group responds more quickly. Increasing the target CPU (C) does the opposite by delaying scale-out until utilization is already high, worsening latency. Adding an arbitrary label (A) has no effect on autoscaling behavior, and removing health checks (E) would harm reliability without improving scaling responsiveness.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para suavizar picos de latência durante o scale-up, o autoscaler precisa reagir mais cedo e colocar instâncias em serviço mais rapidamente. Diminuir o target de utilização de CPU (D) faz com que o autoscaler adicione instâncias mais cedo, antes que a pressão de CPU se torne severa, dando mais folga. Diminuir o período de cool-down (inicialização) (B) significa que as instâncias recém-adicionadas são consideradas prontas e contabilizadas na capacidade mais cedo, então o grupo responde mais rapidamente. Aumentar o target de CPU (C) faz o oposto, atrasando o scale-out até que a utilização já esteja alta, piorando a latência. Adicionar um label arbitrário (A) não tem efeito sobre o comportamento de autoscaling, e remover os health checks (E) prejudicaria a confiabilidade sem melhorar a responsividade do scaling.

questions.question: You have an application controlled by a managed instance group. When you deploy a new version of the application, costs should be minimized and the number of instances should not increase. You want to ensure that, when each new instance is created, the deployment only continues if the new instance is healthy.What should you do?

options.text: Perform a rolling-action with maxSurge set to 1, maxUnavailable set to 0.
Perform a rolling-action with maxSurge set to 0, maxUnavailable set to 1
Perform a rolling-action with maxHealthy set to 1, maxUnhealthy set to 0.
Perform a rolling-action with maxHealthy set to 0, maxUnhealthy set to 1.

questions.correct_text: Perform a rolling-action with maxSurge set to 0, maxUnavailable set to 1
questions.explanation: A managed instance group rolling update is controlled by maxSurge (how many extra instances may be created above the target size) and maxUnavailable (how many existing instances may be taken offline). To keep the total number of instances from increasing and minimize cost, maxSurge must be 0, which means an old instance is removed and replaced rather than adding capacity, so maxUnavailable is set to 1 (B). The MIG only proceeds to the next instance once the newly created instance passes its health check, ensuring deployment continues only when the new instance is healthy. Option A (maxSurge 1) would temporarily add an instance, increasing the count and cost. Options C and D reference maxHealthy/maxUnhealthy, which are not valid rolling-action parameters.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Um rolling update de um managed instance group é controlado por maxSurge (quantas instâncias extras podem ser criadas acima do tamanho alvo) e maxUnavailable (quantas instâncias existentes podem ser tiradas de operação). Para evitar que o número total de instâncias aumente e minimizar o custo, maxSurge deve ser 0, o que significa que uma instância antiga é removida e substituída em vez de adicionar capacidade, então maxUnavailable é definido como 1 (B). O MIG só prossegue para a próxima instância depois que a instância recém-criada passa em seu health check, garantindo que a implantação continue somente quando a nova instância estiver saudável. A opção A (maxSurge 1) adicionaria temporariamente uma instância, aumentando a contagem e o custo. As opções C e D referenciam maxHealthy/maxUnhealthy, que não são parâmetros válidos de rolling-action.

questions.question: Your application requires service accounts to be authenticated to GCP products via credentials stored on its host Compute Engine virtual machine instances. You want to distribute these credentials to the host instances as securely as possible.What should you do?

options.text: Use HTTP signed URLs to securely provide access to the required resources.
Use the instance's service account Application Default Credentials to authenticate to the required resources.
Generate a P12 file from the GCP Console after the instance is deployed, and copy the credentials to the host instance before starting the application.
Commit the credential JSON file into your application's source repository, and have your CI/CD process package it with the software that is deployed to the instance.

questions.correct_text: Use the instance's service account Application Default Credentials to authenticate to the required resources.
questions.explanation: The most secure way to authenticate from a Compute Engine instance is to attach a service account to the VM and use Application Default Credentials (B). The credentials are short-lived tokens fetched automatically from the instance metadata server, so no long-lived key file is ever stored on disk or distributed manually, and they rotate automatically. Generating and copying a P12 file (C) or committing a JSON key into source control (D) creates static, long-lived secrets that can leak and are an anti-pattern. Signed URLs (A) grant time-limited access to specific objects (typically Cloud Storage) and are not a mechanism for authenticating a service account to GCP APIs generally.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: A forma mais segura de autenticar a partir de uma instância do Compute Engine é anexar uma service account à VM e usar Application Default Credentials (B). As credenciais são tokens de curta duração obtidos automaticamente do metadata server da instância, então nenhum arquivo de chave de longa duração é armazenado em disco ou distribuído manualmente, e eles rotacionam automaticamente. Gerar e copiar um arquivo P12 (C) ou commitar uma chave JSON no controle de versão (D) cria segredos estáticos e de longa duração que podem vazar e são um anti-pattern. Signed URLs (A) concedem acesso por tempo limitado a objetos específicos (tipicamente no Cloud Storage) e não são um mecanismo para autenticar uma service account nas APIs do GCP de forma geral.

questions.question: Your application is deployed in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You want to expose this application publicly behind a Cloud Load Balancing HTTP(S) load balancer.What should you do?

options.text: Configure a GKE Ingress resource.
Configure a GKE Service resource.
Configure a GKE Ingress resource with type: LoadBalancer.
Configure a GKE Service resource with type: LoadBalancer.

questions.correct_text: Configure a GKE Ingress resource.
questions.explanation: In GKE, exposing an application publicly behind a Cloud Load Balancing HTTP(S) load balancer is done by creating an Ingress resource (A). The GKE Ingress controller provisions an external HTTP(S) load balancer and routes traffic to backing Services based on HTTP rules. A Service of type LoadBalancer (D) creates a regional external network (L4) load balancer, not an HTTP(S) (L7) load balancer. A plain Service (B) only exposes the app internally or via NodePort/ClusterIP and does not create an HTTP(S) load balancer. Option C is invalid because Ingress resources do not take a type: LoadBalancer field.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: No GKE, expor uma aplicação publicamente por trás de um load balancer HTTP(S) do Cloud Load Balancing é feito criando um recurso Ingress (A). O Ingress controller do GKE provisiona um load balancer HTTP(S) externo e roteia o tráfego para os Services de backend com base em regras HTTP. Um Service do tipo LoadBalancer (D) cria um load balancer de rede externo regional (L4), não um load balancer HTTP(S) (L7). Um Service simples (B) só expõe a aplicação internamente ou via NodePort/ClusterIP e não cria um load balancer HTTP(S). A opção C é inválida porque recursos Ingress não aceitam um campo type: LoadBalancer.

questions.question: Your company is planning to migrate their on-premises Hadoop environment to the cloud. Increasing storage cost and maintenance of data stored in HDFS is a major concern for your company. You also want to make minimal changes to existing data analytics jobs and existing architecture.How should you proceed with the migration?

options.text: Migrate your data stored in Hadoop to BigQuery. Change your jobs to source their information from BigQuery instead of the on-premises Hadoop environment.
Create Compute Engine instances with HDD instead of SSD to save costs. Then perform a full migration of your existing environment into the new one in Compute Engine instances.

Create a Cloud Dataproc cluster on Google Cloud Platform, and then migrate your Hadoop environment to the new Cloud Dataproc cluster. Move your HDFS data into larger HDD disks to save on storage costs.

Create a Cloud Dataproc cluster on Google Cloud Platform, and then migrate your Hadoop code objects to the new cluster. Move your data to Cloud Storage and leverage the Cloud Dataproc connector to run jobs on that data.

questions.correct_text: Create a Cloud Dataproc cluster on Google Cloud Platform, and then migrate your Hadoop code objects to the new cluster. Move your data to Cloud Storage and leverage the Cloud Dataproc connector to run jobs on that data.
questions.explanation: The recommended pattern for lift-and-shift of Hadoop to Google Cloud while reducing storage cost is to run jobs on Dataproc and store data in Cloud Storage rather than HDFS (D). Dataproc clusters can read and write Cloud Storage directly through the Cloud Storage connector, so existing Hadoop/Spark jobs need minimal changes while you decouple compute from storage and benefit from cheaper, durable, scalable object storage. Keeping data in HDFS on persistent disks (B and C) does not solve the storage cost and maintenance concern because you still manage and pay for disk-backed HDFS. Migrating to BigQuery (A) would require significant rewrites of the analytics jobs, contradicting the requirement for minimal changes.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O padrão recomendado para o lift-and-shift de Hadoop para o Google Cloud reduzindo o custo de armazenamento é executar os jobs no Dataproc e armazenar os dados no Cloud Storage em vez de HDFS (D). Os clusters do Dataproc podem ler e gravar diretamente no Cloud Storage por meio do conector do Cloud Storage, de modo que os jobs Hadoop/Spark existentes exigem mudanças mínimas, ao mesmo tempo em que você desacopla a computação do armazenamento e se beneficia de um armazenamento de objetos mais barato, durável e escalável. Manter os dados em HDFS em discos persistentes (B e C) não resolve a preocupação com custo e manutenção de armazenamento, porque você ainda gerencia e paga pelo HDFS apoiado em disco. Migrar para o BigQuery (A) exigiria reescritas significativas dos jobs de análise, contrariando o requisito de mudanças mínimas.

questions.question: Your data is stored in Cloud Storage buckets. Fellow developers have reported that data downloaded from Cloud Storage is resulting in slow API performance.You want to research the issue to provide details to the GCP support team.Which command should you run?

options.text: gsutil test ג€"o output.json gs://my-bucket
gsutil perfdiag ג€"o output.json gs://my-bucket
gcloud compute scp example-instance:~/test-data ג€"o output.json gs://my-bucket
gcloud services test ג€"o output.json gs://my-bucket

questions.correct_text: gsutil perfdiag ג€"o output.json gs://my-bucket
questions.explanation: The gsutil perfdiag command runs a suite of diagnostic tests against a target bucket, measuring upload/download throughput, latency, and other performance metrics, and can write the results to a file with the -o flag that you can share with Google Cloud support. This is exactly the kind of data needed to investigate slow Cloud Storage transfer performance. Option A is invalid because gsutil has no 'test' subcommand. Option C uses gcloud compute scp to copy files between Compute Engine instances over SSH and does not produce performance diagnostics for a bucket. Option D references a nonexistent 'gcloud services test' command.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O comando gsutil perfdiag executa um conjunto de testes de diagnóstico contra um bucket de destino, medindo a taxa de transferência de upload/download, a latência e outras métricas de desempenho, e pode gravar os resultados em um arquivo com a flag -o que você pode compartilhar com o suporte do Google Cloud. Esse é exatamente o tipo de dado necessário para investigar um desempenho lento de transferência do Cloud Storage. A opção A é inválida porque o gsutil não tem um subcomando 'test'. A opção C usa o gcloud compute scp para copiar arquivos entre instâncias do Compute Engine via SSH e não produz diagnósticos de desempenho para um bucket. A opção D faz referência a um comando inexistente 'gcloud services test'.

questions.question: You are using Cloud Build build to promote a Docker image to Development, Test, and Production environments. You need to ensure that the same Docker image is deployed to each of these environments.How should you identify the Docker image in your build?

options.text: Use the latest Docker image tag.
Use a unique Docker image name.
Use the digest of the Docker image.
Use a semantic version Docker image tag.

questions.correct_text: Use the digest of the Docker image.
questions.explanation: Referencing the image by its content-addressable digest (sha256) guarantees that the exact same immutable image bits are deployed to Development, Test, and Production, since the digest is a cryptographic hash of the image contents. Tags such as 'latest' (option A) or a semantic version tag (option D) are mutable pointers that can be reassigned to a different image, so the same tag could resolve to different binaries across environments. Using a unique image name (option B) does not help promote one validated artifact unchanged through environments and complicates the pipeline. Only the digest provides the immutability needed for reliable promotion.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Referenciar a imagem por seu digest endereçável por conteúdo (sha256) garante que exatamente os mesmos bits imutáveis da imagem sejam implantados em Development, Test e Production, já que o digest é um hash criptográfico do conteúdo da imagem. Tags como 'latest' (opção A) ou uma tag de versão semântica (opção D) são ponteiros mutáveis que podem ser reatribuídos a uma imagem diferente, de modo que a mesma tag poderia resolver para binários diferentes entre os ambientes. Usar um nome de imagem único (opção B) não ajuda a promover um único artefato validado sem alterações pelos ambientes e complica o pipeline. Apenas o digest fornece a imutabilidade necessária para uma promoção confiável.

questions.question: Your company has created an application that uploads a report to a Cloud Storage bucket. When the report is uploaded to the bucket, you want to publish a message to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic. You want to implement a solution that will take a small amount to effort to implement.What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Cloud Storage bucket to trigger Cloud Pub/Sub notifications when objects are modified.
Create an App Engine application to receive the file; when it is received, publish a message to the Cloud Pub/Sub topic.
Create a Cloud Function that is triggered by the Cloud Storage bucket. In the Cloud Function, publish a message to the Cloud Pub/Sub topic.
Create an application deployed in a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster to receive the file; when it is received, publish a message to the Cloud Pub/Sub topic.

questions.correct_text: Configure the Cloud Storage bucket to trigger Cloud Pub/Sub notifications when objects are modified.
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage supports native Pub/Sub notifications that can be configured directly on a bucket to publish a message to a topic whenever objects are created, deleted, or otherwise changed. This requires only a single gsutil/gcloud configuration command and no custom code, making it the lowest-effort solution. Options C and B require writing and maintaining a Cloud Function or App Engine app, and option D requires building and running a GKE-hosted application, all of which add development and operational overhead. The built-in bucket notification is the most direct integration with Pub/Sub.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Storage oferece suporte a notificações nativas do Pub/Sub que podem ser configuradas diretamente em um bucket para publicar uma mensagem em um topic sempre que objetos são criados, excluídos ou alterados de outra forma. Isso exige apenas um único comando de configuração gsutil/gcloud e nenhum código personalizado, tornando-a a solução de menor esforço. As opções C e B exigem escrever e manter uma Cloud Function ou um app do App Engine, e a opção D exige construir e executar uma aplicação hospedada no GKE, todas adicionando sobrecarga de desenvolvimento e operação. A notificação de bucket integrada é a integração mais direta com o Pub/Sub.

questions.question: Your teammate has asked you to review the code below, which is adding a credit to an account balance in Cloud Datastore.Which improvement should you suggest your teammate make?

options.text: Get the entity with an ancestor query.
Get and put the entity in a transaction.
Use a strongly consistent transactional database.
Don't return the account entity from the function.

questions.correct_text: Get and put the entity in a transaction.
questions.explanation: Updating an account balance is a read-modify-write operation: you read the current balance, add the credit, and write it back. Without a transaction, concurrent updates can cause a lost-update race condition and an inconsistent balance, so the get and put must be wrapped in a single Datastore transaction to ensure atomicity and consistency. Datastore/Firestore in Datastore mode already provides ACID transactions, so there is no need to switch to a different strongly consistent database (option C). An ancestor query (option A) addresses query consistency, not the atomicity of the update, and whether the function returns the entity (option D) has no bearing on data correctness.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Atualizar o saldo de uma conta é uma operação de leitura-modificação-gravação: você lê o saldo atual, adiciona o crédito e o grava de volta. Sem uma transação, atualizações concorrentes podem causar uma condição de corrida de atualização perdida (lost-update) e um saldo inconsistente, então o get e o put devem ser encapsulados em uma única transação do Datastore para garantir atomicidade e consistência. O Datastore/Firestore no modo Datastore já fornece transações ACID, então não há necessidade de mudar para um banco de dados fortemente consistente diferente (opção C). Uma consulta de ancestral (ancestor query, opção A) trata da consistência da consulta, não da atomicidade da atualização, e o fato de a função retornar ou não a entidade (opção D) não tem relação com a correção dos dados.

questions.question: Your company stores their source code in a Cloud Source Repositories repository. Your company wants to build and test their code on each source code commit to the repository and requires a solution that is managed and has minimal operations overhead.Which method should they use?

options.text: Use Cloud Build with a trigger configured for each source code commit.
Use Jenkins deployed via the Google Cloud Platform Marketplace, configured to watch for source code commits.
Use a Compute Engine virtual machine instance with an open source continuous integration tool, configured to watch for source code commits.
Use a source code commit trigger to push a message to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic that triggers an App Engine service to build the source code.

questions.correct_text: Use Cloud Build with a trigger configured for each source code commit.
questions.explanation: Cloud Build is Google Cloud's fully managed, serverless CI/CD service, and a build trigger can be configured to run on every commit to a Cloud Source Repositories repository, providing build and test automation with no servers to maintain. This directly satisfies the requirements of a managed solution with minimal operations overhead. Options B and C require deploying and operating Jenkins or another open-source CI tool on infrastructure you manage, which adds significant maintenance burden. Option D builds a fragile custom pipeline through Pub/Sub and App Engine that is far more complex than simply configuring a native Cloud Build trigger.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Build é o serviço de CI/CD totalmente gerenciado e serverless do Google Cloud, e um build trigger pode ser configurado para executar a cada commit em um repositório do Cloud Source Repositories, fornecendo automação de build e teste sem servidores para manter. Isso atende diretamente aos requisitos de uma solução gerenciada com mínima sobrecarga operacional. As opções B e C exigem implantar e operar o Jenkins ou outra ferramenta de CI open-source em infraestrutura que você gerencia, o que adiciona uma carga significativa de manutenção. A opção D constrói um pipeline customizado e frágil por meio de Pub/Sub e App Engine, que é muito mais complexo do que simplesmente configurar um build trigger nativo do Cloud Build.

questions.question: You are writing a Compute Engine hosted application in project A that needs to securely authenticate to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic in project B.What should you do?

options.text: Configure the instances with a service account owned by project B. Add the service account as a Cloud Pub/Sub publisher to project A.
Configure the instances with a service account owned by project A. Add the service account as a publisher on the topic.
Configure Application Default Credentials to use the private key of a service account owned by project B. Add the service account as a Cloud Pub/Sub publisher to project A.
Configure Application Default Credentials to use the private key of a service account owned by project A. Add the service account as a publisher on the topic

questions.correct_text: Configure the instances with a service account owned by project A. Add the service account as a publisher on the topic.
questions.explanation: The recommended pattern for cross-project authentication is to attach a service account that belongs to project A (where the Compute Engine instances run) and then grant that service account the Pub/Sub Publisher role on the topic in project B. IAM permissions can be granted to a principal from any project, so a service account from project A can be given publisher access to a resource in project B. Application Default Credentials are automatically supplied by the attached service account on the VM, so there is no need to download or distribute a private key, which avoids the security risk of managing key files (eliminating C and D). Options A and C are wrong because the service account would be owned by project B and the publisher permission is mistakenly added to project A rather than on the topic in project B.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O padrão recomendado para autenticação entre projetos é anexar uma service account que pertence ao projeto A (onde as instâncias do Compute Engine são executadas) e então conceder a essa service account o papel Pub/Sub Publisher no tópico do projeto B. Permissões de IAM podem ser concedidas a um principal de qualquer projeto, portanto uma service account do projeto A pode receber acesso de publisher a um recurso no projeto B. As Application Default Credentials são fornecidas automaticamente pela service account anexada à VM, então não há necessidade de baixar ou distribuir uma chave privada, o que evita o risco de segurança de gerenciar arquivos de chave (eliminando C e D). As opções A e C estão erradas porque a service account seria de propriedade do projeto B e a permissão de publisher é adicionada por engano ao projeto A em vez de ao tópico no projeto B.

questions.question: You are developing a corporate tool on Compute Engine for the finance department, which needs to authenticate users and verify that they are in the finance department. All company employees use G Suite.What should you do?

options.text: Enable Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy on the HTTP(s) load balancer and restrict access to a Google Group containing users in the finance department. Verify the provided JSON Web Token within the application.

Enable Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy on the HTTP(s) load balancer and restrict access to a Google Group containing users in the finance department. Issue client-side certificates to everybody in the finance team and verify the certificates in the application.
Configure Cloud Armor Security Policies to restrict access to only corporate IP address ranges. Verify the provided JSON Web Token within the application.

Configure Cloud Armor Security Policies to restrict access to only corporate IP address ranges. Issue client side certificates to everybody in the finance team and verify the certificates in the application.

questions.correct_text: Enable Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy on the HTTP(s) load balancer and restrict access to a Google Group containing users in the finance department. Verify the provided JSON Web Token within the application.
questions.explanation: Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) sits in front of the HTTP(S) load balancer and authenticates users with their Google/G Suite identities, allowing access to be restricted to a Google Group that contains only finance department members. IAP forwards a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) to the backend, which the application can cryptographically verify to confirm the user's identity and group membership, providing defense in depth. Issuing client-side certificates (B and D) is operationally heavy and does not leverage the existing G Suite identities, while Cloud Armor (C and D) only filters by IP address and cannot authenticate individual users or verify department membership. Therefore A is correct because it combines IAP-based identity authorization with in-app JWT verification.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) fica na frente do load balancer HTTP(S) e autentica usuários com suas identidades Google/G Suite, permitindo que o acesso seja restrito a um Google Group que contém apenas membros do departamento financeiro. O IAP encaminha um JSON Web Token (JWT) assinado ao backend, que a aplicação pode verificar criptograficamente para confirmar a identidade do usuário e a participação no grupo, fornecendo defesa em profundidade. Emitir certificados client-side (B e D) é operacionalmente pesado e não aproveita as identidades G Suite existentes, enquanto o Cloud Armor (C e D) filtra apenas por endereço IP e não pode autenticar usuários individuais nem verificar a participação no departamento. Portanto, A está correta porque combina a autorização de identidade baseada em IAP com a verificação de JWT dentro da aplicação.

questions.question: Your API backend is running on multiple cloud providers. You want to generate reports for the network latency of your API.Which two steps should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Zipkin collector to gather data.
Use Fluentd agent to gather data.
Use Stackdriver Trace to generate reports.
Use Stackdriver Debugger to generate report.
Use Stackdriver Profiler to generate report.

questions.correct_text: Use Zipkin collector to gather data. | Use Stackdriver Trace to generate reports.
questions.explanation: Cloud Trace (formerly Stackdriver Trace) is the distributed tracing service used to measure and report request and network latency, and it is compatible with the Zipkin tracing format. By deploying a Zipkin collector you can gather trace/latency data from API backends running across multiple cloud providers and forward that data into Cloud Trace, which then generates the latency reports. The Fluentd agent (B) is for collecting logs, not latency traces. Cloud Debugger (D) inspects application state at runtime and Cloud Profiler (E) analyzes CPU and memory consumption, so neither produces network latency reports, making A and C the correct pair.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Trace (anteriormente Stackdriver Trace) é o serviço de rastreamento distribuído usado para medir e relatar a latência de requisições e de rede, e é compatível com o formato de rastreamento Zipkin. Ao implantar um coletor Zipkin, você pode reunir dados de rastreamento/latência de backends de API executados em múltiplos provedores de nuvem e encaminhar esses dados para o Cloud Trace, que então gera os relatórios de latência. O agente Fluentd (B) é para coletar logs, não rastreamentos de latência. O Cloud Debugger (D) inspeciona o estado da aplicação em tempo de execução e o Cloud Profiler (E) analisa o consumo de CPU e memória, então nenhum produz relatórios de latência de rede, tornando A e C o par correto.

questions.question: Case study -This is a case study. Case studies are not timed separately. You can use as much exam time as you would like to complete each case. However, there may be additional case studies and sections on this exam. You must manage your time to ensure that you are able to complete all questions included on this exam in the time provided.To answer the questions included in a case study, you will need to reference information that is provided in the case study. Case studies might contain exhibits and other resources that provide more information about the scenario that is described in the case study. Each question is independent of the other questions in this case study.At the end of this case study, a review screen will appear. This screen allows you to review your answers and to make changes before you move to the next section of the exam. After you begin a new section, you cannot return to this section.To start the case study -To display the first question in this case study, click the Next button. Use the buttons in the left pane to explore the content of the case study before you answer the questions. Clicking these buttons displays information such as business requirements, existing environment, and problem statements. If the case study has anAll Information tab, note that the information displayed is identical to the information displayed on the subsequent tabs. When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.Company Overview -HipLocal is a community application designed to facilitate communication between people in close proximity. It is used for event planning and organizing sporting events, and for businesses to connect with their local communities. HipLocal launched recently in a few neighborhoods in Dallas and is rapidly growing into a global phenomenon. Its unique style of hyper-local community communication and business outreach is in demand around the world.Executive Statement -We are the number one local community app; it's time to take our local community services global. Our venture capital investors want to see rapid growth and the same great experience for new local and virtual communities that come online, whether their members are 10 or 10000 miles away from each other.Solution Concept -HipLocal wants to expand their existing service, with updated functionality, in new regions to better serve their global customers. They want to hire and train a new team to support these regions in their time zones. They will need to ensure that the application scales smoothly and provides clear uptime data.Existing Technical Environment -HipLocal's environment is a mix of on-premises hardware and infrastructure running in Google Cloud Platform. The HipLocal team understands their application well, but has limited experience in global scale applications. Their existing technical environment is as follows:* Existing APIs run on Compute Engine virtual machine instances hosted in GCP.* State is stored in a single instance MySQL database in GCP.* Data is exported to an on-premises Teradata/Vertica data warehouse.* Data analytics is performed in an on-premises Hadoop environment.* The application has no logging.* There are basic indicators of uptime; alerts are frequently fired when the APIs are unresponsive.Business Requirements -HipLocal's investors want to expand their footprint and support the increase in demand they are seeing. Their requirements are:* Expand availability of the application to new regions.* Increase the number of concurrent users that can be supported.* Ensure a consistent experience for users when they travel to different regions.* Obtain user activity metrics to better understand how to monetize their product.* Ensure compliance with regulations in the new regions (for example, GDPR).* Reduce infrastructure management time and cost.* Adopt the Google-recommended practices for cloud computing.Technical Requirements -* The application and backend must provide usage metrics and monitoring.* APIs require strong authentication and authorization.* Logging must be increased, and data should be stored in a cloud analytics platform.* Move to serverless architecture to facilitate elastic scaling.* Provide authorized access to internal apps in a secure manner.Which database should HipLocal use for storing user activity?

options.text: BigQuery
Cloud SQL
Cloud Spanner
Cloud Datastore

questions.correct_text: BigQuery
questions.explanation: User activity data is needed to obtain analytics and monetization metrics, and HipLocal's requirement is to store data in a cloud analytics platform. BigQuery is Google's serverless, highly scalable data warehouse purpose-built for analytical queries over large volumes of event/activity data, making it the ideal target for user activity metrics. Cloud SQL (B) is a relational OLTP database that does not scale well for large-scale analytics, Cloud Spanner (C) is for globally consistent transactional workloads rather than analytics, and Cloud Datastore/Firestore (D) is a NoSQL operational store not designed for analytical reporting. Therefore BigQuery (A) best satisfies the analytics and metrics requirement.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Dados de atividade do usuário são necessários para obter métricas de analytics e monetização, e o requisito da HipLocal é armazenar dados em uma plataforma de analytics na nuvem. O BigQuery é o data warehouse serverless e altamente escalável do Google, projetado especificamente para consultas analíticas sobre grandes volumes de dados de eventos/atividade, tornando-o o destino ideal para métricas de atividade do usuário. O Cloud SQL (B) é um banco de dados relacional OLTP que não escala bem para analytics em larga escala, o Cloud Spanner (C) é para cargas de trabalho transacionais globalmente consistentes em vez de analytics, e o Cloud Datastore/Firestore (D) é um armazenamento operacional NoSQL não projetado para relatórios analíticos. Portanto, o BigQuery (A) é o que melhor atende ao requisito de analytics e métricas.

options.text: Block all traffic on port 443.
Allow all traffic into the network.
Allow traffic on port 443 for a specific tag.
Allow all traffic on port 443 into the network.

questions.correct_text: Allow traffic on port 443 for a specific tag.
questions.explanation: Google Cloud VPC firewall rules follow the principle of least privilege, so traffic should only be permitted to the specific resources that need it rather than broadly. Allowing traffic on port 443 (HTTPS) only for instances carrying a specific network tag scopes the rule precisely to the intended servers, which is the recommended secure configuration. Blocking all traffic on port 443 (A) would break the HTTPS application entirely, while allowing all traffic into the network (B) or allowing all traffic on 443 network-wide (D) violate least privilege by exposing more than necessary. Therefore C, allowing port 443 only for a specific tag, is the correct firewall configuration.

questions.explanation_pt: As regras de firewall da VPC do Google Cloud seguem o princípio do menor privilégio, então o tráfego deve ser permitido apenas para os recursos específicos que precisam dele, em vez de de forma ampla. Permitir tráfego na porta 443 (HTTPS) apenas para instâncias que carregam uma network tag específica limita a regra precisamente aos servidores pretendidos, que é a configuração segura recomendada. Bloquear todo o tráfego na porta 443 (A) quebraria completamente a aplicação HTTPS, enquanto permitir todo o tráfego na rede (B) ou permitir todo o tráfego na 443 em toda a rede (D) violam o menor privilégio ao expor mais do que o necessário. Portanto C, permitir a porta 443 apenas para uma tag específica, é a configuração correta de firewall.

options.text: Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API for redaction of the review dataset.
Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API for de-identification of the review dataset.
Use the Cloud Natural Language Processing API for redaction of the review dataset.
Use the Cloud Natural Language Processing API for de-identification of the review dataset.

questions.correct_text: Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API for de-identification of the review dataset.
questions.explanation: Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP) is purpose-built to inspect data for sensitive elements (PII such as names, emails, phone numbers) and transform it. For an analytics use case where the data science team still needs usable, structured review data, de-identification is the correct transformation because it removes or masks sensitive fields while preserving the analytical value and format of the dataset (for example, via tokenization, masking, or bucketing). Redaction, by contrast, simply removes the sensitive content entirely, which destroys context that may be useful for analysis, so option A is less appropriate. The Cloud Natural Language API (options C and D) performs entity extraction, sentiment, and syntax analysis; it is not a tool for redacting or de-identifying sensitive data, so both options that reference it are incorrect.

options.text: Cloud Spanner
Cloud Datastore
Cloud Memorystore as a cache
Separate Cloud SQL clusters for each region

questions.correct_text: Cloud Spanner
questions.explanation: HipLocal needs a database that scales horizontally to support more concurrent users, spans multiple regions to serve new geographies, and provides a consistent experience for users who travel between regions. Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed, horizontally scalable relational database offering strong external consistency, making it the only option that satisfies global scale plus a consistent SQL-based experience as a migration from MySQL. Memorystore is an in-memory cache, not a system of record, and separate regional Cloud SQL clusters would fragment state and break the requirement for a single consistent experience across regions.

questions.question: You have an application deployed in production. When a new version is deployed, you want to ensure that all production traffic is routed to the new version of your application. You also want to keep the previous version deployed so that you can revert to it if there is an issue with the new version.Which deployment strategy should you use?

options.text: Blue/green deployment
Canary deployment
Rolling deployment
Recreate deployment

questions.correct_text: Blue/green deployment
questions.explanation: A blue/green deployment runs two complete environments: the current (blue) version serving all traffic and the new (green) version deployed in parallel. Traffic is switched all at once from blue to green, satisfying the requirement that all production traffic is routed to the new version, while keeping the old version intact so you can instantly roll back if the new version misbehaves. A canary deployment sends only a small percentage of traffic to the new version, so it does not route all traffic at once. A rolling deployment gradually replaces instances, mixing old and new versions and removing old instances as it progresses, which does not preserve a clean revert target. A recreate deployment tears down the old version before bringing up the new one, leaving no fallback to revert to.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Um blue/green deployment executa dois ambientes completos: a versão atual (blue) atendendo todo o tráfego e a nova versão (green) implantada em paralelo. O tráfego é trocado de uma só vez da blue para a green, satisfazendo o requisito de que todo o tráfego de produção seja roteado para a nova versão, ao mesmo tempo em que mantém a versão antiga intacta para que você possa fazer rollback instantaneamente caso a nova versão se comporte mal. Um canary deployment envia apenas uma pequena porcentagem do tráfego para a nova versão, então não roteia todo o tráfego de uma só vez. Um rolling deployment substitui instâncias gradualmente, misturando versões antigas e novas e removendo instâncias antigas conforme avança, o que não preserva um alvo limpo de reversão. Um recreate deployment desativa a versão antiga antes de subir a nova, não deixando nenhum fallback para reverter.

questions.question: You are porting an existing Apache/MySQL/PHP application stack from a single machine to GoogleKubernetes Engine. You need to determine how to containerize the application. Your approach should follow Google-recommended best practices for availability.What should you do?

options.text: Package each component in a separate container. Implement readiness and liveness probes.
Package the application in a single container. Use a process management tool to manage each component.
Package each component in a separate container. Use a script to orchestrate the launch of the components.
Package the application in a single container. Use a bash script as an entrypoint to the container, and then spawn each component as a background job.

questions.correct_text: Package each component in a separate container. Implement readiness and liveness probes.
questions.explanation: Google's container best practices follow the principle of one process/concern per container, so the Apache web server, the PHP application, and the MySQL database should each be packaged in separate containers rather than bundled together. Readiness probes ensure traffic is only sent to a pod once it is ready to serve, and liveness probes restart unhealthy containers, which together maximize availability in GKE. Packaging everything in a single container (options B and D) violates the single-responsibility model, complicates scaling, and makes Kubernetes health management and independent updates impossible. Using a custom script to orchestrate component launch (option C) reinvents what Kubernetes already provides and omits the health probes essential for high availability.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: As melhores práticas de contêineres do Google seguem o princípio de um processo/responsabilidade por contêiner, então o servidor web Apache, a aplicação PHP e o banco de dados MySQL devem cada um ser empacotados em contêineres separados, em vez de agrupados juntos. Readiness probes garantem que o tráfego só seja enviado a um pod quando ele estiver pronto para atender, e liveness probes reiniciam contêineres não saudáveis, o que juntos maximizam a disponibilidade no GKE. Empacotar tudo em um único contêiner (opções B e D) viola o modelo de responsabilidade única, complica o escalonamento e torna impossível o gerenciamento de saúde do Kubernetes e as atualizações independentes. Usar um script personalizado para orquestrar o lançamento dos componentes (opção C) reinventa o que o Kubernetes já fornece e omite os health probes essenciais para a alta disponibilidade.

questions.question: You are developing an application that will be launched on Compute Engine instances into multiple distinct projects, each corresponding to the environments in your software development process (development, QA, staging, and production). The instances in each project have the same application code but a different configuration. During deployment, each instance should receive the application's configuration based on the environment it serves. You want to minimize the number of steps to configure this flow. What should you do?

options.text: When creating your instances, configure a startup script using the gcloud command to determine the project name that indicates the correct environment.

In each project, configure a metadata key ג€environmentג€ whose value is the environment it serves. Use your deployment tool to query the instance metadata and configure the application based on the ג€environmentג€ value.

Deploy your chosen deployment tool on an instance in each project. Use a deployment job to retrieve the appropriate configuration file from your version control system, and apply the configuration when deploying the application on each instance.

During each instance launch, configure an instance custom-metadata key named ג€environmentג€ whose value is the environment the instance serves. Use your deployment tool to query the instance metadata, and configure the application based on the ג€environmentג€ value.

questions.correct_text: In each project, configure a metadata key ג€environmentג€ whose value is the environment it serves. Use your deployment tool to query the instance metadata and configure the application based on the ג€environmentג€ value.
questions.explanation: Because each environment lives in its own project, setting a single project-wide metadata key 'environment' once per project is the simplest approach: the value is defined a single time and every instance in that project inherits it. The deployment tool then queries the instance metadata server to read the 'environment' value and applies the matching configuration, minimizing the number of configuration steps. Option D is functionally similar but sets the metadata per-instance at every launch, which adds a repeated step for each instance rather than configuring it once per project. Option A relies on parsing the project name in a startup script, which is brittle and more error-prone, and option C requires deploying and maintaining a separate deployment tool instance plus version-control retrieval logic in each project, adding significant overhead.
