questions.explanation_pt: Como cada ambiente vive em seu próprio projeto, definir uma única chave de metadados 'environment' no nível do projeto, uma vez por projeto, é a abordagem mais simples: o valor é definido uma única vez e toda instância nesse projeto o herda. A ferramenta de implantação então consulta o servidor de metadados da instância para ler o valor de 'environment' e aplica a configuração correspondente, minimizando o número de etapas de configuração. A opção D é funcionalmente semelhante, mas define os metadados por instância a cada inicialização, o que adiciona uma etapa repetida para cada instância em vez de configurá-la uma vez por projeto. A opção A depende de analisar o nome do projeto em um startup script, o que é frágil e mais propenso a erros, e a opção C exige implantar e manter uma instância separada da ferramenta de implantação, além de lógica de recuperação por controle de versão em cada projeto, adicionando sobrecarga significativa.

questions.question: You are developing an ecommerce application that stores customer, order, and inventory data as relational tables inside Cloud Spanner. During a recent load test, you discover that Spanner performance is not scaling linearly as expected. Which of the following is the cause?

options.text: The use of 64-bit numeric types for 32-bit numbers.
The use of the STRING data type for arbitrary-precision values.
The use of Version 1 UUIDs as primary keys that increase monotonically.
The use of LIKE instead of STARTS_WITH keyword for parameterized SQL queries.

questions.correct_text: The use of Version 1 UUIDs as primary keys that increase monotonically.
questions.explanation: Cloud Spanner distributes data across splits based on primary key ranges, so primary keys must be designed to spread writes evenly. Using Version 1 UUIDs (or any monotonically increasing value such as timestamps or auto-increment integers) as the primary key causes all new writes to land at the same key range, creating a hotspot on a single split that prevents linear scaling. The recommended practice is to use random keys such as Version 4 UUIDs, hash the key, or bit-reverse a sequential value. Using a 64-bit type for a 32-bit number (A) or STRING for numeric values (B) wastes minor storage but does not break scaling, and LIKE vs STARTS_WITH (D) affects query optimization, not write scalability under load.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Spanner distribui dados entre splits com base em intervalos de chave primária, então as chaves primárias devem ser projetadas para distribuir as gravações de forma uniforme. Usar UUIDs Version 1 (ou qualquer valor monotonicamente crescente, como timestamps ou inteiros auto-increment) como chave primária faz com que todas as novas gravações caiam no mesmo intervalo de chave, criando um hotspot em um único split que impede o escalonamento linear. A prática recomendada é usar chaves aleatórias, como UUIDs Version 4, aplicar hash na chave ou inverter os bits (bit-reverse) de um valor sequencial. Usar um tipo de 64 bits para um número de 32 bits (A) ou STRING para valores numéricos (B) desperdiça uma pequena quantidade de armazenamento, mas não quebra o escalonamento, e LIKE vs STARTS_WITH (D) afeta a otimização de consultas, não a escalabilidade de gravação sob carga.

questions.question: You are developing an application that reads credit card data from a Pub/Sub subscription. You have written code and completed unit testing. You need to test thePub/Sub integration before deploying to Google Cloud. What should you do?

options.text: Create a service to publish messages, and deploy the Pub/Sub emulator. Generate random content in the publishing service, and publish to the emulator.
Create a service to publish messages to your application. Collect the messages from Pub/Sub in production, and replay them through the publishing service.
Create a service to publish messages, and deploy the Pub/Sub emulator. Collect the messages from Pub/Sub in production, and publish them to the emulator.
Create a service to publish messages, and deploy the Pub/Sub emulator. Publish a standard set of testing messages from the publishing service to the emulator.

questions.correct_text: Create a service to publish messages, and deploy the Pub/Sub emulator. Publish a standard set of testing messages from the publishing service to the emulator.
questions.explanation: The Pub/Sub emulator lets you test integration locally without connecting to the production Pub/Sub service or incurring cost. Because the goal is repeatable integration testing, you should publish a standard, deterministic set of test messages to the emulator so results are consistent and verifiable across runs. Random content (A) produces non-deterministic, hard-to-validate behavior, and copying real production messages (B and C) is dangerous and noncompliant since the payloads contain credit card data that should never be moved into a test environment. Therefore deploying the emulator and replaying a fixed set of crafted test messages (D) is the correct, safe, and reproducible approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O emulador do Pub/Sub permite testar a integração localmente sem se conectar ao serviço de produção do Pub/Sub nem incorrer em custo. Como o objetivo é um teste de integração repetível, você deve publicar um conjunto padrão e determinístico de mensagens de teste no emulador para que os resultados sejam consistentes e verificáveis entre execuções. Conteúdo aleatório (A) produz comportamento não determinístico e difícil de validar, e copiar mensagens reais de produção (B e C) é perigoso e não conforme, já que os payloads contêm dados de cartão de crédito que nunca deveriam ser movidos para um ambiente de teste. Portanto, implantar o emulador e reproduzir um conjunto fixo de mensagens de teste elaboradas (D) é a abordagem correta, segura e reproduzível.

questions.question: You are designing an application that will subscribe to and receive messages from a single Pub/Sub topic and insert corresponding rows into a database. Your application runs on Linux and leverages preemptible virtual machines to reduce costs. You need to create a shutdown script that will initiate a graceful shutdown.What should you do?

options.text: Write a shutdown script that uses inter-process signals to notify the application process to disconnect from the database.
Write a shutdown script that broadcasts a message to all signed-in users that the Compute Engine instance is going down and instructs them to save current work and sign out.
Write a shutdown script that writes a file in a location that is being polled by the application once every five minutes. After the file is read, the application disconnects from the database.
Write a shutdown script that publishes a message to the Pub/Sub topic announcing that a shutdown is in progress. After the application reads the message, it disconnects from the database.

questions.correct_text: Write a shutdown script that uses inter-process signals to notify the application process to disconnect from the database.
questions.explanation: Preemptible (and Spot) VMs receive a 30-second termination notice, and Compute Engine runs the configured shutdown script during that window, so the script must act quickly. The correct, immediate way to trigger graceful cleanup is to have the shutdown script send an inter-process signal (such as SIGTERM) to the application process, which then catches it and disconnects from the database in time. Broadcasting to signed-in users (B) is irrelevant to a backend subscriber service. Polling a file every five minutes (C) is far too slow for the 30-second shutdown window, and publishing a Pub/Sub message back to the topic (D) is indirect, unreliable within the short window, and could be consumed by other subscribers rather than the local process.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: VMs Preemptible (e Spot) recebem um aviso de encerramento de 30 segundos, e o Compute Engine executa o shutdown script configurado durante essa janela, então o script deve agir rapidamente. A forma correta e imediata de acionar a limpeza graciosa é fazer com que o shutdown script envie um sinal entre processos (como SIGTERM) ao processo da aplicação, que então o captura e se desconecta do banco de dados a tempo. Transmitir uma mensagem aos usuários conectados (B) é irrelevante para um serviço de assinante de backend. Consultar um arquivo a cada cinco minutos (C) é lento demais para a janela de encerramento de 30 segundos, e publicar uma mensagem do Pub/Sub de volta ao tópico (D) é indireto, não confiável dentro da janela curta e poderia ser consumido por outros assinantes em vez do processo local.

questions.question: You work for a web development team at a small startup. Your team is developing a Node.js application using Google Cloud services, including Cloud Storage and Cloud Build. The team uses a Git repository for version control. Your manager calls you over the weekend and instructs you to make an emergency update to one of the company's websites, and you're the only developer available. You need to access Google Cloud to make the update, but you don't have your work laptop. You are not allowed to store source code locally on a non-corporate computer. How should you set up your developer environment?

options.text: Use a text editor and the Git command line to send your source code updates as pull requests from a public computer.
Use a text editor and the Git command line to send your source code updates as pull requests from a virtual machine running on a public computer.
Use Cloud Shell and the built-in code editor for development. Send your source code updates as pull requests.

Use a Cloud Storage bucket to store the source code that you need to edit. Mount the bucket to a public computer as a drive, and use a code editor to update the code. Turn on versioning for the bucket, and point it to the team's Git repository.

questions.correct_text: Use Cloud Shell and the built-in code editor for development. Send your source code updates as pull requests.
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell provides a browser-based, ephemeral development environment with the gcloud CLI, Git, and a built-in code editor, and all work happens on Google-managed infrastructure rather than the local machine. This satisfies the requirement to make the update without a work laptop and without storing source code locally on a non-corporate computer, since nothing persists on the public machine. Options A and B store and run source code on the public computer (even inside a VM, the code resides locally), violating the policy, and option D misuses Cloud Storage as if it were a Git repository, which is technically incorrect and still mounts editable code to the untrusted machine.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Shell fornece um ambiente de desenvolvimento efêmero baseado em navegador, com a gcloud CLI, o Git e um editor de código integrado, e todo o trabalho acontece em infraestrutura gerenciada pelo Google, e não na máquina local. Isso atende ao requisito de fazer a atualização sem um laptop de trabalho e sem armazenar o código-fonte localmente em um computador não corporativo, já que nada persiste na máquina pública. As opções A e B armazenam e executam o código-fonte no computador público (mesmo dentro de uma VM, o código reside localmente), violando a política, e a opção D usa indevidamente o Cloud Storage como se fosse um repositório Git, o que é tecnicamente incorreto e ainda monta código editável na máquina não confiável.

questions.question: Your team develops services that run on Google Kubernetes Engine. You need to standardize their log data using Google-recommended practices and make the data more useful in the fewest number of steps. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create aggregated exports on application logs to BigQuery to facilitate log analytics.
Create aggregated exports on application logs to Cloud Storage to facilitate log analytics.
Write log output to standard output (stdout) as single-line JSON to be ingested into Cloud Logging as structured logs.
Mandate the use of the Logging API in the application code to write structured logs to Cloud Logging.
Mandate the use of the Pub/Sub API to write structured data to Pub/Sub and create a Dataflow streaming pipeline to normalize logs and write them to BigQuery for analytics.

questions.correct_text: Create aggregated exports on application logs to BigQuery to facilitate log analytics. | Write log output to standard output (stdout) as single-line JSON to be ingested into Cloud Logging as structured logs.
questions.explanation: On GKE the Google-recommended logging practice is for containers to write structured logs as single-line JSON to stdout/stderr, which the logging agent automatically picks up and ingests into Cloud Logging as structured entries with parsed fields, requiring no application coupling to a logging SDK (C). To make that data more useful for analytics, you then create a log sink (aggregated export) to BigQuery, enabling SQL-based log analytics (A). Writing logs to Cloud Storage (B) supports archival but not interactive analytics. Mandating direct use of the Logging API (D) or routing logs through Pub/Sub and a Dataflow pipeline to BigQuery (E) adds unnecessary code and operational steps compared to the simpler stdout-plus-sink approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: No GKE, a prática de logging recomendada pelo Google é que os containers escrevam logs estruturados como JSON de linha única em stdout/stderr, que o logging agent captura e ingere automaticamente no Cloud Logging como entradas estruturadas com campos já parseados, sem exigir nenhum acoplamento da aplicação a um SDK de logging (C). Para tornar esses dados mais úteis para análise, você então cria um log sink (exportação agregada) para o BigQuery, habilitando análise de logs baseada em SQL (A). Escrever logs no Cloud Storage (B) atende ao arquivamento, mas não à análise interativa. Exigir o uso direto da Logging API (D) ou rotear logs através do Pub/Sub e de um pipeline do Dataflow até o BigQuery (E) adiciona código e etapas operacionais desnecessárias em comparação com a abordagem mais simples de stdout mais sink.

questions.question: You are designing a deployment technique for your new applications on Google Cloud. As part of your deployment planning, you want to use live traffic to gather performance metrics for both new and existing applications. You need to test against the full production load prior to launch. What should you do?

options.text: Use canary deployment
Use blue/green deployment
Use rolling updates deployment
Use A/B testing with traffic mirroring during deployment

questions.correct_text: Use A/B testing with traffic mirroring during deployment
questions.explanation: A/B testing combined with traffic mirroring lets you send a copy of live production traffic to the new version while the original still serves users, so you gather real performance metrics under the full production load without affecting end users before launch. Canary deployment only routes a small subset of real users to the new version, so it does not exercise the full production load and end users are exposed to the unproven release. Blue/green deployment switches all traffic at once after testing in isolation, so it does not use live traffic to compare versions side by side. Rolling updates gradually replace instances but do not mirror traffic for comparative performance analysis.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: O teste A/B combinado com traffic mirroring permite enviar uma cópia do tráfego de produção em tempo real para a nova versão, enquanto a versão original continua atendendo os usuários, de modo que você coleta métricas reais de desempenho sob a carga total de produção sem afetar os usuários finais antes do lançamento. O canary deployment apenas roteia um pequeno subconjunto de usuários reais para a nova versão, então não exercita a carga total de produção e os usuários finais ficam expostos a um release não comprovado. O blue/green deployment troca todo o tráfego de uma vez após testar em isolamento, então não usa tráfego em tempo real para comparar as versões lado a lado. Os rolling updates substituem instâncias gradualmente, mas não espelham o tráfego para análise comparativa de desempenho.

questions.question: You support an application that uses the Cloud Storage API. You review the logs and discover multiple HTTP 503 Service Unavailable error responses from theAPI. Your application logs the error and does not take any further action. You want to implement Google-recommended retry logic to improve success rates.Which approach should you take?

options.text: Retry the failures in batch after a set number of failures is logged.
Retry each failure at a set time interval up to a maximum number of times.
Retry each failure at increasing time intervals up to a maximum number of tries.
Retry each failure at decreasing time intervals up to a maximum number of tries.

questions.correct_text: Retry each failure at increasing time intervals up to a maximum number of tries.
questions.explanation: HTTP 503 errors are transient, and Google recommends retrying with truncated exponential backoff, which means waiting at increasing time intervals between retries up to a maximum number of attempts. This spreads out retries and avoids overwhelming the service while it recovers. Retrying at a fixed interval (B) can create synchronized retry storms and does not back off as the service stays busy. Decreasing intervals (D) would hammer the service more aggressively as failures continue, worsening the overload. Batching retries after a number of failures (A) adds latency and does not follow the recommended per-request backoff pattern.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Erros HTTP 503 são transitórios, e o Google recomenda fazer retry com truncated exponential backoff, o que significa esperar intervalos de tempo crescentes entre as tentativas até um número máximo de tentativas. Isso distribui os retries e evita sobrecarregar o serviço enquanto ele se recupera. Fazer retry em intervalo fixo (B) pode criar tempestades de retry sincronizadas e não recua à medida que o serviço permanece ocupado. Diminuir os intervalos (D) pressionaria o serviço de forma mais agressiva à medida que as falhas continuam, piorando a sobrecarga. Agrupar retries após um número de falhas (A) adiciona latência e não segue o padrão de backoff por requisição recomendado.

questions.question: You need to redesign the ingestion of audit events from your authentication service to allow it to handle a large increase in traffic. Currently, the audit service and the authentication system run in the same Compute Engine virtual machine. You plan to use the following Google Cloud tools in the new architecture:✑ Multiple Compute Engine machines, each running an instance of the authentication service✑ Multiple Compute Engine machines, each running an instance of the audit service✑ Pub/Sub to send the events from the authentication services.How should you set up the topics and subscriptions to ensure that the system can handle a large volume of messages and can scale efficiently?

options.text: Create one Pub/Sub topic. Create one pull subscription to allow the audit services to share the messages.
Create one Pub/Sub topic. Create one pull subscription per audit service instance to allow the services to share the messages.
Create one Pub/Sub topic. Create one push subscription with the endpoint pointing to a load balancer in front of the audit services.
Create one Pub/Sub topic per authentication service. Create one pull subscription per topic to be used by one audit service.
Create one Pub/Sub topic per authentication service. Create one push subscription per topic, with the endpoint pointing to one audit service.

questions.correct_text: Create one Pub/Sub topic. Create one pull subscription to allow the audit services to share the messages.
questions.explanation: A single Pub/Sub topic with a single pull subscription shared by all audit service instances is the correct pattern: Pub/Sub load-balances the delivery of messages from one subscription across all connected subscriber instances, so adding more audit instances scales throughput automatically. Creating a pull subscription per instance (B) would deliver every message to every subscription, causing each instance to process all messages rather than sharing the work. Multiple topics per authentication service (D, E) fragments the stream unnecessarily and complicates scaling. A push subscription to a load balancer (C) adds an extra component and loses the native flow control and horizontal scaling benefits of shared pull subscribers.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Um único tópico do Pub/Sub com uma única pull subscription compartilhada por todas as instâncias do serviço de auditoria é o padrão correto: o Pub/Sub faz o balanceamento de carga da entrega de mensagens de uma subscription entre todas as instâncias subscriber conectadas, então adicionar mais instâncias de auditoria escala a vazão automaticamente. Criar uma pull subscription por instância (B) entregaria cada mensagem a todas as subscriptions, fazendo com que cada instância processasse todas as mensagens em vez de dividir o trabalho. Múltiplos tópicos por serviço de autenticação (D, E) fragmenta o fluxo desnecessariamente e complica o escalonamento. Uma push subscription para um load balancer (C) adiciona um componente extra e perde o flow control nativo e os benefícios de escalonamento horizontal dos pull subscribers compartilhados.

questions.question: You are developing a marquee stateless web application that will run on Google Cloud. The rate of the incoming user traffic is expected to be unpredictable, with no traffic on some days and large spikes on other days. You need the application to automatically scale up and down, and you need to minimize the cost associated with running the application. What should you do?

options.text: Build the application in Python with Firestore as the database. Deploy the application to Cloud Run.
Build the application in C# with Firestore as the database. Deploy the application to App Engine flexible environment.
Build the application in Python with CloudSQL as the database. Deploy the application to App Engine standard environment.
Build the application in Python with Firestore as the database. Deploy the application to a Compute Engine managed instance group with autoscaling.

questions.correct_text: Build the application in Python with Firestore as the database. Deploy the application to Cloud Run.
questions.explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform that automatically scales stateless containers from zero to many instances based on incoming requests, so it handles unpredictable spikes and scales to zero on idle days, minimizing cost. Pairing it with Firestore, a serverless NoSQL database that also scales automatically, keeps the whole stack pay-per-use. App Engine flexible environment (B) runs on always-on VMs that do not scale to zero, so it incurs cost during no-traffic days. App Engine standard with Cloud SQL (C) can scale the app to zero but Cloud SQL instances run continuously and add fixed cost. A Compute Engine managed instance group (D) requires at least one running VM and scales slower than serverless, increasing cost and complexity.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Run é uma plataforma serverless totalmente gerenciada que escala automaticamente containers stateless de zero a muitas instâncias com base nas requisições recebidas, então lida com picos imprevisíveis e escala a zero em dias ociosos, minimizando custos. Combiná-lo com o Firestore, um banco de dados NoSQL serverless que também escala automaticamente, mantém toda a stack no modelo pague-pelo-uso. O App Engine flexible environment (B) roda em VMs sempre ativas que não escalam a zero, então gera custo durante dias sem tráfego. O App Engine standard com Cloud SQL (C) pode escalar a aplicação a zero, mas as instâncias do Cloud SQL rodam continuamente e adicionam custo fixo. Um managed instance group do Compute Engine (D) requer pelo menos uma VM em execução e escala mais lentamente que o serverless, aumentando custo e complexidade.

questions.question: You have written a Cloud Function that accesses other Google Cloud resources. You want to secure the environment using the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new service account that has Editor authority to access the resources. The deployer is given permission to get the access token.
Create a new service account that has a custom IAM role to access the resources. The deployer is given permission to get the access token.
Create a new service account that has Editor authority to access the resources. The deployer is given permission to act as the new service account.
Create a new service account that has a custom IAM role to access the resources. The deployer is given permission to act as the new service account.

questions.correct_text: Create a new service account that has a custom IAM role to access the resources. The deployer is given permission to act as the new service account.
questions.explanation: Least privilege is achieved by creating a dedicated service account with a custom IAM role that grants only the specific permissions the function needs, and granting the deployer the iam.serviceAccountUser role (permission to act as the service account) so it can deploy the function with that identity. Editor authority (A, C) is far too broad and violates least privilege. Granting only permission to get an access token (A, B) is not the correct mechanism for deploying a function under a service account; the deployer needs the serviceAccountUser permission to attach the identity at deploy time. Therefore the combination of a custom IAM role plus actAs permission is correct.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O menor privilégio é alcançado criando uma service account dedicada com um papel IAM personalizado que concede apenas as permissões específicas de que a função precisa, e concedendo ao implantador o papel iam.serviceAccountUser (permissão para atuar como a service account) para que ele possa implantar a função com essa identidade. A autoridade de Editor (A, C) é abrangente demais e viola o menor privilégio. Conceder apenas a permissão de obter um access token (A, B) não é o mecanismo correto para implantar uma função sob uma service account; o implantador precisa da permissão serviceAccountUser para anexar a identidade no momento da implantação. Portanto, a combinação de um papel IAM personalizado com a permissão actAs é a correta.

questions.question: You are a SaaS provider deploying dedicated blogging software to customers in your Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You want to configure a secure multi-tenant platform to ensure that each customer has access to only their own blog and can't affect the workloads of other customers. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Application-layer Secrets on the GKE cluster to protect the cluster.
Deploy a namespace per tenant and use Network Policies in each blog deployment.
Use GKE Audit Logging to identify malicious containers and delete them on discovery.
Build a custom image of the blogging software and use Binary Authorization to prevent untrusted image deployments.

questions.correct_text: Deploy a namespace per tenant and use Network Policies in each blog deployment.
questions.explanation: Deploying a separate namespace per tenant provides logical isolation of resources within the GKE cluster, and applying Network Policies restricts pod-to-pod traffic so one customer's blog cannot reach or affect another's workloads. This combination is the standard Google-recommended approach for soft multi-tenancy on GKE. Application-layer Secrets only encrypts Kubernetes Secrets with a KMS key and does nothing to isolate tenant workloads from one another. Audit Logging is detective and reactive rather than preventive, and Binary Authorization only ensures trusted images are deployed but does not isolate running tenants.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Implantar um namespace separado por tenant fornece isolamento lógico de recursos dentro do cluster GKE, e aplicar Network Policies restringe o tráfego pod-a-pod para que o blog de um cliente não possa alcançar ou afetar as cargas de trabalho de outro. Essa combinação é a abordagem padrão recomendada pelo Google para multi-tenancy flexível (soft multi-tenancy) no GKE. O Application-layer Secrets apenas criptografa Kubernetes Secrets com uma chave KMS e não faz nada para isolar as cargas de trabalho dos tenants entre si. O Audit Logging é detectivo e reativo, em vez de preventivo, e o Binary Authorization apenas garante que imagens confiáveis sejam implantadas, mas não isola os tenants em execução.

questions.question: You have decided to migrate your Compute Engine application to Google Kubernetes Engine. You need to build a container image and push it to Artifact Registry using Cloud Build. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Run gcloud builds submit in the directory that contains the application source code.
Run gcloud run deploy app-name --image gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/app-name in the directory that contains the application source code.
Run gcloud container images add-tag gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/app-name gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/app-name:latest in the directory that contains the application source code.
In the application source directory, create a file named cloudbuild.yaml that contains the following contents:
In the application source directory, create a file named cloudbuild.yaml that contains the following contents:

questions.correct_text: Run gcloud builds submit in the directory that contains the application source code. | In the application source directory, create a file named cloudbuild.yaml that contains the following contents:
questions.explanation: Running gcloud builds submit from the application source directory triggers Cloud Build, which by default looks for build configuration to build and push the image. Providing a cloudbuild.yaml file that defines the docker build and push steps (or uses the gcloud/docker builder) instructs Cloud Build exactly how to build the container and push it to Artifact Registry. Together these two actions accomplish the build-and-push workflow. gcloud run deploy targets Cloud Run, not the requested build/push to Artifact Registry; gcloud container images add-tag only retags an existing image rather than building one.

questions.explanation_pt: Executar gcloud builds submit a partir do diretório de código-fonte da aplicação aciona o Cloud Build, que por padrão procura a configuração de build para construir e enviar (push) a imagem. Fornecer um arquivo cloudbuild.yaml que define as etapas de docker build e push (ou usa o builder gcloud/docker) instrui o Cloud Build exatamente sobre como construir o contêiner e enviá-lo ao Artifact Registry. Juntas, essas duas ações realizam o fluxo de build-and-push. O gcloud run deploy tem como alvo o Cloud Run, e não o build/push solicitado para o Artifact Registry; o gcloud container images add-tag apenas re-marca (retag) uma imagem existente, em vez de construir uma.

questions.question: You are developing an internal application that will allow employees to organize community events within your company. You deployed your application on a single Compute Engine instance. Your company uses Google Workspace (formerly G Suite), and you need to ensure that the company employees can authenticate to the application from anywhere. What should you do?

options.text: Add a public IP address to your instance, and restrict access to the instance using firewall rules. Allow your company's proxy as the only source IP address.
Add an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the instance, and set up Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP). Configure the IAP settings to allow your company domain to access the website.

Set up a VPN tunnel between your company network and your instance's VPC location on Google Cloud. Configure the required firewall rules and routing information to both the on-premises and Google Cloud networks.

Add a public IP address to your instance, and allow traffic from the internet. Generate a random hash, and create a subdomain that includes this hash and points to your instance. Distribute this DNS address to your company's employees.

questions.correct_text: Add an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the instance, and set up Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP). Configure the IAP settings to allow your company domain to access the website.
questions.explanation: Placing an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the instance and enabling Identity-Aware Proxy lets you enforce Google Workspace identity-based access without a VPN, allowing employees to authenticate from anywhere while you restrict access to your company domain. IAP integrates directly with Google identities and applies context-aware access control at the application layer. Restricting by proxy source IP is brittle and does not authenticate individual users. A VPN tunnel adds operational complexity and does not provide per-user authentication, and exposing the instance via a secret hashed subdomain provides only security-through-obscurity with no real authentication.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Colocar um HTTP(S) load balancer na frente da instância e habilitar o Identity-Aware Proxy permite impor controle de acesso baseado em identidade do Google Workspace sem uma VPN, permitindo que os funcionários se autentiquem de qualquer lugar enquanto você restringe o acesso ao domínio da sua empresa. O IAP integra-se diretamente com as identidades do Google e aplica controle de acesso sensível ao contexto (context-aware) na camada de aplicação. Restringir pelo IP de origem do proxy é frágil e não autentica usuários individuais. Um túnel VPN adiciona complexidade operacional e não fornece autenticação por usuário, e expor a instância por meio de um subdomínio secreto com hash fornece apenas segurança por obscuridade, sem autenticação real.

questions.question: Your development team is using Cloud Build to promote a Node.js application built on App Engine from your staging environment to production. The application relies on several directories of photos stored in a Cloud Storage bucket named webphotos-staging in the staging environment. After the promotion, these photos must be available in a Cloud Storage bucket named webphotos-prod in the production environment. You want to automate the process where possible. What should you do?

options.text: Manually copy the photos to webphotos-prod.
Add a startup script in the application's app.yami file to move the photos from webphotos-staging to webphotos-prod.
Add a build step in the cloudbuild.yaml file before the promotion step with the arguments:
Add a build step in the cloudbuild.yaml file before the promotion step with the arguments:

questions.correct_text: Add a build step in the cloudbuild.yaml file before the promotion step with the arguments:
questions.explanation: Adding a build step in cloudbuild.yaml before the promotion step that uses gsutil to copy the photos from webphotos-staging to webphotos-prod automates the file transfer as part of the existing Cloud Build pipeline. This keeps the process repeatable and integrated with the deployment workflow. Manually copying the photos defeats the automation goal. Using a startup script in app.yaml is not how App Engine works, and app.yaml has no startup script directive for moving bucket contents; bucket-to-bucket copies belong in the build pipeline, not the application runtime.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Adicionar uma etapa de build no cloudbuild.yaml, antes da etapa de promoção, que usa o gsutil para copiar as fotos de webphotos-staging para webphotos-prod automatiza a transferência de arquivos como parte do pipeline existente do Cloud Build. Isso mantém o processo repetível e integrado ao fluxo de implantação. Copiar as fotos manualmente anula o objetivo de automação. Usar um startup script no app.yaml não é como o App Engine funciona, e o app.yaml não possui uma diretiva de startup script para mover o conteúdo de buckets; cópias entre buckets pertencem ao pipeline de build, não ao tempo de execução da aplicação.

questions.question: You are developing a web application that will be accessible over both HTTP and HTTPS and will run on Compute Engine instances. On occasion, you will need to SSH from your remote laptop into one of the Compute Engine instances to conduct maintenance on the app. How should you configure the instances while following Google-recommended best practices?

options.text: Set up a backend with Compute Engine web server instances with a private IP address behind a TCP proxy load balancer.
Configure the firewall rules to allow all ingress traffic to connect to the Compute Engine web servers, with each server having a unique external IP address.
Configure Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy API for SSH access. Then configure the Compute Engine servers with private IP addresses behind an HTTP(s) load balancer for the application web traffic.

Set up a backend with Compute Engine web server instances with a private IP address behind an HTTP(S) load balancer. Set up a bastion host with a public IP address and open firewall ports. Connect to the web instances using the bastion host.

questions.correct_text: Configure Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy API for SSH access. Then configure the Compute Engine servers with private IP addresses behind an HTTP(s) load balancer for the application web traffic.
questions.explanation: Using Identity-Aware Proxy for TCP/SSH forwarding lets you securely SSH into instances that have only private IP addresses without exposing them to the internet, while placing the web servers behind an HTTP(S) load balancer handles the public HTTP and HTTPS application traffic. This follows Google best practices by eliminating public IPs on the VMs and avoiding open SSH ports. Allowing all ingress with unique external IPs is insecure, and a TCP proxy load balancer does not natively terminate HTTP/HTTPS application traffic as required. A bastion host with a public IP and open firewall ports adds attack surface and operational overhead that IAP removes.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Usar o Identity-Aware Proxy para encaminhamento de TCP/SSH permite que você faça SSH de forma segura em instâncias que possuem apenas endereços IP privados, sem expô-las à internet, enquanto colocar os servidores web atrás de um HTTP(S) load balancer trata o tráfego público de aplicação HTTP e HTTPS. Isso segue as práticas recomendadas do Google ao eliminar IPs públicos nas VMs e evitar portas SSH abertas. Permitir todo o tráfego de entrada (ingress) com IPs externos exclusivos é inseguro, e um TCP proxy load balancer não termina nativamente o tráfego de aplicação HTTP/HTTPS conforme exigido. Um bastion host com IP público e portas de firewall abertas adiciona superfície de ataque e sobrecarga operacional que o IAP elimina.

questions.question: You have a mixture of packaged and internally developed applications hosted on a Compute Engine instance that is running Linux. These applications write log records as text in local files. You want the logs to be written to Cloud Logging. What should you do?

options.text: Pipe the content of the files to the Linux Syslog daemon.
Install a Google version of fluentd on the Compute Engine instance.
Install a Google version of collectd on the Compute Engine instance.
Using cron, schedule a job to copy the log files to Cloud Storage once a day.

questions.correct_text: Install a Google version of fluentd on the Compute Engine instance.
questions.explanation: The Google version of the Cloud Logging agent is built on fluentd, which can tail text log files and stream their records to Cloud Logging without modifying the applications. Installing it on the Linux Compute Engine instance lets both packaged and internally developed apps that write to local files have their logs ingested automatically. Piping to the Syslog daemon (A) only captures what is sent to syslog and is not a complete solution for arbitrary application log files. collectd (C) is the metrics/monitoring agent, not the logging agent, so it does not send log text. Copying files to Cloud Storage with cron (D) does not place the data in Cloud Logging and loses near-real-time visibility.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: A versão do Google do agente do Cloud Logging é baseada no fluentd, que pode acompanhar (tail) arquivos de log de texto e transmitir seus registros para o Cloud Logging sem modificar as aplicações. Instalá-lo na instância Linux do Compute Engine permite que tanto aplicativos empacotados quanto desenvolvidos internamente que gravam em arquivos locais tenham seus logs ingeridos automaticamente. Redirecionar (piping) para o daemon Syslog (A) captura apenas o que é enviado ao syslog e não é uma solução completa para arquivos de log de aplicação arbitrários. O collectd (C) é o agente de métricas/monitoramento, não o agente de logging, portanto não envia o texto dos logs. Copiar arquivos para o Cloud Storage com cron (D) não coloca os dados no Cloud Logging e perde a visibilidade em tempo quase real.

questions.question: You want to create `fully baked` or `golden` Compute Engine images for your application. You need to bootstrap your application to connect to the appropriate database according to the environment the application is running on (test, staging, production). What should you do?

options.text: Embed the appropriate database connection string in the image. Create a different image for each environment.

When creating the Compute Engine instance, add a tag with the name of the database to be connected. In your application, query the Compute Engine API to pull the tags for the current instance, and use the tag to construct the appropriate database connection string.

When creating the Compute Engine instance, create a metadata item with a key of ג€DATABASEג€ and a value for the appropriate database connection string. In your application, read the ג€DATABASEג€ environment variable, and use the value to connect to the appropriate database.

When creating the Compute Engine instance, create a metadata item with a key of ג€DATABASEג€ and a value for the appropriate database connection string. In your application, query the metadata server for the ג€DATABASEג€ value, and use the value to connect to the appropriate database.

questions.correct_text: When creating the Compute Engine instance, create a metadata item with a key of ג€DATABASEג€ and a value for the appropriate database connection string. In your application, query the metadata server for the ג€DATABASEג€ value, and use the value to connect to the appropriate database.
questions.explanation: Golden images should be environment-agnostic so the same image can be promoted across test, staging, and production. Storing the database connection string as instance metadata and having the application read it from the metadata server at runtime keeps configuration external to the image and avoids per-environment images. Embedding the string and building separate images (A) defeats the purpose of a single golden image and multiplies maintenance. Compute Engine tags (B) are for network firewall targeting and do not hold arbitrary key/value configuration data. Option C is incorrect because custom metadata keys are not automatically exposed as environment variables; the application must explicitly query the metadata server, which is what D describes.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Golden images devem ser independentes do ambiente, para que a mesma imagem possa ser promovida entre teste, staging e produção. Armazenar a string de conexão do banco de dados como metadados da instância e fazer com que a aplicação a leia do servidor de metadados em tempo de execução mantém a configuração externa à imagem e evita imagens por ambiente. Embutir a string e construir imagens separadas (A) anula o propósito de uma única golden image e multiplica a manutenção. As tags do Compute Engine (B) servem para direcionamento de firewall de rede e não armazenam dados de configuração arbitrários no formato chave/valor. A opção C está incorreta porque chaves de metadados personalizadas não são automaticamente expostas como variáveis de ambiente; a aplicação deve consultar explicitamente o servidor de metadados, que é o que a opção D descreve.

questions.question: You are developing a microservice-based application that will be deployed on a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. The application needs to read and write to aSpanner database. You want to follow security best practices while minimizing code changes. How should you configure your application to retrieve Spanner credentials?

options.text: Configure the appropriate service accounts, and use Workload Identity to run the pods.
Store the application credentials as Kubernetes Secrets, and expose them as environment variables.
Configure the appropriate routing rules, and use a VPC-native cluster to directly connect to the database.
Store the application credentials using Cloud Key Management Service, and retrieve them whenever a database connection is made.

questions.correct_text: Configure the appropriate service accounts, and use Workload Identity to run the pods.
questions.explanation: Workload Identity is the Google-recommended way for GKE workloads to authenticate to Google Cloud APIs such as Spanner. It binds a Kubernetes service account to an IAM service account so pods obtain short-lived, automatically rotated credentials via Application Default Credentials, requiring minimal or no code changes and no static secrets. Storing credentials as Kubernetes Secrets and exposing them as environment variables (B) keeps long-lived keys that can leak and must be rotated manually. VPC-native networking (C) governs pod IP routing, not credential retrieval or authentication. Storing keys in Cloud KMS (D) still relies on managing exported service account keys and adds code to fetch and decrypt them, which is less secure and more intrusive than Workload Identity.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Workload Identity é a forma recomendada pelo Google para que cargas de trabalho do GKE se autentiquem nas APIs do Google Cloud, como o Spanner. Ele vincula uma conta de serviço do Kubernetes a uma conta de serviço do IAM, de modo que os pods obtenham credenciais de curta duração e rotacionadas automaticamente por meio do Application Default Credentials, exigindo alterações mínimas ou nenhuma alteração de código e nenhum segredo estático. Armazenar credenciais como Kubernetes Secrets e expô-las como variáveis de ambiente (B) mantém chaves de longa duração que podem vazar e precisam ser rotacionadas manualmente. A rede VPC-native (C) governa o roteamento de IP dos pods, não a obtenção de credenciais ou a autenticação. Armazenar chaves no Cloud KMS (D) ainda depende do gerenciamento de chaves de conta de serviço exportadas e adiciona código para buscá-las e descriptografá-las, o que é menos seguro e mais intrusivo do que o Workload Identity.

questions.question: You are deploying your application on a Compute Engine instance that communicates with Cloud SQL. You will use Cloud SQL Proxy to allow your application to communicate to the database using the service account associated with the application's instance. You want to follow the Google-recommended best practice of providing minimum access for the role assigned to the service account. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the Project Editor role.
Assign the Project Owner role.
Assign the Cloud SQL Client role.
Assign the Cloud SQL Editor role.

questions.correct_text: Assign the Cloud SQL Client role.
questions.explanation: Following least privilege, the service account only needs to connect through the Cloud SQL Proxy, which the Cloud SQL Client role (roles/cloudsql.client) grants by providing connectivity and instance metadata access required by the proxy. Project Editor (A) and Project Owner (B) are broad, highly privileged roles that violate least privilege by granting far more than database connectivity. The Cloud SQL Editor role (D) allows managing and modifying instances, which exceeds what an application that merely connects to the database requires. Cloud SQL Client is therefore the minimal role appropriate for proxy-based application connections.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Seguindo o princípio do menor privilégio, a conta de serviço só precisa se conectar através do Cloud SQL Proxy, o que o papel Cloud SQL Client (roles/cloudsql.client) concede ao fornecer a conectividade e o acesso aos metadados da instância exigidos pelo proxy. Project Editor (A) e Project Owner (B) são papéis amplos e altamente privilegiados que violam o menor privilégio ao conceder muito mais do que apenas conectividade ao banco de dados. O papel Cloud SQL Editor (D) permite gerenciar e modificar instâncias, o que excede o que uma aplicação que apenas se conecta ao banco de dados requer. O Cloud SQL Client é, portanto, o papel mínimo apropriado para conexões de aplicação baseadas em proxy.

questions.question: Your team develops stateless services that run on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You need to deploy a new service that will only be accessed by other services running in the GKE cluster. The service will need to scale as quickly as possible to respond to changing load. What should you do?

options.text: Use a Vertical Pod Autoscaler to scale the containers, and expose them via a ClusterIP Service.
Use a Vertical Pod Autoscaler to scale the containers, and expose them via a NodePort Service.
Use a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler to scale the containers, and expose them via a ClusterIP Service.
Use a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler to scale the containers, and expose them via a NodePort Service.

questions.correct_text: Use a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler to scale the containers, and expose them via a ClusterIP Service.
questions.explanation: A Horizontal Pod Autoscaler adds or removes pod replicas in response to load, which is the fastest way to scale a stateless service for changing demand. Because the service is only consumed by other workloads inside the cluster, a ClusterIP Service is the correct exposure type, providing an internal-only virtual IP. Vertical Pod Autoscaler (A and B) resizes a pod's CPU/memory and typically restarts pods, making it slow and unsuitable for rapidly responding to load. NodePort (B and D) exposes the service externally on every node, which is unnecessary and less secure for an internal-only service. Thus HPA plus ClusterIP (C) best meets both the scaling and internal-access requirements.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Um Horizontal Pod Autoscaler adiciona ou remove réplicas de pods em resposta à carga, o que é a maneira mais rápida de escalar um serviço stateless para uma demanda variável. Como o serviço é consumido apenas por outras cargas de trabalho dentro do cluster, um Service do tipo ClusterIP é o tipo de exposição correto, fornecendo um IP virtual apenas interno. O Vertical Pod Autoscaler (A e B) redimensiona a CPU/memória de um pod e normalmente reinicia os pods, tornando-o lento e inadequado para responder rapidamente à carga. O NodePort (B e D) expõe o serviço externamente em cada nó, o que é desnecessário e menos seguro para um serviço apenas interno. Portanto, HPA mais ClusterIP (C) atende melhor tanto aos requisitos de escalabilidade quanto aos de acesso interno.

questions.question: You recently migrated a monolithic application to Google Cloud by breaking it down into microservices. One of the microservices is deployed using CloudFunctions. As you modernize the application, you make a change to the API of the service that is backward-incompatible. You need to support both existing callers who use the original API and new callers who use the new API. What should you do?

options.text: Leave the original Cloud Function as-is and deploy a second Cloud Function with the new API. Use a load balancer to distribute calls between the versions.
Leave the original Cloud Function as-is and deploy a second Cloud Function that includes only the changed API. Calls are automatically routed to the correct function.
Leave the original Cloud Function as-is and deploy a second Cloud Function with the new API. Use Cloud Endpoints to provide an API gateway that exposes a versioned API.
Re-deploy the Cloud Function after making code changes to support the new API. Requests for both versions of the API are fulfilled based on a version identifier included in the call.

questions.correct_text: Leave the original Cloud Function as-is and deploy a second Cloud Function with the new API. Use Cloud Endpoints to provide an API gateway that exposes a versioned API.
questions.explanation: Cloud Endpoints acts as an API gateway that can expose a versioned API, routing callers to the appropriate backend based on the version path or configuration. By keeping the original Cloud Function untouched and deploying a second Cloud Function with the new API, both existing and new callers are served through a single managed, versioned endpoint. Option A's load balancer cannot distinguish between API versions based on contract semantics and would split traffic arbitrarily. Option B is wrong because Cloud Functions do not automatically route between versions of an API. Option D forces redeployment and custom in-code version handling, which is fragile and not the recommended pattern for managing backward-incompatible API changes.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Endpoints atua como um API gateway que pode expor uma API versionada, roteando os chamadores para o backend apropriado com base no caminho da versão ou na configuração. Ao manter a Cloud Function original intacta e implantar uma segunda Cloud Function com a nova API, tanto os chamadores existentes quanto os novos são atendidos por meio de um único endpoint gerenciado e versionado. O load balancer da opção A não consegue distinguir entre versões da API com base na semântica do contrato e dividiria o tráfego arbitrariamente. A opção B está errada porque as Cloud Functions não roteiam automaticamente entre versões de uma API. A opção D força uma reimplantação e o tratamento de versão personalizado no código, o que é frágil e não é o padrão recomendado para gerenciar mudanças de API incompatíveis com versões anteriores.

questions.question: You are developing an application that will allow users to read and post comments on news articles. You want to configure your application to store and display user-submitted comments using Firestore. How should you design the schema to support an unknown number of comments and articles?

options.text: Store each comment in a subcollection of the article.
Add each comment to an array property on the article.
Store each comment in a document, and add the comment's key to an array property on the article.
Store each comment in a document, and add the comment's key to an array property on the user profile.

questions.correct_text: Store each comment in a subcollection of the article.
questions.explanation: In Firestore, storing each comment as a document in a subcollection of its article scales to an unbounded number of comments and articles, because subcollections grow independently and queries fetch only the documents needed. Firestore documents have a 1 MiB size limit, so options B and C, which append comments or keys to an array property on the article, would eventually hit that limit and cause write contention on a single document. Option C and D also add unnecessary key-management overhead and extra lookups. Subcollections are the idiomatic Firestore pattern for one-to-many relationships of unknown cardinality.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: No Firestore, armazenar cada comentário como um documento em uma subcoleção de seu artigo escala para um número ilimitado de comentários e artigos, porque as subcoleções crescem de forma independente e as consultas buscam apenas os documentos necessários. Os documentos do Firestore têm um limite de tamanho de 1 MiB, então as opções B e C, que anexam comentários ou chaves a uma propriedade de array no artigo, acabariam atingindo esse limite e causando contenção de escrita em um único documento. As opções C e D também adicionam sobrecarga desnecessária de gerenciamento de chaves e consultas extras. As subcoleções são o padrão idiomático do Firestore para relacionamentos um-para-muitos de cardinalidade desconhecida.

questions.question: You recently developed an application. You need to call the Cloud Storage API from a ComputeEngine instance that doesn't have a public IP address. What should you do?

options.text: Use Carrier Peering
Use VPC Network Peering
Use Shared VPC networks
Use Private Google Access

questions.correct_text: Use Private Google Access
questions.explanation: Private Google Access lets VM instances that have only internal IP addresses reach Google APIs and services, such as the Cloud Storage API, over Google's internal network without requiring external IPs. It is enabled per subnet and is the standard solution for instances without public IP addresses. VPC Network Peering connects two VPC networks together but does not by itself grant access to Google APIs. Shared VPC shares network resources across projects, and Carrier Peering is for on-premises connectivity to Google services; neither directly solves the no-public-IP API access requirement.
