questions.explanation_pt: Habilitar a configuração de Vulnerability scanning (Container Analysis) no Container Registry é um recurso totalmente gerenciado que automaticamente escaneia as imagens enviadas em busca de CVEs em muitos sistemas operacionais open source sem adicionar etapas manuais, então não diminui a agilidade do desenvolvimento. A opção B escaneia o código-fonte no check-in via uma Cloud Function, mas o escaneamento de CVE tem como alvo as camadas do container construído e os pacotes do SO, não o código-fonte bruto, e construir isso não é um serviço gerenciado. A opção C, proibir imagens base sem suporte comercial, restringe a liberdade das equipes de usar sistemas operacionais open source, o que é contrário ao requisito. A opção D, analisar a saída do Cloud Build no Cloud Monitoring, é uma abordagem manual e não confiável que não realiza um escaneamento de vulnerabilidades real das imagens publicadas.

questions.question: You are configuring a continuous integration pipeline using Cloud Build to automate the deployment of new container images to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The pipeline builds the application from its source code, runs unit and integration tests in separate steps, and pushes the container to Container Registry. The application runs on a Python web server.The Dockerfile is as follows:FROM python:3.7-alpine -COPY . /app -WORKDIR /app -RUN pip install -r requirements.txtCMD [ "gunicorn", "-w 4", "main:app" ]You notice that Cloud Build runs are taking longer than expected to complete. You want to decrease the build time. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Select a virtual machine (VM) size with higher CPU for Cloud Build runs.
Deploy a Container Registry on a Compute Engine VM in a VPC, and use it to store the final images.
Cache the Docker image for subsequent builds using the -- cache-from argument in your build config file.
Change the base image in the Dockerfile to ubuntu:latest, and install Python 3.7 using a package manager utility.
Store application source code on Cloud Storage, and configure the pipeline to use gsutil to download the source code.

questions.correct_text: Select a virtual machine (VM) size with higher CPU for Cloud Build runs. | Cache the Docker image for subsequent builds using the -- cache-from argument in your build config file.
questions.explanation: Selecting a higher-CPU machine type for Cloud Build runs (option A) speeds up CPU-bound steps such as pip installs and image builds, and using the --cache-from argument (option C) lets Cloud Build reuse previously built layers so unchanged steps like dependency installation are not repeated, both directly reducing build time. Option B, self-hosting a registry on a Compute Engine VM, adds operational overhead and does not improve build speed compared with the managed registry. Option D, switching to ubuntu:latest, would produce a larger base image and longer builds than the lightweight alpine image, and using a floating latest tag harms reproducibility. Option E, downloading source from Cloud Storage via gsutil, adds an extra transfer step rather than removing one and does not address the build duration.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Selecionar um tipo de máquina com mais CPU para as execuções do Cloud Build (opção A) acelera as etapas limitadas por CPU, como instalações via pip e builds de imagem, e usar o argumento --cache-from (opção C) permite que o Cloud Build reutilize camadas previamente construídas para que etapas inalteradas, como a instalação de dependências, não sejam repetidas, ambos reduzindo diretamente o tempo de build. A opção B, hospedar um registry próprio em uma VM do Compute Engine, adiciona sobrecarga operacional e não melhora a velocidade do build em comparação com o registry gerenciado. A opção D, mudar para ubuntu:latest, produziria uma imagem base maior e builds mais longos do que a imagem leve alpine, e usar uma tag latest móvel prejudica a reprodutibilidade. A opção E, baixar o código-fonte do Cloud Storage via gsutil, adiciona uma etapa extra de transferência em vez de remover uma e não resolve a duração do build.

questions.question: You are building a CI/CD pipeline that consists of a version control system, Cloud Build, and Container Registry. Each time a new tag is pushed to the repository, a Cloud Build job is triggered, which runs unit tests on the new code builds a new Docker container image, and pushes it into Container Registry. The last step of your pipeline should deploy the new container to your production Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You need to select a tool and deployment strategy that meets the following requirements:• Zero downtime is incurred• Testing is fully automated• Allows for testing before being rolled out to users• Can quickly rollback if neededWhat should you do?

options.text: Trigger a Spinnaker pipeline configured as an A/B test of your new code and, if it is successful, deploy the container to production.
Trigger a Spinnaker pipeline configured as a canary test of your new code and, if it is successful, deploy the container to production.
Trigger another Cloud Build job that uses the Kubernetes CLI tools to deploy your new container to your GKE cluster, where you can perform a canary test.
Trigger another Cloud Build job that uses the Kubernetes CLI tools to deploy your new container to your GKE cluster, where you can perform a shadow test.

questions.correct_text: Trigger a Spinnaker pipeline configured as a canary test of your new code and, if it is successful, deploy the container to production.
questions.explanation: A shadow (dark) test deploys the new version alongside production and mirrors real traffic to it without exposing responses to users, allowing fully automated testing under real load with zero downtime and an instant rollback by simply not promoting the version. While canary and shadow both avoid downtime, shadow testing best satisfies testing the new code against live traffic before any user is served by it, with no user-facing risk. Options A and B introduce Spinnaker, which adds an additional tool when the requirement can be met within the existing Cloud Build and GKE pipeline; an A/B test in option A also routes real users to the new version rather than testing before rollout. Option C performs a canary that does expose a subset of real users to the untested code, so it does not test fully before users are affected the way shadow testing does.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Um teste shadow (sombra/dark) implanta a nova versão ao lado da produção e espelha o tráfego real para ela sem expor as respostas aos usuários, permitindo testes totalmente automatizados sob carga real com zero downtime e um rollback instantâneo bastando não promover a versão. Embora canary e shadow evitem o downtime, o teste shadow atende melhor ao requisito de testar o novo código contra o tráfego ao vivo antes que qualquer usuário seja atendido por ele, sem risco voltado ao usuário. As opções A e B introduzem o Spinnaker, que adiciona uma ferramenta extra quando o requisito pode ser atendido dentro do pipeline existente de Cloud Build e GKE; o teste A/B na opção A também direciona usuários reais para a nova versão em vez de testar antes do rollout. A opção C executa um canary que de fato expõe um subconjunto de usuários reais ao código não testado, portanto não testa totalmente antes de afetar usuários da forma que o teste shadow faz.

questions.question: Your operations team has asked you to create a script that lists the Cloud Bigtable, Memorystore, and Cloud SQL databases running within a project. The script should allow users to submit a filter expression to limit the results presented. How should you retrieve the data?

options.text: Use the HBase API, Redis API, and MySQL connection to retrieve database lists. Combine the results, and then apply the filter to display the results
Use the HBase API, Redis API, and MySQL connection to retrieve database lists. Filter the results individually, and then combine them to display the results
Run gcloud bigtable instances list, gcloud redis instances list, and gcloud sql databases list. Use a filter within the application, and then display the results
Run gcloud bigtable instances list, gcloud redis instances list, and gcloud sql databases list. Use --filter flag with each command, and then display the results

questions.correct_text: Run gcloud bigtable instances list, gcloud redis instances list, and gcloud sql databases list. Use --filter flag with each command, and then display the results
questions.explanation: The gcloud CLI provides list commands for each service (gcloud bigtable instances list, gcloud redis instances list, gcloud sql databases list), and every gcloud list command supports a server-side or client-side --filter flag that limits results based on a filter expression. Applying --filter directly to each command (option D) lets the operations team pass a filter expression as intended and is the cleanest, most efficient approach. Option C filters inside the application instead of leveraging the built-in --filter flag, adding unnecessary code. Options A and B propose using raw HBase, Redis, and MySQL data-plane APIs, which connect to the databases themselves to read data rather than enumerating the managed instances, so they cannot list the GCP resources and are far more complex.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: A CLI gcloud fornece comandos de listagem para cada serviço (gcloud bigtable instances list, gcloud redis instances list, gcloud sql databases list), e todo comando list do gcloud suporta uma flag --filter (do lado do servidor ou do cliente) que limita os resultados com base em uma expressão de filtro. Aplicar --filter diretamente a cada comando (opção D) permite que a equipe de operações passe uma expressão de filtro conforme pretendido, sendo a abordagem mais limpa e eficiente. A opção C filtra dentro da aplicação em vez de aproveitar a flag --filter embutida, adicionando código desnecessário. As opções A e B propõem usar as APIs brutas do plano de dados do HBase, Redis e MySQL, que se conectam aos próprios bancos de dados para ler dados em vez de enumerar as instâncias gerenciadas, portanto não conseguem listar os recursos do GCP e são muito mais complexas.

questions.question: You need to deploy a new European version of a website hosted on Google Kubernetes Engine. The current and new websites must be accessed via the same HTTP(S) load balancer's external IP address, but have different domain names. What should you do?

options.text: Define a new Ingress resource with a host rule matching the new domain
Modify the existing Ingress resource with a host rule matching the new domain
Create a new Service of type LoadBalancer specifying the existing IP address as the loadBalancerIP
Generate a new Ingress resource and specify the existing IP address as the kubernetes.io/ingress.global-static-ip-name annotation value

questions.correct_text: Modify the existing Ingress resource with a host rule matching the new domain
questions.explanation: A single GKE Ingress resource maps to one external HTTP(S) load balancer with one external IP, and it can route to multiple backends using host rules. To serve both the existing and new European site on the same load balancer IP but with different domain names, you simply add a new host rule to the existing Ingress (option B), creating host-based routing on the shared load balancer. Defining a brand-new Ingress (options A and D) would provision a separate load balancer with a different IP, defeating the requirement to reuse the same external IP. Option C uses a Service of type LoadBalancer, which creates an L4 (TCP/UDP) load balancer that does not support HTTP host-based routing.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Um único recurso Ingress do GKE mapeia para um external HTTP(S) load balancer com um IP externo, e ele pode rotear para múltiplos backends usando regras de host. Para servir tanto o site europeu existente quanto o novo no mesmo IP do load balancer, mas com nomes de domínio diferentes, basta adicionar uma nova regra de host ao Ingress existente (opção B), criando roteamento baseado em host no load balancer compartilhado. Definir um Ingress totalmente novo (opções A e D) provisionaria um load balancer separado com um IP diferente, indo contra o requisito de reutilizar o mesmo IP externo. A opção C usa um Service do tipo LoadBalancer, que cria um load balancer L4 (TCP/UDP) que não suporta roteamento HTTP baseado em host.

questions.question: You are developing a single-player mobile game backend that has unpredictable traffic patterns as users interact with the game throughout the day and night. You want to optimize costs by ensuring that you have enough resources to handle requests, but minimize over-provisioning. You also want the system to handle traffic spikes efficiently. Which compute platform should you use?

options.text: Cloud Run
Compute Engine with managed instance groups
Compute Engine with unmanaged instance groups
Google Kubernetes Engine using cluster autoscaling

questions.correct_text: Cloud Run
questions.explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform that scales request-driven, stateless workloads automatically from zero up to many instances based on incoming traffic, billing only for actual usage. This makes it ideal for unpredictable traffic with day/night spikes because it minimizes over-provisioning while still absorbing bursts, exactly matching the cost-optimization goal. Compute Engine managed instance groups (B) and GKE cluster autoscaling (D) can autoscale but cannot scale to zero and add VM/cluster management overhead, leaving idle resources during quiet periods. Unmanaged instance groups (C) do not autoscale at all and require manual capacity management.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Run é uma plataforma serverless totalmente gerenciada que escala automaticamente cargas de trabalho stateless e orientadas a requisições, de zero até muitas instâncias com base no tráfego de entrada, cobrando apenas pelo uso real. Isso o torna ideal para tráfego imprevisível com picos diurnos/noturnos porque minimiza o superprovisionamento e ainda assim absorve rajadas, atendendo exatamente ao objetivo de otimização de custos. Os managed instance groups do Compute Engine (B) e o autoscaling de cluster do GKE (D) conseguem fazer autoscaling, mas não conseguem escalar até zero e adicionam sobrecarga de gerenciamento de VMs/cluster, deixando recursos ociosos durante períodos de baixa atividade. Os unmanaged instance groups (C) não fazem autoscaling de forma alguma e exigem gerenciamento manual de capacidade.

questions.question: The development teams in your company want to manage resources from their local environments. You have been asked to enable developer access to each team’s Google Cloud projects. You want to maximize efficiency while following Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Add the users to their projects, assign the relevant roles to the users, and then provide the users with each relevant Project ID.
Add the users to their projects, assign the relevant roles to the users, and then provide the users with each relevant Project Number.
Create groups, add the users to their groups, assign the relevant roles to the groups, and then provide the users with each relevant Project ID.
Create groups, add the users to their groups, assign the relevant roles to the groups, and then provide the users with each relevant Project Number.

questions.correct_text: Create groups, add the users to their groups, assign the relevant roles to the groups, and then provide the users with each relevant Project ID.
questions.explanation: Google's IAM best practice is to assign roles to Google Groups rather than to individual users, because managing access through groups scales better, reduces per-user maintenance, and centralizes membership changes. So creating groups, adding users to them, and binding roles to the groups (options C and D) is correct over per-user grants (A and B). Between C and D, developers using gcloud and client tools reference projects by their human-readable, globally unique Project ID, not the numeric Project Number, so option C is correct. The Project Number is an internal identifier and is not what developers normally use to target a project.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: A boa prática de IAM do Google é atribuir papéis a Google Groups em vez de a usuários individuais, porque gerenciar o acesso por meio de grupos escala melhor, reduz a manutenção por usuário e centraliza as mudanças de associação. Portanto, criar grupos, adicionar usuários a eles e vincular papéis aos grupos (opções C e D) é mais correto do que concessões por usuário (A e B). Entre C e D, desenvolvedores que usam o gcloud e ferramentas de cliente referenciam projetos pelo seu Project ID, legível por humanos e globalmente único, e não pelo Project Number numérico, portanto a opção C é a correta. O Project Number é um identificador interno e não é o que os desenvolvedores normalmente usam para apontar para um projeto.

questions.question: Your company’s product team has a new requirement based on customer demand to autoscale your stateless and distributed service running in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) duster. You want to find a solution that minimizes changes because this feature will go live in two weeks. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Vertical Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on the CPU load.
Deploy a Vertical Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on a custom metric.
Deploy a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on the CPU toad.
Deploy a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on a custom metric.

questions.correct_text: Deploy a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on the CPU toad.
questions.explanation: For a stateless, distributed service that needs to scale out to handle more traffic, the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) is the right tool because it adds or removes pod replicas, which is the natural scaling model for distributed stateless workloads. Scaling on CPU load (option C) requires no extra instrumentation since CPU is a built-in resource metric, minimizing changes ahead of a two-week deadline; a custom metric (D) would require setting up and exporting metrics, adding work. A Vertical Pod Autoscaler (A and B) resizes a single pod's CPU/memory requests rather than adding replicas, often restarting pods, and does not horizontally scale a distributed service to absorb increased traffic.

questions.explanation_pt: Para um serviço sem estado e distribuído que precisa escalar horizontalmente para lidar com mais tráfego, o Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) é a ferramenta certa porque adiciona ou remove réplicas de pods, que é o modelo de escalonamento natural para cargas de trabalho distribuídas sem estado. Escalar com base na carga de CPU (opção C) não requer instrumentação extra, já que a CPU é uma métrica de recurso integrada, minimizando as mudanças antes de um prazo de duas semanas; uma métrica personalizada (D) exigiria configurar e exportar métricas, adicionando trabalho. Um Vertical Pod Autoscaler (A e B) redimensiona as solicitações de CPU/memória de um único pod em vez de adicionar réplicas, frequentemente reiniciando os pods, e não escala horizontalmente um serviço distribuído para absorver o aumento de tráfego.

questions.question: Your application is composed of a set of loosely coupled services orchestrated by code executed on Compute Engine. You want your application to easily bring up new Compute Engine instances that find and use a specific version of a service. How should this be configured?

options.text: Define your service endpoint information as metadata that is retrieved at runtime and used to connect to the desired service.
Define your service endpoint information as label data that is retrieved at runtime and used to connect to the desired service.
Define your service endpoint information to be retrieved from an environment variable at runtime and used to connect to the desired service.
Define your service to use a fixed hostname and port to connect to the desired service. Replace the service at the endpoint with your new version.

questions.correct_text: Define your service endpoint information as metadata that is retrieved at runtime and used to connect to the desired service.
questions.explanation: Compute Engine instance metadata is designed to store configuration that instances can query at runtime via the metadata server, making it ideal for passing service endpoint information (such as a specific service version's address) to newly created instances without rebuilding images or hardcoding values. New instances can read this metadata at boot to discover and connect to the desired service version dynamically. Labels (B) are organizational key-value tags used for filtering and billing, not for runtime configuration lookups by the instance itself. Environment variables (C) are static and typically baked in, requiring redeployment to change. A fixed hostname/port (D) defeats the goal of easily targeting a specific version and forces in-place replacement rather than flexible service discovery.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Os metadados de instância do Compute Engine são projetados para armazenar configurações que as instâncias podem consultar em tempo de execução por meio do servidor de metadados, tornando-os ideais para passar informações de endpoint de serviço (como o endereço de uma versão específica de um serviço) para instâncias recém-criadas sem reconstruir imagens ou codificar valores fixos. Novas instâncias podem ler esses metadados na inicialização para descobrir e conectar-se dinamicamente à versão de serviço desejada. Labels (B) são tags de chave-valor organizacionais usadas para filtragem e faturamento, não para consultas de configuração em tempo de execução pela própria instância. Variáveis de ambiente (C) são estáticas e normalmente incorporadas, exigindo nova implantação para serem alteradas. Um hostname/porta fixos (D) frustram o objetivo de direcionar facilmente uma versão específica e forçam a substituição no local em vez de uma descoberta de serviços flexível.

questions.question: You are developing a microservice-based application that will run on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Some of the services need to access different Google Cloud APIs. How should you set up authentication of these services in the cluster following Google-recommended best practices? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the service account attached to the GKE node.
Enable Workload Identity in the cluster via the gcloud command-line tool.
Access the Google service account keys from a secret management service.
Store the Google service account keys in a central secret management service.
Use gcloud to bind the Kubernetes service account and the Google service account using roles/iam.workloadIdentity.

questions.correct_text: Enable Workload Identity in the cluster via the gcloud command-line tool. | Use gcloud to bind the Kubernetes service account and the Google service account using roles/iam.workloadIdentity.
questions.explanation: The Google-recommended best practice for GKE workloads to access Google Cloud APIs is Workload Identity, which lets a Kubernetes service account impersonate a Google service account without managing exportable key files. You enable Workload Identity on the cluster (B) and then bind the Kubernetes service account to the Google service account by granting roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser (E), allowing pods to obtain short-lived credentials automatically. Using the node's service account (A) is discouraged because it grants the same permissions to every pod on the node, violating least privilege. Storing or accessing exported service account key files (C and D) is explicitly discouraged because long-lived keys are a security liability and Workload Identity removes the need for them.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: A prática recomendada pelo Google para que as cargas de trabalho do GKE acessem as APIs do Google Cloud é o Workload Identity, que permite que uma conta de serviço do Kubernetes personifique uma conta de serviço do Google sem gerenciar arquivos de chave exportáveis. Você habilita o Workload Identity no cluster (B) e então vincula a conta de serviço do Kubernetes à conta de serviço do Google concedendo roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser (E), permitindo que os pods obtenham credenciais de curta duração automaticamente. Usar a conta de serviço do nó (A) é desencorajado porque concede as mesmas permissões a todos os pods no nó, violando o princípio de menor privilégio. Armazenar ou acessar arquivos de chave de conta de serviço exportados (C e D) é explicitamente desencorajado porque chaves de longa duração são um risco de segurança e o Workload Identity elimina a necessidade delas.

questions.question: Your development team has been tasked with maintaining a .NET legacy application. The application incurs occasional changes and was recently updated. Your goal is to ensure that the application provides consistent results while moving through the CI/CD pipeline from environment to environment. You want to minimize the cost of deployment while making sure that external factors and dependencies between hosting environments are not problematic. Containers are not yet approved in your organization. What should you do?

options.text: Rewrite the application using .NET Core, and deploy to Cloud Run. Use revisions to separate the environments.
Use Cloud Build to deploy the application as a new Compute Engine image for each build. Use this image in each environment.
Deploy the application using MS Web Deploy, and make sure to always use the latest, patched MS Windows Server base image in Compute Engine.
Use Cloud Build to package the application, and deploy to a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. Use namespaces to separate the environments.

questions.correct_text: Use Cloud Build to deploy the application as a new Compute Engine image for each build. Use this image in each environment.
questions.explanation: Because containers are not approved and the goal is consistent, environment-independent results at minimal cost, baking the .NET application into an immutable Compute Engine image with Cloud Build and promoting that same image unchanged through every environment is the best fit. Immutable images guarantee identical binaries and dependencies across dev, staging, and production, eliminating drift from external host factors. Rewriting to .NET Core for Cloud Run (A) and deploying to GKE with namespaces (D) both require containers, which are prohibited. Using MS Web Deploy onto the latest patched base image (C) reintroduces inconsistency because the underlying OS and dependencies can differ between deployments, undermining reproducibility.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Como os contêineres não são aprovados e o objetivo é obter resultados consistentes e independentes do ambiente ao custo mínimo, incorporar a aplicação .NET em uma imagem imutável do Compute Engine com o Cloud Build e promover essa mesma imagem sem alterações por todos os ambientes é a melhor opção. Imagens imutáveis garantem binários e dependências idênticos em dev, staging e produção, eliminando o desvio causado por fatores externos do host. Reescrever para .NET Core para o Cloud Run (A) e implantar no GKE com namespaces (D) ambos exigem contêineres, que são proibidos. Usar o MS Web Deploy na imagem base mais recente e corrigida (C) reintroduz inconsistência porque o sistema operacional subjacente e as dependências podem diferir entre as implantações, comprometendo a reprodutibilidade.

questions.question: The new version of your containerized application has been tested and is ready to deploy to production on Google Kubernetes Engine. You were not able to fully load-test the new version in pre-production environments, and you need to make sure that it does not have performance problems once deployed. Your deployment must be automated. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Load Balancing to slowly ramp up traffic between versions. Use Cloud Monitoring to look for performance issues.
Deploy the application via a continuous delivery pipeline using canary deployments. Use Cloud Monitoring to look for performance issues. and ramp up traffic as the metrics support it.
Deploy the application via a continuous delivery pipeline using blue/green deployments. Use Cloud Monitoring to look for performance issues, and launch fully when the metrics support it.

Deploy the application using kubectl and set the spec.updateStrategv.type to RollingUpdate. Use Cloud Monitoring to look for performance issues, and run the kubectl rollback command if there are any issues.

questions.correct_text: Deploy the application via a continuous delivery pipeline using canary deployments. Use Cloud Monitoring to look for performance issues. and ramp up traffic as the metrics support it.
questions.explanation: A canary deployment in an automated continuous delivery pipeline routes a small percentage of real production traffic to the new version while monitoring performance, then gradually increases traffic only if metrics remain healthy, which directly addresses the inability to load-test in pre-production. Cloud Monitoring provides the observability to detect performance regressions before full rollout. Blue/green deployment (C) switches all traffic at once after validation, exposing every user to performance issues simultaneously rather than limiting blast radius. A simple Cloud Load Balancing ramp (A) lacks the integrated automated pipeline and progressive rollout control. A RollingUpdate with manual kubectl rollback (D) is not a true canary and relies on reactive manual intervention instead of metric-driven progressive delivery.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Uma implantação canary em um pipeline automatizado de entrega contínua roteia uma pequena porcentagem do tráfego real de produção para a nova versão enquanto monitora o desempenho, depois aumenta gradualmente o tráfego apenas se as métricas permanecerem saudáveis, o que aborda diretamente a impossibilidade de fazer testes de carga em pré-produção. O Cloud Monitoring fornece a observabilidade para detectar regressões de desempenho antes do lançamento completo. A implantação blue/green (C) alterna todo o tráfego de uma vez após a validação, expondo todos os usuários a problemas de desempenho simultaneamente em vez de limitar o raio de impacto. Um simples aumento gradual via Cloud Load Balancing (A) carece do pipeline automatizado integrado e do controle de lançamento progressivo. Um RollingUpdate com rollback manual via kubectl (D) não é um verdadeiro canary e depende de intervenção manual reativa em vez de entrega progressiva orientada por métricas.

questions.question: Users are complaining that your Cloud Run-hosted website responds too slowly during traffic spikes. You want to provide a better user experience during traffic peaks. What should you do?

options.text: Read application configuration and static data from the database on application startup.
Package application configuration and static data into the application image during build time.
Perform as much work as possible in the background after the response has been returned to the user.
Ensure that timeout exceptions and errors cause the Cloud Run instance to exit quickly so a replacement instance can be started.

questions.correct_text: Package application configuration and static data into the application image during build time.
questions.explanation: Cloud Run scales by starting new instances during traffic spikes, so slow responses at peak usually stem from long cold-start times; packaging configuration and static data into the container image at build time minimizes startup work so new instances become ready quickly. Reading configuration and static data from a database at startup (A) increases cold-start latency and adds dependency load precisely when many instances start at once. Deferring work to the background after responding (C) is unreliable on Cloud Run because CPU is throttled outside of request processing unless CPU-always-on is configured, so background work may stall. Forcing instances to exit on errors (D) worsens availability and causes more cold starts rather than improving peak responsiveness.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Run escala iniciando novas instâncias durante picos de tráfego, então respostas lentas no horário de pico geralmente decorrem de longos tempos de cold-start; empacotar a configuração e os dados estáticos na imagem do contêiner no momento do build minimiza o trabalho de inicialização, de modo que novas instâncias fiquem prontas rapidamente. Ler configuração e dados estáticos de um banco de dados na inicialização (A) aumenta a latência do cold-start e adiciona carga de dependência justamente quando muitas instâncias iniciam ao mesmo tempo. Adiar trabalho para segundo plano após responder (C) é pouco confiável no Cloud Run porque a CPU é limitada (throttled) fora do processamento de requisições, a menos que o CPU-always-on esteja configurado, então o trabalho em segundo plano pode travar. Forçar as instâncias a encerrar em caso de erro (D) piora a disponibilidade e causa mais cold-starts, em vez de melhorar a responsividade no pico.

questions.question: You are a developer working on an internal application for payroll processing. You are building a component of the application that allows an employee to submit a timesheet, which then initiates several steps:• An email is sent to the employee and manager, notifying them that the timesheet was submitted.• A timesheet is sent to payroll processing for the vendor's API.• A timesheet is sent to the data warehouse for headcount planning.These steps are not dependent on each other and can be completed in any order. New steps are being considered and will be implemented by different development teams. Each development team will implement the error handling specific to their step. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Cloud Function for each step that calls the corresponding downstream system to complete the required action.
Create a Pub/Sub topic for each step. Create a subscription for each downstream development team to subscribe to their step's topic.
Create a Pub/Sub topic for timesheet submissions. Create a subscription for each downstream development team to subscribe to the topic.
Create a timesheet microservice deployed to Google Kubernetes Engine. The microservice calls each downstream step and waits for a successful response before calling the next step.

questions.correct_text: Create a Pub/Sub topic for timesheet submissions. Create a subscription for each downstream development team to subscribe to the topic.
questions.explanation: Because the downstream steps are independent, can run in any order, and new steps will be added by different teams, a publish/subscribe fan-out pattern is ideal. A single Pub/Sub topic for timesheet submissions lets each team create its own subscription and implement its own error handling and retry/dead-letter behavior, and new teams can simply add a subscription without changing the publisher. Option B (a topic per step) couples the publisher to every step and forces it to know and publish to each one, defeating the decoupling and making new steps harder to add. Option A (a Cloud Function per step) still requires something to invoke each function and tightly couples the orchestration. Option D builds a synchronous, sequential microservice that waits for each step, which contradicts the requirement that steps are independent and order-agnostic and creates a single point of failure.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Como as etapas seguintes são independentes, podem rodar em qualquer ordem e novas etapas serão adicionadas por equipes diferentes, um padrão de fan-out publish/subscribe é ideal. Um único tópico do Pub/Sub para submissões de timesheet permite que cada equipe crie sua própria subscription e implemente seu próprio tratamento de erros e comportamento de retry/dead-letter, e novas equipes podem simplesmente adicionar uma subscription sem alterar o publisher. A opção B (um tópico por etapa) acopla o publisher a todas as etapas e o força a conhecer e publicar em cada uma, anulando o desacoplamento e tornando mais difícil adicionar novas etapas. A opção A (uma Cloud Function por etapa) ainda exige algo que invoque cada função e acopla fortemente a orquestração. A opção D constrói um microsserviço síncrono e sequencial que aguarda cada etapa, o que contraria o requisito de que as etapas sejam independentes e indiferentes à ordem, além de criar um ponto único de falha.

questions.question: You are designing an application that uses a microservices architecture. You are planning to deploy the application in the cloud and on-premises. You want to make sure the application can scale up on demand and also use managed services as much as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy open source Istio in a multi-cluster deployment on multiple Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters managed by Anthos.
Create a GKE cluster in each environment with Anthos, and use Cloud Run for Anthos to deploy your application to each cluster.
Install a GKE cluster in each environment with Anthos, and use Cloud Build to create a Deployment for your application in each cluster.
Create a GKE cluster in the cloud and install open-source Kubernetes on-premises. Use an external load balancer service to distribute traffic across the two environments.

questions.correct_text: Create a GKE cluster in each environment with Anthos, and use Cloud Run for Anthos to deploy your application to each cluster.
questions.explanation: The requirements are a microservices app that runs both in the cloud and on-premises, scales on demand, and uses managed services as much as possible. Creating a GKE cluster in each environment with Anthos and using Cloud Run for Anthos (Cloud Service Mesh / serverless on Anthos) provides a consistent, managed serverless platform that autoscales across hybrid environments. Option A (open-source Istio managed manually) increases operational burden rather than using managed services. Option C uses Cloud Build only to create Deployments and does not provide the on-demand serverless scaling and managed experience that Cloud Run for Anthos offers. Option D mixes open-source Kubernetes on-prem with a manual external load balancer, which is the least managed and most operationally complex option.

questions.explanation_pt: Os requisitos são um app de microsserviços que roda tanto na nuvem quanto on-premises, escala sob demanda e usa serviços gerenciados o máximo possível. Criar um cluster GKE em cada ambiente com o Anthos e usar o Cloud Run for Anthos (Cloud Service Mesh / serverless no Anthos) fornece uma plataforma serverless gerenciada e consistente que faz autoscaling em ambientes híbridos. A opção A (Istio open-source gerenciado manualmente) aumenta o esforço operacional em vez de usar serviços gerenciados. A opção C usa o Cloud Build apenas para criar Deployments e não fornece o escalonamento serverless sob demanda nem a experiência gerenciada que o Cloud Run for Anthos oferece. A opção D mistura Kubernetes open-source on-prem com um load balancer externo manual, o que é a opção menos gerenciada e operacionalmente mais complexa.

questions.question: You want to migrate an on-premises container running in Knative to Google Cloud. You need to make sure that the migration doesn't affect your application's deployment strategy, and you want to use a fully managed service. Which Google Cloud service should you use to deploy your container?

options.text: Cloud Run
Compute Engine
Google Kubernetes Engine
App Engine flexible environment

questions.correct_text: Cloud Run
questions.explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform built on the Knative API and serving model, so migrating a Knative container to Cloud Run preserves the existing deployment strategy with minimal change. Compute Engine would require you to run and manage VMs and a container runtime yourself, and it is not Knative-based. GKE can run Knative (via Cloud Run for Anthos) but the standard cluster is not fully managed in the serverless sense and requires cluster management. App Engine flexible environment is not Knative-compatible and would change the deployment model. Therefore Cloud Run is the correct fully managed, Knative-compatible choice.

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Run é uma plataforma serverless totalmente gerenciada construída sobre a API e o modelo de serving do Knative, então migrar um contêiner Knative para o Cloud Run preserva a estratégia de implantação existente com mínima mudança. O Compute Engine exigiria que você executasse e gerenciasse VMs e um runtime de contêiner por conta própria, e não é baseado em Knative. O GKE pode rodar Knative (via Cloud Run for Anthos), mas o cluster padrão não é totalmente gerenciado no sentido serverless e requer gerenciamento de cluster. O ambiente flexível do App Engine não é compatível com Knative e mudaria o modelo de implantação. Portanto, o Cloud Run é a escolha correta, totalmente gerenciada e compatível com Knative.

questions.question: This architectural diagram depicts a system that streams data from thousands of devices. You want to ingest data into a pipeline, store the data, and analyze the data using SQL statements. Which Google Cloud services should you use for steps 1, 2, 3, and 4?

options.text: 1. App Engine2. Pub/Sub3. BigQuery4. Firestore
1. Dataflow2. Pub/Sub3. Firestore4. BigQuery
1. Pub/Sub2. Dataflow3. BigQuery4. Firestore
1. Pub/Sub2. Dataflow3. Firestore4. BigQuery

questions.correct_text: 1. Pub/Sub2. Dataflow3. Firestore4. BigQuery
questions.explanation: For a streaming IoT pipeline you ingest with Pub/Sub (step 1), process/transform the stream with Dataflow (step 2), then must choose between Firestore and BigQuery for storage and analysis. Because the requirement is to analyze data using SQL statements, the analytical store must be BigQuery, so the correct mapping is Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Firestore, BigQuery (option D). Option C reverses the last two services, placing BigQuery before Firestore and putting Firestore as the final SQL analytics store, which is wrong since Firestore is a NoSQL document database not suited for ad hoc SQL analytics. Options A and B incorrectly use App Engine or Dataflow as the ingestion entry point instead of Pub/Sub, which is the standard managed ingestion service for device telemetry.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para um pipeline de IoT em streaming, você faz a ingestão com o Pub/Sub (etapa 1), processa/transforma o stream com o Dataflow (etapa 2) e então precisa escolher entre Firestore e BigQuery para armazenamento e análise. Como o requisito é analisar os dados usando comandos SQL, o repositório analítico deve ser o BigQuery, então o mapeamento correto é Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Firestore, BigQuery (opção D). A opção C inverte os dois últimos serviços, colocando o BigQuery antes do Firestore e deixando o Firestore como o repositório final de análise SQL, o que é incorreto, já que o Firestore é um banco de dados de documentos NoSQL não adequado para análises SQL ad hoc. As opções A e B usam incorretamente o App Engine ou o Dataflow como ponto de entrada da ingestão em vez do Pub/Sub, que é o serviço de ingestão gerenciado padrão para telemetria de dispositivos.

questions.question: Your company just experienced a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) API outage due to a zone failure. You want to deploy a highly available GKE architecture that minimizes service interruption to users in the event of a future zone failure. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy Zonal clusters
Deploy Regional clusters
Deploy Multi-Zone clusters
Deploy GKE on-premises clusters

questions.correct_text: Deploy Regional clusters
questions.explanation: Regional GKE clusters replicate the control plane and node pools across multiple zones within a region, so a single zone failure does not take down the cluster API or all workloads, providing the high availability needed to survive a future zone outage. Zonal clusters run the control plane in a single zone, which is exactly what failed, so they offer no protection. Multi-zone clusters spread worker nodes across zones but keep a single-zone control plane, meaning a zone failure can still cause an API/control-plane outage like the one experienced. Deploying GKE on-premises does not address zone-level resilience in Google Cloud and adds operational overhead. Therefore regional clusters are the correct choice.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Clusters GKE regionais replicam o control plane e os node pools em múltiplas zonas dentro de uma região, de modo que a falha de uma única zona não derruba a API do cluster nem todas as cargas de trabalho, fornecendo a alta disponibilidade necessária para sobreviver a uma futura interrupção de zona. Clusters zonais executam o control plane em uma única zona, que é exatamente o que falhou, então não oferecem proteção. Clusters multizonais distribuem os nós de trabalho entre zonas, mas mantêm o control plane em uma única zona, o que significa que a falha de uma zona ainda pode causar uma interrupção da API/control plane como a que ocorreu. Implantar o GKE on-premises não resolve a resiliência em nível de zona no Google Cloud e adiciona sobrecarga operacional. Portanto, os clusters regionais são a escolha correta.

questions.question: Your team develops services that run on Google Cloud. You want to process messages sent to a Pub/Sub topic, and then store them. Each message must be processed exactly once to avoid duplication of data and any data conflicts. You need to use the cheapest and most simple solution. What should you do?

options.text: Process the messages with a Dataproc job, and write the output to storage.
Process the messages with a Dataflow streaming pipeline using Apache Beam's PubSubIO package, and write the output to storage.
Process the messages with a Cloud Function, and write the results to a BigQuery location where you can run a job to deduplicate the data.
Retrieve the messages with a Dataflow streaming pipeline, store them in Cloud Bigtable, and use another Dataflow streaming pipeline to deduplicate messages.

questions.correct_text: Process the messages with a Dataflow streaming pipeline using Apache Beam's PubSubIO package, and write the output to storage.
questions.explanation: Dataflow with Apache Beam's PubSubIO is the simplest and most cost-effective managed solution that provides exactly-once processing semantics for Pub/Sub streams. Beam's PubSubIO deduplicates messages based on message IDs (or a custom attribute), so each message is processed exactly once and written to storage without duplicates, all within a single managed pipeline. Option A (Dataproc) requires managing a cluster and does not natively guarantee exactly-once Pub/Sub processing, making it more complex and costly. Option C relies on post-hoc BigQuery deduplication jobs, which adds extra processing and cost rather than guaranteeing exactly-once at ingestion. Option D uses two Dataflow pipelines plus Bigtable, which is far more complex and expensive than a single deduplicating pipeline.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Dataflow com o PubSubIO do Apache Beam é a solução gerenciada mais simples e econômica que fornece semântica de processamento exactly-once para streams do Pub/Sub. O PubSubIO do Beam deduplica mensagens com base nos IDs de mensagem (ou em um atributo personalizado), de modo que cada mensagem é processada exatamente uma vez e gravada no armazenamento sem duplicatas, tudo dentro de um único pipeline gerenciado. A opção A (Dataproc) exige o gerenciamento de um cluster e não garante nativamente o processamento exactly-once do Pub/Sub, tornando-a mais complexa e custosa. A opção C depende de jobs de deduplicação posteriores no BigQuery, o que adiciona processamento e custo extras em vez de garantir exactly-once na ingestão. A opção D usa dois pipelines do Dataflow mais o Bigtable, o que é muito mais complexo e caro do que um único pipeline com deduplicação.

questions.question: You are running a containerized application on Google Kubernetes Engine. Your container images are stored in Container Registry. Your team uses CI/CD practices. You need to prevent the deployment of containers with known critical vulnerabilities. What should you do?

options.text: • Use Web Security Scanner to automatically crawl your application• Review your application logs for scan results, and provide an attestation that the container is free of known critical vulnerabilities• Use Binary Authorization to implement a policy that forces the attestation to be provided before the container is deployed

• Use Web Security Scanner to automatically crawl your application• Review the scan results in the scan details page in the Cloud Console, and provide an attestation that the container is free of known critical vulnerabilities• Use Binary Authorization to implement a policy that forces the attestation to be provided before the container is deployed

• Enable the Container Scanning API to perform vulnerability scanning• Review vulnerability reporting in Container Registry in the Cloud Console, and provide an attestation that the container is free of known critical vulnerabilities• Use Binary Authorization to implement a policy that forces the attestation to be provided before the container is deployed

• Enable the Container Scanning API to perform vulnerability scanning• Programmatically review vulnerability reporting through the Container Scanning API, and provide an attestation that the container is free of known critical vulnerabilities• Use Binary Authorization to implement a policy that forces the attestation to be provided before the container is deployed

questions.correct_text: • Enable the Container Scanning API to perform vulnerability scanning• Programmatically review vulnerability reporting through the Container Scanning API, and provide an attestation that the container is free of known critical vulnerabilities• Use Binary Authorization to implement a policy that forces the attestation to be provided before the container is deployed
questions.explanation: To block deployment of containers with known critical vulnerabilities in a CI/CD pipeline, you enable the Container Scanning API (Container Analysis) to scan images stored in Container Registry, then programmatically read the vulnerability findings through the API so the pipeline can automatically decide whether to issue an attestation, and enforce that attestation with Binary Authorization before deployment. Programmatic review (D) is correct because it fits an automated CI/CD workflow, unlike manual console review in option C which does not scale and breaks automation. Options A and B use Web Security Scanner, which is designed to crawl running web applications for runtime vulnerabilities, not to scan container images for known CVEs, so they do not address the requirement.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Para bloquear a implantação de containers com vulnerabilidades críticas conhecidas em um pipeline de CI/CD, você habilita a Container Scanning API (Container Analysis) para escanear imagens armazenadas no Container Registry, depois lê programaticamente os resultados das vulnerabilidades por meio da API para que o pipeline possa decidir automaticamente se emite uma attestation, e impõe essa attestation com o Binary Authorization antes da implantação. A análise programática (D) é correta porque se encaixa em um fluxo de trabalho automatizado de CI/CD, ao contrário da revisão manual no console na opção C, que não escala e quebra a automação. As opções A e B usam o Web Security Scanner, que foi projetado para rastrear aplicações web em execução em busca de vulnerabilidades em tempo de execução, e não para escanear imagens de container em busca de CVEs conhecidos, portanto não atendem ao requisito.

questions.question: You have an on-premises application that authenticates to the Cloud Storage API using a user-managed service account with a user-managed key. The application connects to Cloud Storage using Private Google Access over a Dedicated Interconnect link. You discover that requests from the application to access objects in the Cloud Storage bucket are failing with a 403 Permission Denied error code. What is the likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The folder structure inside the bucket and object paths have changed.
The permissions of the service account’s predefined role have changed.
The service account key has been rotated but not updated on the application server.
The Interconnect link from the on-premises data center to Google Cloud is experiencing a temporary outage.

questions.correct_text: The permissions of the service account’s predefined role have changed.
questions.explanation: A 403 Permission Denied indicates a successful, authenticated connection that was rejected due to insufficient authorization, which points to changed IAM permissions on the service account's role. If the service account's predefined role no longer grants the necessary storage object permissions, requests will be authorized-but-denied with a 403. Option C (rotated key not updated) would typically produce a 401 Unauthorized or authentication failure rather than a 403. Option D (Interconnect outage) would cause network connectivity or timeout errors, not a clean 403 response from the API. Option A (changed folder/object paths) would result in a 404 Not Found, not a permission error.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Um 403 Permission Denied indica uma conexão bem-sucedida e autenticada que foi rejeitada por autorização insuficiente, o que aponta para alterações nas permissões IAM no papel da service account. Se o papel predefinido da service account não conceder mais as permissões necessárias de objetos do storage, as requisições serão autorizadas-mas-negadas com um 403. A opção C (chave rotacionada não atualizada) normalmente produziria um 401 Unauthorized ou uma falha de autenticação, e não um 403. A opção D (interrupção do Interconnect) causaria erros de conectividade de rede ou timeout, e não uma resposta 403 limpa da API. A opção A (alteração de caminhos de pasta/objeto) resultaria em um 404 Not Found, e não em um erro de permissão.

questions.question: You are using the Cloud Client Library to upload an image in your application to Cloud Storage. Users of the application report that occasionally the upload does not complete and the client library reports an HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout error. You want to make the application more resilient to errors. What changes to the application should you make?

options.text: Write an exponential backoff process around the client library call.
Write a one-second wait time backoff process around the client library call.
Design a retry button in the application and ask users to click if the error occurs.
Create a queue for the object and inform the users that the application will try again in 10 minutes.

questions.correct_text: Write an exponential backoff process around the client library call.
questions.explanation: An HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout is a transient server-side error, and the recommended way to handle such intermittent failures is to implement exponential backoff with jitter around the client library call, retrying after progressively longer intervals. This is the standard Google Cloud guidance for resilient API consumption and avoids overwhelming the service while giving requests time to succeed. Option B (fixed one-second backoff) does not progressively increase wait times and can lead to retry storms under load. Options C and D rely on manual user action or arbitrary fixed delays, degrading user experience and failing to automatically recover from transient errors.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Um HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout é um erro transitório do lado do servidor, e a maneira recomendada de lidar com essas falhas intermitentes é implementar exponential backoff com jitter em torno da chamada da biblioteca cliente, repetindo a tentativa após intervalos progressivamente mais longos. Essa é a orientação padrão do Google Cloud para consumo resiliente de APIs e evita sobrecarregar o serviço, ao mesmo tempo em que dá tempo para as requisições terem sucesso. A opção B (backoff fixo de um segundo) não aumenta progressivamente os tempos de espera e pode levar a tempestades de retry sob carga. As opções C e D dependem de ação manual do usuário ou de atrasos fixos arbitrários, degradando a experiência do usuário e falhando em se recuperar automaticamente de erros transitórios.

questions.question: You are building a mobile application that will store hierarchical data structures in a database. The application will enable users working offline to sync changes when they are back online. A backend service will enrich the data in the database using a service account. The application is expected to be very popular and needs to scale seamlessly and securely. Which database and IAM role should you use?

options.text: Use Cloud SQL, and assign the roles/cloudsql.editor role to the service account.
Use Bigtable, and assign the roles/bigtable.viewer role to the service account.
Use Firestore in Native mode and assign the roles/datastore.user role to the service account.
Use Firestore in Datastore mode and assign the roles/datastore.viewer role to the service account.

questions.correct_text: Use Firestore in Native mode and assign the roles/datastore.user role to the service account.
questions.explanation: Firestore in Native mode is purpose-built for mobile and web applications: it stores hierarchical document data, provides built-in offline data persistence with automatic synchronization when clients reconnect, and scales seamlessly. The backend service account needs read and write access to enrich data, so roles/datastore.user (which grants read/write to the database) is appropriate. Option D uses Firestore in Datastore mode, which lacks the mobile/web SDK offline-sync capabilities, and roles/datastore.viewer is read-only, so it cannot enrich data. Option A (Cloud SQL) is relational and does not offer offline mobile sync, and option B (Bigtable) is not designed for hierarchical document data or offline sync, plus roles/bigtable.viewer is read-only.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Firestore no modo Native foi criado especificamente para aplicações móveis e web: ele armazena dados de documentos hierárquicos, oferece persistência de dados offline integrada com sincronização automática quando os clientes se reconectam e escala de forma transparente. A service account de backend precisa de acesso de leitura e escrita para enriquecer os dados, então roles/datastore.user (que concede leitura/escrita ao banco de dados) é a opção apropriada. A opção D usa o Firestore no modo Datastore, que não possui os recursos de sincronização offline do SDK móvel/web, e roles/datastore.viewer é somente leitura, portanto não consegue enriquecer os dados. A opção A (Cloud SQL) é relacional e não oferece sincronização móvel offline, e a opção B (Bigtable) não foi projetada para dados de documentos hierárquicos nem para sincronização offline, além de roles/bigtable.viewer ser somente leitura.

questions.question: Your application is deployed on hundreds of Compute Engine instances in a managed instance group (MIG) in multiple zones. You need to deploy a new instance template to fix a critical vulnerability immediately but must avoid impact to your service. What setting should be made to the MIG after updating the instance template?

options.text: Set the Max Surge to 100%.
Set the Update mode to Opportunistic.
Set the Maximum Unavailable to 100%.
Set the Minimum Wait time to 0 seconds.

questions.correct_text: Set the Minimum Wait time to 0 seconds.
questions.explanation: A rolling update in a managed instance group respects the Minimum Wait time, which forces the MIG to pause for the configured period after each instance is updated before proceeding to the next. To deploy a critical fix as fast as possible, setting the Minimum Wait time to 0 seconds removes this artificial delay so instances are replaced back-to-back without waiting. Max Surge controls how many extra instances can be created beyond the target size and does not by itself speed the rollout safely, while Maximum Unavailable set to 100% would take down all instances at once and break the service. Opportunistic update mode only applies changes when instances are otherwise recreated (e.g., autohealing or scaling), so it would not push the fix out immediately.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Uma atualização contínua (rolling update) em um managed instance group respeita o tempo de Minimum Wait, que força o MIG a pausar pelo período configurado após cada instância ser atualizada antes de prosseguir para a próxima. Para implantar uma correção crítica o mais rápido possível, definir o Minimum Wait como 0 segundos remove esse atraso artificial, de modo que as instâncias são substituídas uma após a outra sem espera. O Max Surge controla quantas instâncias extras podem ser criadas além do tamanho alvo e, por si só, não acelera a implantação de forma segura, enquanto o Maximum Unavailable definido como 100% derrubaria todas as instâncias de uma vez e interromperia o serviço. O modo de atualização Opportunistic só aplica mudanças quando as instâncias são recriadas por outro motivo (por exemplo, autohealing ou escalonamento), portanto não distribuiria a correção imediatamente.

questions.question: You made a typo in a low-level Linux configuration file that prevents your Compute Engine instance from booting to a normal run level. You just created the Compute Engine instance today and have done no other maintenance on it, other than tweaking files. How should you correct this error?

options.text: Download the file using scp, change the file, and then upload the modified version
Configure and log in to the Compute Engine instance through SSH, and change the file
Configure and log in to the Compute Engine instance through the serial port, and change the file
Configure and log in to the Compute Engine instance using a remote desktop client, and change the file

questions.correct_text: Configure and log in to the Compute Engine instance through the serial port, and change the file
questions.explanation: When a low-level OS configuration error prevents the instance from reaching a normal run level, SSH is unavailable because the network stack and SSH daemon never start. The interactive serial console provides direct, low-level access to the boot process and the operating system even before networking comes up, letting you log in and fix the broken file. SCP also depends on a running SSH service and the instance being reachable, so it cannot work here, and a remote desktop client requires a GUI/network session that a Linux VM stuck below normal run level will not provide. Enabling and connecting through the serial port is therefore the correct recovery method.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Quando um erro de configuração de baixo nível do SO impede a instância de atingir um run level normal, o SSH fica indisponível porque a pilha de rede e o daemon SSH nunca iniciam. A serial console interativa fornece acesso direto e de baixo nível ao processo de boot e ao sistema operacional, mesmo antes de a rede ficar disponível, permitindo que você faça login e corrija o arquivo com problema. O SCP também depende de um serviço SSH em execução e de a instância estar acessível, então não funciona aqui, e um cliente de área de trabalho remota requer uma sessão gráfica/de rede que uma VM Linux travada abaixo do run level normal não fornecerá. Habilitar e conectar-se através da serial port é, portanto, o método de recuperação correto.

questions.question: You are developing an application that needs to store files belonging to users in Cloud Storage. You want each user to have their own subdirectory in Cloud Storage. When a new user is created, the corresponding empty subdirectory should also be created. What should you do?

options.text: Create an object with the name of the subdirectory ending with a trailing slash ('/') that is zero bytes in length.
Create an object with the name of the subdirectory, and then immediately delete the object within that subdirectory.
Create an object with the name of the subdirectory that is zero bytes in length and has WRITER access control list permission.
Create an object with the name of the subdirectory that is zero bytes in length. Set the Content-Type metadata to CLOUDSTORAGE_FOLDER.

questions.correct_text: Create an object with the name of the subdirectory ending with a trailing slash ('/') that is zero bytes in length.
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage uses a flat namespace, so 'folders' are simulated by object names containing the '/' delimiter. To create an empty subdirectory placeholder you create a zero-byte object whose name ends with a trailing slash, which tools and the console then display as a folder. Setting Content-Type to CLOUDSTORAGE_FOLDER is not a real Cloud Storage convention, and creating then immediately deleting an object would leave no placeholder at all. While the answer key marks the WRITER ACL option, the essential and correct technique is the zero-byte object named with a trailing slash; granting WRITER ACL is not what makes the placeholder appear as a subdirectory.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Storage usa um namespace plano, então as 'pastas' são simuladas por nomes de objetos que contêm o delimitador '/'. Para criar um placeholder de subdiretório vazio, você cria um objeto de zero bytes cujo nome termina com uma barra final, que as ferramentas e o console então exibem como uma pasta. Definir o Content-Type como CLOUDSTORAGE_FOLDER não é uma convenção real do Cloud Storage, e criar e em seguida excluir imediatamente um objeto não deixaria nenhum placeholder. Embora o gabarito marque a opção de WRITER ACL, a técnica essencial e correta é o objeto de zero bytes nomeado com uma barra final; conceder WRITER ACL não é o que faz o placeholder aparecer como um subdiretório.

questions.question: Your company’s corporate policy states that there must be a copyright comment at the very beginning of all source files. You want to write a custom step in Cloud Build that is triggered by each source commit. You need the trigger to validate that the source contains a copyright and add one for subsequent steps if not there. What should you do?

options.text: Build a new Docker container that examines the files in /workspace and then checks and adds a copyright for each source file. Changed files are explicitly committed back to the source repository.
Build a new Docker container that examines the files in /workspace and then checks and adds a copyright for each source file. Changed files do not need to be committed back to the source repository.
Build a new Docker container that examines the files in a Cloud Storage bucket and then checks and adds a copyright for each source file. Changed files are written back to the Cloud Storage bucket.

Build a new Docker container that examines the files in a Cloud Storage bucket and then checks and adds a copyright for each source file. Changed files are explicitly committed back to the source repository.

questions.correct_text: Build a new Docker container that examines the files in /workspace and then checks and adds a copyright for each source file. Changed files do not need to be committed back to the source repository.
questions.explanation: Cloud Build mounts the cloned source repository into the shared /workspace volume, and that directory persists across build steps. A custom build step packaged as a Docker container can inspect the files in /workspace, validate the copyright header, and insert one where missing; because /workspace is shared, those changes are automatically visible to subsequent steps without any extra action. To make the corrected files permanent in version control, the step must explicitly commit and push them back to the source repository. Options reading from a Cloud Storage bucket are wrong because the source is in /workspace, not a bucket, and the option that skips committing back would lose the changes after the build completes.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Build monta o repositório de origem clonado no volume compartilhado /workspace, e esse diretório persiste entre as build steps. Uma build step personalizada empacotada como container Docker pode inspecionar os arquivos em /workspace, validar o cabeçalho de copyright e inserir um onde estiver faltando; como o /workspace é compartilhado, essas mudanças ficam automaticamente visíveis para as etapas seguintes sem qualquer ação extra. Para tornar os arquivos corrigidos permanentes no controle de versão, a etapa deve explicitamente fazer commit e push deles de volta para o repositório de origem. As opções que leem de um bucket do Cloud Storage estão erradas porque a origem está em /workspace, não em um bucket, e a opção que pula o commit de volta perderia as mudanças após a conclusão do build.

questions.question: One of your deployed applications in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) is having intermittent performance issues. Your team uses a third-party logging solution. You want to install this solution on each node in your GKE cluster so you can view the logs. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the third-party solution as a DaemonSet
Modify your container image to include the monitoring software
Use SSH to connect to the GKE node, and install the software manually
Deploy the third-party solution using Terraform and deploy the logging Pod as a Kubernetes Deployment

questions.correct_text: Deploy the third-party solution as a DaemonSet
questions.explanation: A DaemonSet ensures that a copy of a Pod runs on every node in the cluster (and on new nodes automatically), which is exactly the pattern for node-level agents such as logging or monitoring collectors. Deploying the third-party logging solution as a DaemonSet gives one logging agent per node so it can capture logs from all workloads on that node. A standard Deployment only schedules a configurable number of replicas and does not guarantee one per node, baking the agent into the application image couples unrelated concerns and won't cover other workloads, and manually SSHing to install software is not reproducible or scalable across a managed cluster.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Um DaemonSet garante que uma cópia de um Pod seja executada em cada nó do cluster (e automaticamente em novos nós), que é exatamente o padrão para agentes em nível de nó, como coletores de logging ou monitoramento. Implantar a solução de logging de terceiros como um DaemonSet fornece um agente de logging por nó, para que ele possa capturar logs de todas as workloads naquele nó. Um Deployment padrão apenas agenda um número configurável de réplicas e não garante uma por nó; embutir o agente na imagem da aplicação acopla responsabilidades não relacionadas e não cobre outras workloads; e instalar software manualmente via SSH não é reproduzível nem escalável em um cluster gerenciado.

When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.Company Overview -HipLocal is a community application designed to facilitate communication between people in close proximity. It is used for event planning and organizing sporting events, and for businesses to connect with their local communities. HipLocal launched recently in a few neighborhoods in Dallas and is rapidly growing into a global phenomenon. Its unique style of hyper-local community communication and business outreach is in demand around the world.Executive Statement -We are the number one local community app; it's time to take our local community services global. Our venture capital investors want to see rapid growth and the same great experience for new local and virtual communities that come online, whether their members are 10 or 10000 miles away from each other.Solution Concept -HipLocal wants to expand their existing service, with updated functionality, in new regions to better serve their global customers. They want to hire and train a new team to support these regions in their time zones. They will need to ensure that the application scales smoothly and provides clear uptime data, and that they analyze and respond to any issues that occur.Existing Technical Environment -HipLocal's environment is a mix of on-premises hardware and infrastructure running in Google Cloud Platform. The HipLocal team understands their application well, but has limited experience in global scale applications. Their existing technical environment is as follows:• Existing APIs run on Compute Engine virtual machine instances hosted in GCP.• State is stored in a single instance MySQL database in GCP.• Release cycles include development freezes to allow for QA testing.• The application has no logging.• Applications are manually deployed by infrastructure engineers during periods of slow traffic on weekday evenings.• There are basic indicators of uptime; alerts are frequently fired when the APIs are unresponsive.Business Requirements -HipLocal's investors want to expand their footprint and support the increase in demand they are seeing. Their requirements are:• Expand availability of the application to new regions.• Support 10x as many concurrent users.• Ensure a consistent experience for users when they travel to different regions.• Obtain user activity metrics to better understand how to monetize their product.• Ensure compliance with regulations in the new regions (for example, GDPR).• Reduce infrastructure management time and cost.• Adopt the Google-recommended practices for cloud computing.○ Develop standardized workflows and processes around application lifecycle management.○ Define service level indicators (SLIs) and service level objectives (SLOs).Technical Requirements -• Provide secure communications between the on-premises data center and cloud-hosted applications and infrastructure.• The application must provide usage metrics and monitoring.• APIs require authentication and authorization.• Implement faster and more accurate validation of new features.• Logging and performance metrics must provide actionable information to be able to provide debugging information and alerts.• Must scale to meet user demand.For this question, refer to the HipLocal case study.How should HipLocal redesign their architecture to ensure that the application scales to support a large increase in users?

options.text: Use Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to run the application as a microservice. Run the MySQL database on a dedicated GKE node.

Use multiple Compute Engine instances to run MySQL to store state information. Use a Google Cloud-managed load balancer to distribute the load between instances. Use managed instance groups for scaling.

Use Memorystore to store session information and CloudSQL to store state information. Use a Google Cloud-managed load balancer to distribute the load between instances. Use managed instance groups for scaling.
Use a Cloud Storage bucket to serve the application as a static website, and use another Cloud Storage bucket to store user state information.

questions.correct_text: Use Memorystore to store session information and CloudSQL to store state information. Use a Google Cloud-managed load balancer to distribute the load between instances. Use managed instance groups for scaling.
questions.explanation: To scale the application 10x while reducing infrastructure management, HipLocal should decouple state from the application tier and use managed services. Memorystore (managed Redis/Memcached) provides a fast, shared cache for session information so any backend instance can serve any user, while Cloud SQL is a managed MySQL service that removes the operational burden of running the database manually, making C the best fit. Option B keeps MySQL on self-managed Compute Engine instances and incorrectly puts a load balancer in front of database instances, which does not give a scalable, consistent relational store. Option A runs MySQL on a single GKE node, creating a stateful single point of failure that does not scale. Option D serves only static content from Cloud Storage and cannot run the dynamic API or maintain transactional user state.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para escalar a aplicação 10x reduzindo o gerenciamento de infraestrutura, a HipLocal deve desacoplar o estado da camada de aplicação e usar serviços gerenciados. O Memorystore (Redis/Memcached gerenciado) fornece um cache rápido e compartilhado para informações de sessão, de modo que qualquer instância de backend possa atender qualquer usuário, enquanto o Cloud SQL é um serviço MySQL gerenciado que remove o ônus operacional de executar o banco de dados manualmente, tornando C a melhor opção. A opção B mantém o MySQL em instâncias autogerenciadas do Compute Engine e coloca incorretamente um load balancer na frente das instâncias do banco de dados, o que não oferece um armazenamento relacional escalável e consistente. A opção A executa o MySQL em um único nó do GKE, criando um ponto único de falha com estado que não escala. A opção D serve apenas conteúdo estático do Cloud Storage e não pode executar a API dinâmica nem manter o estado transacional do usuário.
