options.text: Include unit tests in their code, and prevent deployments to QA until all tests have a passing status.
Include performance tests in their code, and prevent deployments to QA until all tests have a passing status.
Create health checks for the QA environment, and redeploy the APIs at a later time if the environment is unhealthy.
Redeploy the APIs to App Engine using Traffic Splitting. Do not move QA traffic to the new versions if errors are found.

questions.correct_text: Include unit tests in their code, and prevent deployments to QA until all tests have a passing status.
questions.explanation: The goal is to increase development speed without destabilizing the QA environment. Adding unit tests to the codebase and gating deployments to QA on passing tests catches defects early in the pipeline, so only validated code reaches QA, which both accelerates iteration and keeps the QA environment stable, making A correct. Option B's performance tests verify scalability and latency rather than feature correctness, so they do not ensure features work and are not the primary gate for QA stability. Option C only reacts to an already-unhealthy QA environment by delaying redeployment, which does not prevent bad code from breaking it. Option D uses App Engine traffic splitting, which is a production rollout technique and does not provide the automated pre-QA validation that increases development speed.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O objetivo é aumentar a velocidade de desenvolvimento sem desestabilizar o ambiente de QA. Adicionar testes unitários ao código e condicionar as implantações em QA à aprovação dos testes detecta defeitos cedo no pipeline, de modo que apenas código validado chegue ao QA, o que acelera a iteração e mantém o ambiente de QA estável, tornando A correta. Os testes de desempenho da opção B verificam escalabilidade e latência em vez da correção das funcionalidades, portanto não garantem que as funcionalidades funcionem e não são o controle principal para a estabilidade do QA. A opção C apenas reage a um ambiente de QA já comprometido, atrasando a reimplantação, o que não impede que código defeituoso o quebre. A opção D usa divisão de tráfego do App Engine, que é uma técnica de lançamento em produção e não fornece a validação automatizada pré-QA que aumenta a velocidade de desenvolvimento.

HipLocal needs to configure authentication and authorization in the Cloud Client Libraries to implement least privileged access for the application. What should they do?

options.text: Create an API key. Use the API key to interact with Google Cloud.
Use the default compute service account to interact with Google Cloud.
Create a service account for the application. Export and deploy the private key for the application. Use the service account to interact with Google Cloud.

Create a service account for the application and for each Google Cloud API used by the application. Export and deploy the private keys used by the application. Use the service account with one Google Cloud API to interact with Google Cloud.

questions.correct_text: Create a service account for the application. Export and deploy the private key for the application. Use the service account to interact with Google Cloud.
questions.explanation: To implement least privilege with Cloud Client Libraries, HipLocal should create a dedicated service account for the application and grant it only the IAM roles it needs, then use that service account's credentials (Application Default Credentials) so the libraries authenticate as the application, making C correct. Option A's API keys do not identify a principal or support fine-grained IAM authorization, so they cannot enforce least privilege. Option B's default Compute Engine service account is overly permissive by default and shared across resources, violating least privilege. Option D needlessly creates a separate service account per API and only uses one of them, which adds complexity and key-management risk without improving access control; a single purpose-built service account with scoped roles is the recommended approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para implementar o privilégio mínimo com as Cloud Client Libraries, a HipLocal deve criar uma service account dedicada para a aplicação e conceder a ela apenas os papéis de IAM necessários, e então usar as credenciais dessa service account (Application Default Credentials) para que as bibliotecas se autentiquem como a aplicação, tornando C correta. As API keys da opção A não identificam um principal nem suportam autorização IAM granular, portanto não podem impor o privilégio mínimo. A service account padrão do Compute Engine da opção B é excessivamente permissiva por padrão e compartilhada entre recursos, violando o privilégio mínimo. A opção D cria desnecessariamente uma service account separada por API e usa apenas uma delas, o que adiciona complexidade e risco de gerenciamento de chaves sem melhorar o controle de acesso; uma única service account criada para o propósito com papéis restritos é a abordagem recomendada.

questions.question: You are in the final stage of migrating an on-premises data center to Google Cloud. You are quickly approaching your deadline, and discover that a web API is running on a server slated for decommissioning. You need to recommend a solution to modernize this API while migrating to Google Cloud. The modernized web API must meet the following requirements:• Autoscales during high traffic periods at the end of each month• Written in Python 3.x• Developers must be able to rapidly deploy new versions in response to frequent code changesYou want to minimize cost, effort, and operational overhead of this migration. What should you do?

options.text: Modernize and deploy the code on App Engine flexible environment.
Modernize and deploy the code on App Engine standard environment.
Deploy the modernized application to an n1-standard-1 Compute Engine instance.
Ask the development team to re-write the application to run as a Docker container on Google Kubernetes Engine.

questions.correct_text: Modernize and deploy the code on App Engine standard environment.
questions.explanation: The requirements are autoscaling for monthly traffic spikes, Python 3.x support, rapid deployment of frequent code changes, and minimal cost, effort, and operational overhead. App Engine standard environment supports Python 3.x, autoscales (including scaling to zero, minimizing cost during idle periods), and lets developers deploy new versions quickly with a single command, making B the best fit. App Engine flexible environment (A) runs on Compute Engine VMs that cannot scale to zero and have slower deployments and higher cost, so it adds unnecessary overhead. A single n1-standard-1 Compute Engine instance (C) does not autoscale and requires significant management. Rewriting the application to run as a container on GKE (D) maximizes effort and operational overhead, contradicting the goal of minimizing migration work.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Os requisitos são autoescalonamento para picos de tráfego mensais, suporte a Python 3.x, implantação rápida de mudanças frequentes de código e custo, esforço e sobrecarga operacional mínimos. O ambiente standard do App Engine suporta Python 3.x, faz autoescalonamento (incluindo escalar até zero, minimizando o custo durante períodos ociosos) e permite que os desenvolvedores implantem novas versões rapidamente com um único comando, tornando B a melhor opção. O ambiente flexible do App Engine (A) roda em VMs do Compute Engine que não conseguem escalar até zero e têm implantações mais lentas e custo maior, adicionando sobrecarga desnecessária. Uma única instância n1-standard-1 do Compute Engine (C) não faz autoescalonamento e requer gerenciamento significativo. Reescrever a aplicação para rodar como um container no GKE (D) maximiza o esforço e a sobrecarga operacional, contrariando o objetivo de minimizar o trabalho de migração.

questions.question: You are developing an application that consists of several microservices running in a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. One microservice needs to connect to a third-party database running on-premises. You need to store credentials to the database and ensure that these credentials can be rotated while following security best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Store the credentials in a sidecar container proxy, and use it to connect to the third-party database.
Configure a service mesh to allow or restrict traffic from the Pods in your microservice to the database.
Store the credentials in an encrypted volume mount, and associate a Persistent Volume Claim with the client Pod.
Store the credentials as a Kubernetes Secret, and use the Cloud Key Management Service plugin to handle encryption and decryption.

questions.correct_text: Store the credentials as a Kubernetes Secret, and use the Cloud Key Management Service plugin to handle encryption and decryption.
questions.explanation: The credentials must be stored in GKE, rotatable, and managed with security best practices. Storing them as a Kubernetes Secret while using the Cloud KMS plugin for Kubernetes encryption at rest (application-layer Secrets encryption / envelope encryption) keeps the secret available to the Pod, encrypts it with a KMS key that can be rotated, and follows recommended security practices, making D correct. Option A places plaintext credentials in a sidecar container, which does not provide encryption or managed rotation. Option B's service mesh controls network traffic between Pods and the database but does not store or rotate credentials at all. Option C's encrypted volume with a Persistent Volume Claim is intended for general data storage rather than managing and rotating secret credentials, and does not integrate with a key-management workflow.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: As credenciais devem ser armazenadas no GKE, ser rotacionáveis e gerenciadas com as melhores práticas de segurança. Armazená-las como um Kubernetes Secret enquanto se usa o plugin do Cloud KMS para criptografia em repouso do Kubernetes (criptografia de Secrets na camada de aplicação / envelope encryption) mantém o segredo disponível para o Pod, criptografa-o com uma chave do KMS que pode ser rotacionada e segue as práticas de segurança recomendadas, tornando D a resposta correta. A opção A coloca credenciais em texto puro em um container sidecar, o que não fornece criptografia nem rotação gerenciada. O service mesh da opção B controla o tráfego de rede entre os Pods e o banco de dados, mas não armazena nem rotaciona credenciais de forma alguma. O volume criptografado com um Persistent Volume Claim da opção C é destinado ao armazenamento geral de dados, e não ao gerenciamento e rotação de credenciais secretas, e não se integra a um fluxo de gerenciamento de chaves.

questions.question: You manage your company's ecommerce platform's payment system, which runs on Google Cloud. Your company must retain user logs for 1 year for internal auditing purposes and for 3 years to meet compliance requirements. You need to store new user logs on Google Cloud to minimize on-premises storage usage and ensure that they are easily searchable. You want to minimize effort while ensuring that the logs are stored correctly. What should you do?

options.text: Store the logs in a Cloud Storage bucket with bucket lock turned on.
Store the logs in a Cloud Storage bucket with a 3-year retention period.
Store the logs in Cloud Logging as custom logs with a custom retention period.
Store the logs in a Cloud Storage bucket with a 1-year retention period. After 1 year, move the logs to another bucket with a 2-year retention period.

questions.correct_text: Store the logs in Cloud Logging as custom logs with a custom retention period.
questions.explanation: Cloud Logging lets you ingest logs and create custom log buckets with configurable retention periods, allowing you to keep logs for up to 3 years while keeping them indexed and easily searchable through the Logs Explorer with minimal operational effort. Storing logs in Cloud Storage with bucket lock or a fixed retention period (A, B) makes them harder to search and would not satisfy the two-tier auditing-versus-compliance requirement cleanly. Option D introduces unnecessary manual bucket-to-bucket movement, increasing effort and risk. Custom Cloud Logging retention directly meets the searchability and low-effort goals.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Logging permite ingerir logs e criar buckets de logs personalizados com períodos de retenção configuráveis, permitindo que você mantenha os logs por até 3 anos, ao mesmo tempo em que eles permanecem indexados e facilmente pesquisáveis por meio do Logs Explorer com mínimo esforço operacional. Armazenar logs no Cloud Storage com bucket lock ou um período de retenção fixo (A, B) torna-os mais difíceis de pesquisar e não atenderia de forma limpa ao requisito de duas camadas de auditoria versus conformidade. A opção D introduz uma movimentação manual desnecessária de bucket para bucket, aumentando o esforço e o risco. A retenção personalizada do Cloud Logging atende diretamente aos objetivos de pesquisabilidade e baixo esforço.

questions.question: Your company has a new security initiative that requires all data stored in Google Cloud to be encrypted by customer-managed encryption keys. You plan to use Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) to configure access to the keys. You need to follow the "separation of duties" principle and Google-recommended best practices. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Provision Cloud KMS in its own project.
Do not assign an owner to the Cloud KMS project.
Provision Cloud KMS in the project where the keys are being used.
Grant the roles/cloudkms.admin role to the owner of the project where the keys from Cloud KMS are being used.
Grant an owner role for the Cloud KMS project to a different user than the owner of the project where the keys from Cloud KMS are being used.

questions.correct_text: Provision Cloud KMS in its own project. | Do not assign an owner to the Cloud KMS project.
questions.explanation: To enforce separation of duties for customer-managed encryption keys, Google recommends provisioning Cloud KMS in its own dedicated project so key management is isolated from the projects consuming the keys (A). Additionally, you should not assign an owner to the Cloud KMS project, because the broad owner role would let a single principal both administer keys and access the encrypted resources, breaking separation of duties (B). Provisioning KMS in the same project as the keys' usage (C) defeats the isolation goal. Granting cloudkms.admin or owner to the consuming project's owner (D, E) concentrates privileges and violates the principle.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para impor a separação de funções (separation of duties) para chaves de criptografia gerenciadas pelo cliente (customer-managed encryption keys), o Google recomenda provisionar o Cloud KMS em seu próprio projeto dedicado, de modo que o gerenciamento de chaves fique isolado dos projetos que consomem as chaves (A). Além disso, você não deve atribuir um owner ao projeto do Cloud KMS, porque o amplo papel de owner permitiria que um único principal tanto administrasse as chaves quanto acessasse os recursos criptografados, quebrando a separação de funções (B). Provisionar o KMS no mesmo projeto em que as chaves são usadas (C) anula o objetivo de isolamento. Conceder cloudkms.admin ou owner ao owner do projeto consumidor (D, E) concentra privilégios e viola o princípio.

questions.question: You need to migrate a standalone Java application running in an on-premises Linux virtual machine (VM) to Google Cloud in a cost-effective manner. You decide not to take the lift-and-shift approach, and instead you plan to modernize the application by converting it to a container. How should you accomplish this task?

options.text: Use Migrate for Anthos to migrate the VM to your Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster as a container.
Export the VM as a raw disk and import it as an image. Create a Compute Engine instance from the Imported image.
Use Migrate for Compute Engine to migrate the VM to a Compute Engine instance, and use Cloud Build to convert it to a container.
Use Jib to build a Docker image from your source code, and upload it to Artifact Registry. Deploy the application in a GKE cluster, and test the application.

questions.correct_text: Use Jib to build a Docker image from your source code, and upload it to Artifact Registry. Deploy the application in a GKE cluster, and test the application.
questions.explanation: Since the goal is to modernize a standalone Java application into a container cost-effectively rather than lift-and-shift, Jib is the ideal tool because it builds optimized Docker/OCI images directly from Java source without a Dockerfile or Docker daemon; you push the image to Artifact Registry and deploy it to GKE (D). Migrate for Anthos (A) and Migrate for Compute Engine (C) are migration tools oriented at moving the VM rather than rebuilding the app as a clean container, adding complexity. Exporting the disk and creating a Compute Engine instance (B) is a lift-and-shift approach, which the requirements explicitly exclude.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Como o objetivo é modernizar uma aplicação Java standalone transformando-a em um container de forma econômica, em vez de fazer lift-and-shift, o Jib é a ferramenta ideal porque constrói imagens Docker/OCI otimizadas diretamente a partir do código-fonte Java, sem um Dockerfile ou um daemon do Docker; você envia a imagem para o Artifact Registry e a implanta no GKE (D). O Migrate for Anthos (A) e o Migrate for Compute Engine (C) são ferramentas de migração orientadas a mover a VM, em vez de reconstruir a aplicação como um container limpo, adicionando complexidade. Exportar o disco e criar uma instância do Compute Engine (B) é uma abordagem de lift-and-shift, que os requisitos excluem explicitamente.

questions.question: Your organization has recently begun an initiative to replatform their legacy applications onto Google Kubernetes Engine. You need to decompose a monolithic application into microservices. Multiple instances have read and write access to a configuration file, which is stored on a shared file system. You want to minimize the effort required to manage this transition, and you want to avoid rewriting the application code. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Cloud Storage bucket, and mount it via FUSE in the container.
Create a new persistent disk, and mount the volume as a shared PersistentVolume.
Create a new Filestore instance, and mount the volume as an NFS PersistentVolume.
Create a new ConfigMap and volumeMount to store the contents of the configuration file.

questions.correct_text: Create a new Filestore instance, and mount the volume as an NFS PersistentVolume.
questions.explanation: Because multiple pods need concurrent read and write access to a shared file via a file-system interface, you need ReadWriteMany shared storage, which Filestore provides as a managed NFS service mounted as an NFS PersistentVolume (C). This requires no application code changes since the app still sees a normal file path. A standard persistent disk (B) only supports ReadWriteOnce for read/write, so it cannot be shared writable across multiple instances. Cloud Storage via FUSE (A) is not a true POSIX file system and performs poorly for shared read/write config files, and a ConfigMap (D) is read-only to pods and unsuitable for files that must be written.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Como vários pods precisam de acesso concorrente de leitura e escrita a um arquivo compartilhado por meio de uma interface de sistema de arquivos, você precisa de armazenamento compartilhado ReadWriteMany, que o Filestore fornece como um serviço NFS gerenciado, montado como um PersistentVolume NFS (C). Isso não exige alterações no código da aplicação, já que o app continua enxergando um caminho de arquivo normal. Um persistent disk padrão (B) só suporta ReadWriteOnce para leitura/escrita, então não pode ser compartilhado com escrita entre várias instâncias. O Cloud Storage via FUSE (A) não é um verdadeiro sistema de arquivos POSIX e tem desempenho ruim para arquivos de configuração compartilhados de leitura/escrita, e um ConfigMap (D) é somente leitura para os pods e inadequado para arquivos que precisam ser escritos.

questions.question: Your development team has built several Cloud Functions using Java along with corresponding integration and service tests. You are building and deploying the functions and launching the tests using Cloud Build. Your Cloud Build job is reporting deployment failures immediately after successfully validating the code. What should you do?

options.text: Check the maximum number of Cloud Function instances.
Verify that your Cloud Build trigger has the correct build parameters.
Retry the tests using the truncated exponential backoff polling strategy.
Verify that the Cloud Build service account is assigned the Cloud Functions Developer role.

questions.correct_text: Verify that the Cloud Build service account is assigned the Cloud Functions Developer role.
questions.explanation: When code validation succeeds but the deployment step immediately fails, the most common cause is that the Cloud Build service account lacks the IAM permissions needed to deploy, so granting it the Cloud Functions Developer role resolves the failure (D). Checking the maximum number of function instances (A) relates to runtime scaling, not deploy-time failures. Build trigger parameters (B) would more likely cause the build or validation to fail earlier rather than only at deployment. Exponential backoff retries (C) address transient rate-limit or availability errors during tests, not a permission-based deployment failure.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Quando a validação do código é bem-sucedida, mas a etapa de deployment falha imediatamente, a causa mais comum é que a service account do Cloud Build não possui as permissões IAM necessárias para fazer o deploy, então conceder a ela o papel Cloud Functions Developer resolve a falha (D). Verificar o número máximo de instâncias da function (A) está relacionado ao scaling em tempo de execução, não a falhas no momento do deployment. Parâmetros do build trigger (B) provavelmente fariam o build ou a validação falhar mais cedo, e não apenas no deployment. Retentativas com exponential backoff (C) tratam erros transitórios de rate-limit ou disponibilidade durante os testes, não uma falha de deployment baseada em permissões.

questions.question: You manage a microservices application on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) using Istio. You secure the communication channels between your microservices by implementing an Istio AuthorizationPolicy, a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, and mTLS on your GKE cluster. You discover that HTTP requests between two Pods to specific URLs fail, while other requests to other URLs succeed. What is the cause of the connection issue?

options.text: A Kubernetes NetworkPolicy resource is blocking HTTP traffic between the Pods.
The Pod initiating the HTTP requests is attempting to connect to the target Pod via an incorrect TCP port.
The Authorization Policy of your cluster is blocking HTTP requests for specific paths within your application.
The cluster has mTLS configured in permissive mode, but the Pod's sidecar proxy is sending unencrypted traffic in plain text.

questions.correct_text: The Authorization Policy of your cluster is blocking HTTP requests for specific paths within your application.
questions.explanation: Because some HTTP requests succeed while only requests to specific URLs/paths fail, the issue is path-specific authorization rather than transport-level connectivity. An Istio AuthorizationPolicy can match on HTTP attributes such as paths and methods, so a policy denying specific URL paths produces exactly this selective behavior. A Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (A) operates at L3/L4 on Pods, ports, and IP ranges, so it would block all traffic between the Pods, not just certain URLs. An incorrect TCP port (B) would cause every connection to fail, and permissive-mode mTLS sending plaintext (D) would still allow traffic since permissive mode accepts both encrypted and plaintext, so neither matches selective per-path failures.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Como algumas requisições HTTP têm sucesso enquanto apenas requisições para URLs/paths específicos falham, o problema é de autorização específica por path, e não de conectividade em nível de transporte. Uma AuthorizationPolicy do Istio pode fazer match em atributos HTTP como paths e methods, então uma policy que nega paths de URL específicos produz exatamente esse comportamento seletivo. Uma NetworkPolicy do Kubernetes (A) opera em L3/L4 sobre Pods, portas e faixas de IP, então bloquearia todo o tráfego entre os Pods, não apenas certas URLs. Uma porta TCP incorreta (B) faria toda conexão falhar, e o mTLS em modo permissive enviando texto plano (D) ainda permitiria o tráfego, já que o modo permissive aceita tanto tráfego criptografado quanto em texto plano, de modo que nenhum corresponde a falhas seletivas por path.

questions.question: You recently migrated an on-premises monolithic application to a microservices application on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The application has dependencies on backend services on-premises, including a CRM system and a MySQL database that contains personally identifiable information (PII). The backend services must remain on-premises to meet regulatory requirements.You established a Cloud VPN connection between your on-premises data center and Google Cloud. You notice that some requests from your microservices application on GKE to the backend services are failing due to latency issues caused by fluctuating bandwidth, which is causing the application to crash. How should you address the latency issues?

options.text: Use Memorystore to cache frequently accessed PII data from the on-premises MySQL database
Use Istio to create a service mesh that includes the microservices on GKE and the on-premises services
Increase the number of Cloud VPN tunnels for the connection between Google Cloud and the on-premises services
Decrease the network layer packet size by decreasing the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) value from its default value on Cloud VPN

questions.correct_text: Use Istio to create a service mesh that includes the microservices on GKE and the on-premises services
questions.explanation: The crashes stem from the application not tolerating latency and bandwidth fluctuations over the hybrid VPN link. Adding the on-premises services into an Istio service mesh lets you apply resilience patterns such as timeouts, retries, and circuit breaking, which gracefully handle transient latency and failures so the application stops crashing. Caching PII in Memorystore (A) is inappropriate because PII data should remain on-premises for regulatory reasons and caching does not address general latency for CRM calls. Adding more VPN tunnels (C) increases aggregate throughput but does not stabilize latency or make the app resilient, and lowering the MTU (D) does not fix bandwidth fluctuation and can degrade performance further.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: As falhas (crashes) decorrem do fato de a aplicação não tolerar as flutuações de latência e largura de banda no link VPN híbrido. Adicionar os serviços on-premises a um service mesh Istio permite aplicar padrões de resiliência como timeouts, retries e circuit breaking, que lidam de forma elegante com latência e falhas transitórias, fazendo a aplicação parar de travar. Fazer cache de PII no Memorystore (A) é inadequado porque dados de PII devem permanecer on-premises por razões regulatórias, e o cache não resolve a latência geral das chamadas ao CRM. Adicionar mais túneis VPN (C) aumenta a vazão agregada, mas não estabiliza a latência nem torna a app resiliente, e reduzir o MTU (D) não corrige a flutuação de largura de banda e pode degradar ainda mais o desempenho.

questions.question: Your company has deployed a new API to a Compute Engine instance. During testing, the API is not behaving as expected. You want to monitor the application over 12 hours to diagnose the problem within the application code without redeploying the application. Which tool should you use?

options.text: Cloud Trace
Cloud Monitoring
Cloud Debugger logpoints
Cloud Debugger snapshots

questions.correct_text: Cloud Debugger logpoints
questions.explanation: Cloud Debugger logpoints let you inject log statements into running production code without redeploying, and they persist for up to 24 hours, making them ideal for observing application behavior over a 12-hour window to diagnose logic problems. Snapshots (D) capture call stack and variable state at a point in time but are limited and not meant for continuous monitoring over many hours. Cloud Trace (A) measures latency of requests and Cloud Monitoring (B) tracks metrics, but neither inspects application code logic to diagnose unexpected behavior. Logpoints uniquely combine code-level visibility with an extended observation period and no redeployment.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Os logpoints do Cloud Debugger permitem injetar instruções de log em código de produção em execução sem fazer redeploy, e eles persistem por até 24 horas, o que os torna ideais para observar o comportamento da aplicação ao longo de uma janela de 12 horas para diagnosticar problemas de lógica. Os snapshots (D) capturam a call stack e o estado das variáveis em um ponto no tempo, mas são limitados e não foram feitos para monitoramento contínuo por muitas horas. O Cloud Trace (A) mede a latência das requisições e o Cloud Monitoring (B) acompanha métricas, mas nenhum inspeciona a lógica do código da aplicação para diagnosticar comportamento inesperado. Os logpoints combinam de forma única a visibilidade em nível de código com um período de observação estendido e sem necessidade de redeploy.

questions.question: You are designing an application that consists of several microservices. Each microservice has its own RESTful API and will be deployed as a separate Kubernetes Service. You want to ensure that the consumers of these APIs aren't impacted when there is a change to your API, and also ensure that third-party systems aren't interrupted when new versions of the API are released. How should you configure the connection to the application following Google-recommended best practices?

options.text: Use an Ingress that uses the API's URL to route requests to the appropriate backend.
Leverage a Service Discovery system, and connect to the backend specified by the request.
Use multiple clusters, and use DNS entries to route requests to separate versioned backends.
Combine multiple versions in the same service, and then specify the API version in the POST request.

questions.correct_text: Use an Ingress that uses the API's URL to route requests to the appropriate backend.
questions.explanation: Using an Ingress that routes based on the API's URL path lets you expose distinct, versioned endpoints (for example /v1 and /v2) so existing consumers and third-party systems keep hitting their stable path while new versions are added without disruption. This is the Google-recommended way to do path-based routing and API versioning at the cluster edge. Service Discovery (B) handles internal endpoint resolution, not stable external API versioning for third parties. Multiple clusters with DNS (C) is operationally heavy and unnecessary, and combining versions in one service while passing the version in the POST body (D) breaks RESTful conventions and couples clients to request payloads rather than stable routes.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Usar um Ingress que roteia com base no path da URL da API permite expor endpoints distintos e versionados (por exemplo /v1 e /v2), de modo que os consumidores existentes e sistemas de terceiros continuem acessando seu path estável enquanto novas versões são adicionadas sem interrupção. Essa é a forma recomendada pelo Google para fazer roteamento baseado em path e versionamento de API na borda do cluster. O Service Discovery (B) trata da resolução interna de endpoints, não do versionamento externo estável de API para terceiros. Múltiplos clusters com DNS (C) é operacionalmente pesado e desnecessário, e combinar versões em um único serviço passando a versão no body do POST (D) quebra as convenções RESTful e acopla os clientes ao payload da requisição em vez de a rotas estáveis.

questions.question: Your team is building an application for a financial institution. The application's frontend runs on Compute Engine, and the data resides in Cloud SQL and one Cloud Storage bucket. The application will collect data containing PII, which will be stored in the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket. You need to secure the PII data. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create the relevant firewall rules to allow only the frontend to communicate with the Cloud SQL database2. Using IAM, allow only the frontend service account to access the Cloud Storage bucket
1. Create the relevant firewall rules to allow only the frontend to communicate with the Cloud SQL database2. Enable private access to allow the frontend to access the Cloud Storage bucket privately
1. Configure a private IP address for Cloud SQL2. Use VPC-SC to create a service perimeter3. Add the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket to the same service perimeter
1. Configure a private IP address for Cloud SQL2. Use VPC-SC to create a service perimeter3. Add the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket to different service perimeters

questions.correct_text: 1. Configure a private IP address for Cloud SQL2. Use VPC-SC to create a service perimeter3. Add the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket to the same service perimeter
questions.explanation: To protect PII across both Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage, you configure a private IP for Cloud SQL and use VPC Service Controls to create a service perimeter that includes both the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket. Placing them in the same perimeter prevents data exfiltration while still allowing the two resources and the frontend to interact within the trusted boundary. Putting them in different perimeters (D) would block legitimate communication between the resources and complicate access. Firewall rules plus IAM (A) and private access (B) restrict network and identity access but do not provide the data-exfiltration protection of VPC-SC, which is the defining control for securing PII at scale.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para proteger PII tanto no Cloud SQL quanto no Cloud Storage, você configura um IP privado para o Cloud SQL e usa VPC Service Controls para criar um perímetro de serviço que inclua tanto o banco de dados Cloud SQL quanto o bucket do Cloud Storage. Colocá-los no mesmo perímetro impede a exfiltração de dados e ao mesmo tempo permite que os dois recursos e o frontend interajam dentro da fronteira confiável. Colocá-los em perímetros diferentes (D) bloquearia a comunicação legítima entre os recursos e complicaria o acesso. Regras de firewall mais IAM (A) e acesso privado (B) restringem o acesso de rede e de identidade, mas não fornecem a proteção contra exfiltração de dados do VPC-SC, que é o controle definidor para proteger PII em escala.

questions.question: You are designing a chat room application that will host multiple rooms and retain the message history for each room. You have selected Firestore as your database. How should you represent the data in Firestore?

options.text: Create a collection for the rooms. For each room, create a document that lists the contents of the messages
Create a collection for the rooms. For each room, create a collection that contains a document for each message
Create a collection for the rooms. For each room, create a document that contains a collection for documents, each of which contains a message.

Create a collection for the rooms, and create a document for each room. Create a separate collection for messages, with one document per message. Each room’s document contains a list of references to the messages.

questions.correct_text: Create a collection for the rooms. For each room, create a document that contains a collection for documents, each of which contains a message.
questions.explanation: Firestore models hierarchical data using subcollections, which is ideal for a chat application: a top-level 'rooms' collection holds a document per room, and each room document contains a subcollection of message documents. This keeps messages independent, queryable, and scalable per room, avoiding the document size limits and rewrite contention you would hit by stuffing all messages into one document. Option A puts all messages inside a single room document, which does not scale and quickly approaches the 1 MiB document size limit. Option B is invalid because Firestore does not allow a collection to directly contain another collection without an intervening document. Option D uses reference lists, which adds unnecessary complexity and extra reads compared to the natural subcollection model.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Firestore modela dados hierárquicos usando subcollections, o que é ideal para um aplicativo de chat: uma collection de nível superior 'rooms' mantém um documento por sala, e cada documento de sala contém uma subcollection de documentos de mensagem. Isso mantém as mensagens independentes, consultáveis e escaláveis por sala, evitando os limites de tamanho de documento e a contenção de reescrita que você enfrentaria ao amontoar todas as mensagens em um único documento. A opção A coloca todas as mensagens dentro de um único documento de sala, o que não escala e rapidamente se aproxima do limite de tamanho de documento de 1 MiB. A opção B é inválida porque o Firestore não permite que uma collection contenha diretamente outra collection sem um documento intermediário. A opção D usa listas de referências, o que adiciona complexidade desnecessária e leituras extras em comparação com o modelo natural de subcollection.

questions.question: You are developing an application that will handle requests from end users. You need to secure a Cloud Function called by the application to allow authorized end users to authenticate to the function via the application while restricting access to unauthorized users. You will integrate Google Sign-In as part of the solution and want to follow Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy from a source code repository and grant users the roles/cloudfunctions.viewer role.
Deploy from a source code repository and grant users the roles/cloudfunctions.invoker role
Deploy from your local machine using gcloud and grant users the roles/cloudfunctions.admin role
Deploy from your local machine using gcloud and grant users the roles/cloudfunctions.developer role

questions.correct_text: Deploy from a source code repository and grant users the roles/cloudfunctions.invoker role
questions.explanation: To allow only authorized end users to call a Cloud Function, you grant the roles/cloudfunctions.invoker role, which is the minimal IAM role that permits invoking the function while following least privilege. Combined with Google Sign-In, authenticated users present credentials that the function validates, restricting unauthorized access. The cloudfunctions.viewer role only allows reading function metadata, not invoking it, so option A fails. The admin and developer roles in options C and D grant broad management and deployment permissions that far exceed what an end user needs, violating the principle of least privilege.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Para permitir que apenas usuários finais autorizados chamem uma Cloud Function, você concede o papel roles/cloudfunctions.invoker, que é o papel IAM mínimo que permite invocar a função seguindo o princípio do menor privilégio. Combinado com o Google Sign-In, os usuários autenticados apresentam credenciais que a função valida, restringindo o acesso não autorizado. O papel cloudfunctions.viewer permite apenas a leitura dos metadados da função, não a sua invocação, por isso a opção A falha. Os papéis admin e developer nas opções C e D concedem amplas permissões de gerenciamento e implantação que excedem em muito o que um usuário final precisa, violando o princípio do menor privilégio.

questions.question: You are running a web application on Google Kubernetes Engine that you inherited. You want to determine whether the application is using libraries with known vulnerabilities or is vulnerable to XSS attacks. Which service should you use?

options.text: Google Cloud Armor
Debugger
Web Security Scanner
Error Reporting

questions.correct_text: Web Security Scanner
questions.explanation: Web Security Scanner crawls a deployed web application and actively probes it for common vulnerabilities such as cross-site scripting (XSS), use of outdated or insecure libraries, mixed content, and clear-text password fields, which directly matches the requirement. Cloud Armor is a WAF and DDoS protection service that enforces rules at the edge but does not scan application code for vulnerabilities. Debugger inspects application state at runtime and Error Reporting aggregates exceptions, neither of which performs security vulnerability scanning. Therefore Web Security Scanner is the correct service for detecting vulnerable libraries and XSS exposure.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Web Security Scanner rastreia um aplicativo web implantado e o sonda ativamente em busca de vulnerabilidades comuns, como cross-site scripting (XSS), uso de bibliotecas desatualizadas ou inseguras, conteúdo misto e campos de senha em texto puro, o que corresponde diretamente ao requisito. O Cloud Armor é um serviço de WAF e proteção contra DDoS que aplica regras na borda, mas não escaneia o código do aplicativo em busca de vulnerabilidades. O Debugger inspeciona o estado do aplicativo em tempo de execução e o Error Reporting agrega exceções, e nenhum dos dois realiza varredura de vulnerabilidades de segurança. Portanto, o Web Security Scanner é o serviço correto para detectar bibliotecas vulneráveis e exposição a XSS.

questions.question: You are building a highly available and globally accessible application that will serve static content to users. You need to configure the storage and serving components. You want to minimize management overhead and latency while maximizing reliability for users. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create a managed instance group. Replicate the static content across the virtual machines (VMs)2. Create an external HTTP(S) load balancer.3. Enable Cloud CDN, and send traffic to the managed instance group.
1. Create an unmanaged instance group. Replicate the static content across the VMs.2. Create an external HTTP(S) load balancer3. Enable Cloud CDN, and send traffic to the unmanaged instance group.

1. Create a Standard storage class, regional Cloud Storage bucket. Put the static content in the bucket2. Reserve an external IP address, and create an external HTTP(S) load balancer3. Enable Cloud CDN, and send traffic to your backend bucket

1. Create a Standard storage class, multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket. Put the static content in the bucket.2. Reserve an external IP address, and create an external HTTP(S) load balancer.3. Enable Cloud CDN, and send traffic to your backend bucket.

questions.correct_text: 1. Create a Standard storage class, multi-regional Cloud Storage bucket. Put the static content in the bucket.2. Reserve an external IP address, and create an external HTTP(S) load balancer.3. Enable Cloud CDN, and send traffic to your backend bucket.
questions.explanation: For globally accessible static content with minimal management overhead and maximum reliability, a multi-regional Standard Cloud Storage bucket fronted by an external HTTP(S) load balancer with Cloud CDN is the best fit. The multi-regional bucket replicates data across regions for high availability and low latency, Cloud Storage is fully managed (no VMs to operate), and Cloud CDN caches content at the edge close to users. Option C uses a regional bucket, which limits availability and increases latency for distant users. Options A and B rely on instance groups serving static files, which add significant management overhead and are unnecessary for static content; the unmanaged instance group in B also lacks autohealing and autoscaling.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Para conteúdo estático acessível globalmente com mínimo overhead de gerenciamento e máxima confiabilidade, um bucket Standard multirregional do Cloud Storage por trás de um external HTTP(S) load balancer com Cloud CDN é a melhor opção. O bucket multirregional replica os dados entre regiões para alta disponibilidade e baixa latência, o Cloud Storage é totalmente gerenciado (sem VMs para operar), e o Cloud CDN faz cache do conteúdo na borda, próximo aos usuários. A opção C usa um bucket regional, o que limita a disponibilidade e aumenta a latência para usuários distantes. As opções A e B dependem de instance groups servindo arquivos estáticos, o que adiciona overhead de gerenciamento significativo e é desnecessário para conteúdo estático; o unmanaged instance group em B também não possui autohealing nem autoscaling.

When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.Company Overview -HipLocal is a community application designed to facilitate communication between people in close proximity. It is used for event planning and organizing sporting events, and for businesses to connect with their local communities. HipLocal launched recently in a few neighborhoods in Dallas and is rapidly growing into a global phenomenon. Its unique style of hyper-local community communication and business outreach is in demand around the world.Executive Statement -We are the number one local community app; it's time to take our local community services global. Our venture capital investors want to see rapid growth and the same great experience for new local and virtual communities that come online, whether their members are 10 or 10000 miles away from each other.Solution Concept -HipLocal wants to expand their existing service, with updated functionality, in new regions to better serve their global customers. They want to hire and train a new team to support these regions in their time zones. They will need to ensure that the application scales smoothly and provides clear uptime data, and that they analyze and respond to any issues that occur.Existing Technical Environment -HipLocal's environment is a mix of on-premises hardware and infrastructure running in Google Cloud Platform. The HipLocal team understands their application well, but has limited experience in global scale applications. Their existing technical environment is as follows:• Existing APIs run on Compute Engine virtual machine instances hosted in GCP.• State is stored in a single instance MySQL database in GCP.• Release cycles include development freezes to allow for QA testing.• The application has no logging.• Applications are manually deployed by infrastructure engineers during periods of slow traffic on weekday evenings.• There are basic indicators of uptime; alerts are frequently fired when the APIs are unresponsive.Business Requirements -HipLocal's investors want to expand their footprint and support the increase in demand they are seeing. Their requirements are:• Expand availability of the application to new regions.• Support 10x as many concurrent users.• Ensure a consistent experience for users when they travel to different regions.• Obtain user activity metrics to better understand how to monetize their product.• Ensure compliance with regulations in the new regions (for example, GDPR).• Reduce infrastructure management time and cost.• Adopt the Google-recommended practices for cloud computing.○ Develop standardized workflows and processes around application lifecycle management.○ Define service level indicators (SLIs) and service level objectives (SLOs).Technical Requirements -• Provide secure communications between the on-premises data center and cloud-hosted applications and infrastructure.• The application must provide usage metrics and monitoring.• APIs require authentication and authorization.• Implement faster and more accurate validation of new features.• Logging and performance metrics must provide actionable information to be able to provide debugging information and alerts.• Must scale to meet user demand.For this question refer to the HipLocal case study.HipLocal wants to reduce the latency of their services for users in global locations. They have created read replicas of their database in locations where their users reside and configured their service to read traffic using those replicas. How should they further reduce latency for all database interactions with the least amount of effort?

options.text: Migrate the database to Bigtable and use it to serve all global user traffic.
Migrate the database to Cloud Spanner and use it to serve all global user traffic.
Migrate the database to Firestore in Datastore mode and use it to serve all global user traffic.
Migrate the services to Google Kubernetes Engine and use a load balancer service to better scale the application.

questions.correct_text: Migrate the database to Cloud Spanner and use it to serve all global user traffic.
questions.explanation: Cloud Spanner provides a horizontally scalable, strongly consistent relational database with multi-region configurations that deliver low-latency reads and writes globally, eliminating the need to manually manage read replicas while preserving SQL semantics close to the existing MySQL model. Because HipLocal already uses a relational MySQL database, migrating to Spanner is the lowest-effort path that reduces latency for all interactions, including writes, not just reads. Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column store unsuitable for relational query patterns and transactional needs. Firestore in Datastore mode is also NoSQL and would require substantial data-model rework, while moving services to GKE addresses compute scaling but does nothing to reduce database latency.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Spanner oferece um banco de dados relacional horizontalmente escalável e fortemente consistente, com configurações multirregionais que entregam leituras e gravações de baixa latência globalmente, eliminando a necessidade de gerenciar manualmente réplicas de leitura, ao mesmo tempo em que preserva a semântica SQL próxima ao modelo MySQL existente. Como a HipLocal já usa um banco de dados relacional MySQL, migrar para o Spanner é o caminho de menor esforço que reduz a latência de todas as interações, incluindo gravações, e não apenas leituras. O Bigtable é um armazenamento NoSQL wide-column inadequado para padrões de consulta relacionais e necessidades transacionais. O Firestore em modo Datastore também é NoSQL e exigiria uma reformulação substancial do modelo de dados, enquanto mover os serviços para o GKE resolve o escalonamento de computação, mas nada faz para reduzir a latência do banco de dados.

options.text: Cloud Profiler
Cloud Monitoring
Cloud Trace
Cloud Logging

questions.correct_text: Cloud Monitoring
questions.explanation: Cloud Monitoring is the Google Cloud product that lets you define and track service level indicators (SLIs) and service level objectives (SLOs), create uptime checks, and configure alerting policies, directly satisfying HipLocal's requirement to define SLIs and SLOs. Cloud Profiler (A) is for continuous CPU and memory profiling of application code, not for defining SLOs. Cloud Trace (C) provides distributed latency tracing across requests, which can feed metrics but does not manage SLOs. questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Monitoring é o produto do Google Cloud que permite definir e acompanhar service level indicators (SLIs) e service level objectives (SLOs), criar uptime checks e configurar políticas de alerta, atendendo diretamente ao requisito da HipLocal de definir SLIs e SLOs. O Cloud Profiler (A) serve para criar perfis contínuos de CPU e memória do código da aplicação, e não para definir SLOs. O Cloud Trace (C) fornece rastreamento distribuído de latência entre requisições, o que pode alimentar métricas, mas não gerencia SLOs. O Cloud Logging (D) centraliza dados de log e pode gerar métricas baseadas em logs, mas é o serviço de Monitoring que estabelece e avalia SLIs/SLOs em relação aos objetivos.

HipLocal needs to reduce the risk of these credentials being stolen. What should they do?

options.text: Create a service account and download its key. Use the key to authenticate to Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) to obtain the database credentials.
Create a service account and download its key. Use the key to authenticate to Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) to obtain a key used to decrypt the database credentials.
Create a service account and grant it the roles/iam.serviceAccountUser role. Impersonate as this account and authenticate using the Cloud SQL Proxy.
Grant the roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor role to the Compute Engine service account. Store and access the database credentials with the Secret Manager API.

questions.correct_text: Grant the roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor role to the Compute Engine service account. Store and access the database credentials with the Secret Manager API.
questions.explanation: Secret Manager is the Google-recommended service for securely storing and accessing sensitive data such as database credentials, replacing plaintext storage on persistent disks. By granting the Compute Engine service account the roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor role, the application can retrieve credentials at runtime using its attached identity and Application Default Credentials, with no downloaded keys to leak. Options A and B require downloading and distributing a service account key file, which reintroduces a long-lived credential that can itself be stolen, and KMS manages encryption keys rather than storing arbitrary secrets like passwords. Option C misuses roles/iam.serviceAccountUser and the Cloud SQL Proxy, which applies to Cloud SQL connectivity, not to credentials for a self-managed MySQL database on Compute Engine.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Secret Manager é o serviço recomendado pelo Google para armazenar e acessar com segurança dados sensíveis, como credenciais de banco de dados, substituindo o armazenamento em texto puro em discos persistentes. Ao conceder à conta de serviço do Compute Engine o papel roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor, a aplicação pode recuperar as credenciais em tempo de execução usando sua identidade anexada e o Application Default Credentials, sem chaves baixadas que possam vazar. As opções A e B exigem baixar e distribuir um arquivo de chave de conta de serviço, o que reintroduz uma credencial de longa duração que pode ela mesma ser roubada, e o KMS gerencia chaves de criptografia em vez de armazenar segredos arbitrários como senhas. A opção C faz uso indevido do roles/iam.serviceAccountUser e do Cloud SQL Proxy, que se aplicam à conectividade com o Cloud SQL, e não a credenciais de um banco de dados MySQL autogerenciado no Compute Engine.

They must capture additional data each time the application is launched in a new European country. This is causing delays in the development process due to constant schema changes and a lack of environments for conducting testing on the application changes. How should they resolve the issue while meeting the business requirements?

options.text: Create new Cloud SQL instances in Europe and North America for testing and deployment. Provide developers with local MySQL instances to conduct testing on the application changes.
Migrate data to Bigtable. Instruct the development teams to use the Cloud SDK to emulate a local Bigtable development environment.

Move from Cloud SQL to MySQL hosted on Compute Engine. Replicate hosts across regions in the Americas and Europe. Provide developers with local MySQL instances to conduct testing on the application changes.

Migrate data to Firestore in Native mode and set up instances in Europe and North America. Instruct the development teams to use the Cloud SDK to emulate a local Firestore in Native mode development environment.

questions.correct_text: Migrate data to Firestore in Native mode and set up instances in Europe and North America. Instruct the development teams to use the Cloud SDK to emulate a local Firestore in Native mode development environment.
questions.explanation: Firestore in Native mode is a fully managed, serverless NoSQL document database with a flexible schema, so adding new fields per country avoids the disruptive schema-migration delays of a relational system, and it offers multi-region locations plus a local emulator in the Cloud SDK for testing. This directly resolves the frequent schema changes and the lack of testing environments while reducing infrastructure management. Option A keeps Cloud SQL's rigid relational schema, so constant schema changes still cause delays. Option C moves to self-managed MySQL on Compute Engine, increasing operational burden and retaining schema rigidity. Bigtable (B) is a wide-column store optimized for high-throughput analytical or time-series workloads and lacks the document/query model and multi-region transactional semantics suited to this application data.

questions.explanation_pt: O Firestore em modo Native é um banco de dados de documentos NoSQL totalmente gerenciado e serverless, com schema flexível, de modo que adicionar novos campos por país evita os atrasos disruptivos de migração de schema de um sistema relacional, e ele oferece localizações multirregionais além de um emulador local no Cloud SDK para testes. Isso resolve diretamente as frequentes mudanças de schema e a falta de ambientes de teste, ao mesmo tempo em que reduz o gerenciamento de infraestrutura. A opção A mantém o schema relacional rígido do Cloud SQL, de modo que mudanças constantes de schema ainda causam atrasos. A opção C migra para um MySQL autogerenciado no Compute Engine, aumentando a carga operacional e mantendo a rigidez do schema. O Bigtable (B) é um armazenamento wide-column otimizado para cargas de trabalho analíticas ou de séries temporais de alto throughput, e carece do modelo de documento/consulta e da semântica transacional multirregional adequados aos dados desta aplicação.

questions.question: You are writing from a Go application to a Cloud Spanner database. You want to optimize your application’s performance using Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Write to Cloud Spanner using Cloud Client Libraries.
Write to Cloud Spanner using Google API Client Libraries
Write to Cloud Spanner using a custom gRPC client library.
Write to Cloud Spanner using a third-party HTTP client library.

questions.correct_text: Write to Cloud Spanner using Cloud Client Libraries.
questions.explanation: Google recommends using the Cloud Client Libraries for Cloud Spanner because they are idiomatic for each language (including Go), built on gRPC for efficient communication, and include built-in session pooling, retries, and performance optimizations. The Google API Client Libraries (B) are auto-generated, lower-level wrappers that do not provide the same Spanner-specific optimizations and are generally discouraged when a Cloud Client Library exists. Writing a custom gRPC client (C) forces you to reimplement session management, retries, and best practices, adding risk and effort. A third-party HTTP client (D) bypasses the recommended gRPC transport entirely and would be inefficient and unsupported.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Google recomenda usar as Cloud Client Libraries para o Cloud Spanner porque são idiomáticas para cada linguagem (incluindo Go), construídas sobre gRPC para comunicação eficiente e incluem pooling de sessões, retries e otimizações de desempenho embutidos. As Google API Client Libraries (B) são wrappers autogerados de nível mais baixo que não oferecem as mesmas otimizações específicas do Spanner e geralmente são desencorajadas quando existe uma Cloud Client Library. Escrever um cliente gRPC personalizado (C) obriga você a reimplementar o gerenciamento de sessões, retries e boas práticas, adicionando risco e esforço. Um cliente HTTP de terceiros (D) ignora completamente o transporte gRPC recomendado e seria ineficiente e sem suporte.

questions.question: You have an application deployed in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You need to update the application to make authorized requests to Google Cloud managed services. You want this to be a one-time setup, and you need to follow security best practices of auto-rotating your security keys and storing them in an encrypted store. You already created a service account with appropriate access to the Google Cloud service. What should you do next?

options.text: Assign the Google Cloud service account to your GKE Pod using Workload Identity.
Export the Google Cloud service account, and share it with the Pod as a Kubernetes Secret.
Export the Google Cloud service account, and embed it in the source code of the application.
Export the Google Cloud service account, and upload it to HashiCorp Vault to generate a dynamic service account for your application.

questions.correct_text: Assign the Google Cloud service account to your GKE Pod using Workload Identity.
questions.explanation: Workload Identity is the Google-recommended way for GKE workloads to authenticate to Google Cloud services: it binds a Kubernetes service account to a Google Cloud service account so Pods obtain short-lived, automatically rotated credentials without any exported key files. This satisfies the one-time setup, auto-rotation, and secure (no plaintext key) requirements. Exporting the service account key and storing it as a Kubernetes Secret (B) creates a long-lived credential that must be manually rotated and is only base64-encoded by default, not strongly encrypted. Embedding the key in source code (C) is a severe security anti-pattern. Using HashiCorp Vault (D) adds an external dependency and still relies on exporting a Google Cloud key, whereas Workload Identity is the native, simpler, key-free solution.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Workload Identity é a forma recomendada pelo Google para que workloads do GKE se autentiquem em serviços do Google Cloud: ele vincula uma service account do Kubernetes a uma service account do Google Cloud, de modo que os Pods obtêm credenciais de curta duração e rotacionadas automaticamente, sem nenhum arquivo de chave exportado. Isso atende aos requisitos de configuração única, rotação automática e segurança (sem chave em texto plano). Exportar a chave da service account e armazená-la como um Kubernetes Secret (B) cria uma credencial de longa duração que precisa ser rotacionada manualmente e que, por padrão, é apenas codificada em base64, não criptografada de forma robusta. Embutir a chave no código-fonte (C) é um grave antipadrão de segurança. Usar o HashiCorp Vault (D) adiciona uma dependência externa e ainda depende de exportar uma chave do Google Cloud, enquanto o Workload Identity é a solução nativa, mais simples e sem chaves.

questions.question: You are planning to deploy hundreds of microservices in your Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. How should you secure communication between the microservices on GKE using a managed service?

options.text: Use global HTTP(S) Load Balancing with managed SSL certificates to protect your services
Deploy open source Istio in your GKE cluster, and enable mTLS in your Service Mesh
Install cert-manager on GKE to automatically renew the SSL certificates.
Install Anthos Service Mesh, and enable mTLS in your Service Mesh.

questions.correct_text: Install Anthos Service Mesh, and enable mTLS in your Service Mesh.
questions.explanation: Anthos Service Mesh (now Cloud Service Mesh) is the Google-managed service mesh based on Istio, and enabling mutual TLS (mTLS) in the mesh transparently encrypts and authenticates all service-to-service traffic, which is exactly what is needed to secure communication between hundreds of microservices on GKE. Option B (open source Istio) also supports mTLS but is self-managed, contradicting the requirement for a managed service. Options A and C only secure the external/north-south edge: global HTTP(S) Load Balancing with managed SSL and cert-manager protect inbound client traffic but do nothing for internal east-west traffic between microservices.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Anthos Service Mesh (agora Cloud Service Mesh) é o service mesh gerenciado pelo Google baseado no Istio, e habilitar o mutual TLS (mTLS) no mesh criptografa e autentica de forma transparente todo o tráfego entre serviços, que é exatamente o que se precisa para proteger a comunicação entre centenas de microsserviços no GKE. A opção B (Istio open source) também suporta mTLS, mas é autogerenciada, contradizendo o requisito de um serviço gerenciado. As opções A e C protegem apenas a borda externa/norte-sul: o global HTTP(S) Load Balancing com SSL gerenciado e o cert-manager protegem o tráfego de entrada dos clientes, mas não fazem nada pelo tráfego interno leste-oeste entre os microsserviços.

questions.question: You are developing an application that will store and access sensitive unstructured data objects in a Cloud Storage bucket. To comply with regulatory requirements, you need to ensure that all data objects are available for at least 7 years after their initial creation. Objects created more than 3 years ago are accessed very infrequently (less than once a year). You need to configure object storage while ensuring that storage cost is optimized. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Set a retention policy on the bucket with a period of 7 years.
Use IAM Conditions to provide access to objects 7 years after the object creation date.
Enable Object Versioning to prevent objects from being accidentally deleted for 7 years after object creation.
Create an object lifecycle policy on the bucket that moves objects from Standard Storage to Archive Storage after 3 years.

Implement a Cloud Function that checks the age of each object in the bucket and moves the objects older than 3 years to a second bucket with the Archive Storage class. Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger the Cloud Function on a daily schedule.

questions.correct_text: Set a retention policy on the bucket with a period of 7 years. | Create an object lifecycle policy on the bucket that moves objects from Standard Storage to Archive Storage after 3 years.
questions.explanation: A retention policy with a 7-year period (A) enforces the regulatory requirement that objects cannot be deleted or overwritten until 7 years after creation, guaranteeing availability for the mandated period. An object lifecycle policy that transitions objects from Standard to Archive Storage after 3 years (D) optimizes cost because Archive is the cheapest class and matches the access pattern of less than once per year for older objects. IAM Conditions (B) controls access, not durability or retention, and would not preserve data. Object Versioning (C) keeps prior versions but does not prevent deletion of the live object or guarantee a retention period. A custom Cloud Function plus Scheduler (E) reinvents what native lifecycle management does for free, adding operational overhead and cost.

Uma política de object lifecycle que transita os objetos de Standard para Archive Storage após 3 anos (D) otimiza custos, pois Archive é a classe mais barata e corresponde ao padrão de acesso de menos de uma vez por ano para objetos mais antigos. As IAM Conditions (B) controlam o acesso, não a durabilidade ou a retenção, e não preservariam os dados. O Object Versioning (C) mantém versões anteriores, mas não impede a exclusão do objeto ativo nem garante um período de retenção. Uma Cloud Function customizada junto com o Scheduler (E) reinventa o que o gerenciamento nativo de lifecycle faz gratuitamente, adicionando custo e sobrecarga operacional.

questions.question: You are developing an application using different microservices that must remain internal to the cluster. You want the ability to configure each microservice with a specific number of replicas. You also want the ability to address a specific microservice from any other microservice in a uniform way, regardless of the number of replicas the microservice scales to. You plan to implement this solution on Google Kubernetes Engine. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy each microservice as a Deployment. Expose the Deployment in the cluster using a Service, and use the Service DNS name to address it from other microservices within the cluster.
Deploy each microservice as a Deployment. Expose the Deployment in the cluster using an Ingress, and use the Ingress IP address to address the Deployment from other microservices within the cluster.
Deploy each microservice as a Pod. Expose the Pod in the cluster using a Service, and use the Service DNS name to address the microservice from other microservices within the cluster.
Deploy each microservice as a Pod. Expose the Pod in the cluster using an Ingress, and use the Ingress IP address to address the Pod from other microservices within the cluster.

questions.correct_text: Deploy each microservice as a Deployment. Expose the Deployment in the cluster using a Service, and use the Service DNS name to address it from other microservices within the cluster.
questions.explanation: Deploying each microservice as a Deployment (A) lets you declaratively set the number of replicas per microservice and provides self-healing and rolling updates. Exposing each Deployment with a Service gives a stable cluster-internal DNS name and ClusterIP that load-balances across all current replicas, so other microservices can address it uniformly regardless of scaling. Options C and D use bare Pods, which lack replica management and are not recommended for scalable services. Options B and D rely on Ingress, which is designed for external HTTP(S) routing into the cluster rather than uniform internal service-to-service discovery.

questions.explanation_pt: Implantar cada microsserviço como um Deployment (A) permite definir de forma declarativa o número de réplicas por microsserviço e oferece auto-recuperação e atualizações graduais (rolling updates). Expor cada Deployment com um Service fornece um nome DNS estável dentro do cluster e um ClusterIP que distribui a carga entre todas as réplicas atuais, de modo que outros microsserviços possam acessá-lo de forma uniforme, independentemente do escalonamento. As opções C e D usam Pods isolados, que não têm gerenciamento de réplicas e não são recomendados para serviços escaláveis. As opções B e D dependem de Ingress, que foi projetado para roteamento HTTP(S) externo para dentro do cluster, e não para a descoberta interna uniforme entre serviços.

questions.question: You are building an application that uses a distributed microservices architecture. You want to measure the performance and system resource utilization in one of the microservices written in Java. What should you do?

options.text: Instrument the service with Cloud Profiler to measure CPU utilization and method-level execution times in the service.
Instrument the service with Debugger to investigate service errors.
Instrument the service with Cloud Trace to measure request latency.
Instrument the service with OpenCensus to measure service latency, and write custom metrics to Cloud Monitoring.

questions.correct_text: Instrument the service with Cloud Profiler to measure CPU utilization and method-level execution times in the service.
questions.explanation: Cloud Profiler (A) is purpose-built for continuous, low-overhead profiling of CPU and memory consumption and method-level execution times in production code, including Java, which directly answers the need to measure performance and system resource utilization within a microservice. Debugger (B) inspects application state at runtime to investigate code behavior, not resource utilization. Cloud Trace (C) and OpenCensus (D) focus on distributed request latency and tracing across services rather than per-method CPU and resource usage inside a single service, so they do not measure system resource utilization as required.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Profiler (A) foi projetado especificamente para profiling contínuo e de baixo overhead do consumo de CPU e memória e dos tempos de execução por método em código de produção, incluindo Java, o que responde diretamente à necessidade de medir desempenho e utilização de recursos do sistema dentro de um microsserviço. O Debugger (B) inspeciona o estado da aplicação em tempo de execução para investigar o comportamento do código, não a utilização de recursos. O Cloud Trace (C) e o OpenCensus (D) focam na latência de requisições distribuídas e no rastreamento entre serviços, e não no uso de CPU e recursos por método dentro de um único serviço, de modo que não medem a utilização de recursos do sistema como exigido.

questions.question: Your team is responsible for maintaining an application that aggregates news articles from many different sources. Your monitoring dashboard contains publicly accessible real-time reports and runs on a Compute Engine instance as a web application. External stakeholders and analysts need to access these reports via a secure channel without authentication. How should you configure this secure channel?

options.text: Add a public IP address to the instance. Use the service account key of the instance to encrypt the traffic.
Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger Cloud Build every hour to create an export from the reports. Store the reports in a public Cloud Storage bucket.
Add an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the monitoring dashboard. Configure Identity-Aware Proxy to secure the communication channel.
Add an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the monitoring dashboard. Set up a Google-managed SSL certificate on the load balancer for traffic encryption.

questions.correct_text: Add an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the monitoring dashboard. Set up a Google-managed SSL certificate on the load balancer for traffic encryption.
questions.explanation: Because the reports must be publicly accessible without authentication but over a secure (encrypted) channel, placing an HTTP(S) load balancer in front of the dashboard and attaching a Google-managed SSL certificate (D) provides TLS encryption in transit while still allowing unauthenticated access. Identity-Aware Proxy (C) is the opposite of the requirement: it enforces authentication and would block anonymous external users. Exporting to a public Cloud Storage bucket (B) changes the architecture away from the live web application and loses the real-time aspect. Using a service account key to encrypt traffic (A) is not how transport security works and would not provide a valid HTTPS channel.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Como os relatórios precisam ser acessíveis publicamente sem autenticação, mas por um canal seguro (criptografado), colocar um HTTP(S) load balancer na frente do dashboard e anexar um certificado SSL gerenciado pelo Google (D) fornece criptografia TLS em trânsito, permitindo ainda o acesso não autenticado. O Identity-Aware Proxy (C) é o oposto do requisito: ele força a autenticação e bloquearia usuários externos anônimos. Exportar para um bucket público do Cloud Storage (B) afasta a arquitetura da aplicação web ativa e perde o aspecto em tempo real. Usar uma chave de service account para criptografar o tráfego (A) não é como a segurança de transporte funciona e não forneceria um canal HTTPS válido.

questions.question: You are planning to add unit tests to your application. You need to be able to assert that published Pub/Sub messages are processed by your subscriber in order. You want the unit tests to be cost-effective and reliable. What should you do?

options.text: Implement a mocking framework.
Create a topic and subscription for each tester.
Add a filter by tester to the subscription.
Use the Pub/Sub emulator.

questions.correct_text: Use the Pub/Sub emulator.
questions.explanation: The Pub/Sub emulator runs locally and lets you publish and consume messages without touching production resources or incurring cost, making it ideal for reliable, cost-effective unit and integration tests of ordered message processing. With ordering keys configured, the emulator behaves like the real service so you can assert that the subscriber processes messages in order. A mocking framework only simulates your own code's expectations and would not faithfully reproduce Pub/Sub delivery and ordering semantics. Creating a topic and subscription per tester uses real (billable) cloud resources and adds management overhead, and subscription filters select messages by attribute rather than guaranteeing or testing ordering.
