questions.explanation_pt: Um framework de teste de carga distribuído implantado no GKE atende a todos os requisitos: ele pode gerar várias threads paralelas, produzir tráfego a partir de muitos Pods (e, portanto, muitos IPs de origem entre os nós) e escalar horizontalmente adicionando mais Pods conforme a demanda de carga aumenta. O padrão recomendado pelo Google para testes de carga distribuídos usa um framework baseado em containers no Kubernetes justamente por causa dessa elasticidade. cURL em managed ou unmanaged instance groups (A, B) é uma ferramenta simplista de requisição única, que não foi projetada para geração de carga orquestrada e escalável. Executar instâncias de container sequencialmente no Cloud Shell (D) é severamente limitado em recursos e não consegue produzir uma carga realista, paralela, com múltiplas origens e escalável.

questions.question: Your team is creating a serverless web application on Cloud Run. The application needs to access images stored in a private Cloud Storage bucket. You want to give the application Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission to access the images in the bucket, while also securing the services using Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Enforce signed URLs for the desired bucket. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the Compute Engine default service account.
Enforce public access prevention for the desired bucket. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the Compute Engine default service account.

Enforce signed URLs for the desired bucket. Create and update the Cloud Run service to use a user-managed service account. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the service account.

Enforce public access prevention for the desired bucket. Create and update the Cloud Run service to use a user-managed service account. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the service account.

questions.correct_text: Enforce public access prevention for the desired bucket. Create and update the Cloud Run service to use a user-managed service account. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the service account.
questions.explanation: The Google-recommended best practice is to run the Cloud Run service with a dedicated user-managed service account rather than the default Compute Engine service account, granting only the minimal Storage Object Viewer role on the bucket to that service account (least privilege). Enforcing public access prevention ensures the bucket can never be exposed publicly, which is the correct security control for private images accessed via IAM. Signed URLs (A, C) are for granting temporary access to clients without IAM credentials and are unnecessary when the application itself uses its service account identity to read the bucket. Using the default Compute Engine service account (A, B) violates least-privilege principles because it is broadly shared and over-permissioned, making option D the most secure and correct choice.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: A prática recomendada pelo Google é executar o serviço do Cloud Run com uma service account dedicada gerenciada pelo usuário, em vez da service account padrão do Compute Engine, concedendo apenas o papel mínimo de Storage Object Viewer no bucket para essa service account (princípio do menor privilégio). Aplicar a public access prevention garante que o bucket nunca possa ser exposto publicamente, que é o controle de segurança correto para imagens privadas acessadas via IAM. As Signed URLs (A, C) servem para conceder acesso temporário a clientes sem credenciais IAM e são desnecessárias quando a própria aplicação usa a identidade da sua service account para ler o bucket. Usar a service account padrão do Compute Engine (A, B) viola os princípios de menor privilégio, pois ela é amplamente compartilhada e tem permissões excessivas, tornando a opção D a escolha mais segura e correta.

questions.question: You are using Cloud Run to host a global ecommerce web application. Your company’s design team is creating a new color scheme for the web app. You have been tasked with determining whether the new color scheme will increase sales. You want to conduct testing on live production traffic. How should you design the study?

options.text: Use an external HTTP(S) load balancer to route a predetermined percentage of traffic to two different color schemes of your application. Analyze the results to determine whether there is a statistically significant difference in sales.

Use an external HTTP(S) load balancer to route traffic to the original color scheme while the new deployment is created and tested. After testing is complete, reroute all traffic to the new color scheme. Analyze the results to determine whether there is a statistically significant difference in sales.
Use an external HTTP(S) load balancer to mirror traffic to the new version of your application. Analyze the results to determine whether there is a statistically significant difference in sales.
Enable a feature flag that displays the new color scheme to half of all users. Monitor sales to see whether they increase for this group of users.

questions.correct_text: Use an external HTTP(S) load balancer to route a predetermined percentage of traffic to two different color schemes of your application. Analyze the results to determine whether there is a statistically significant difference in sales.
questions.explanation: To compare two variants on live production traffic and measure their effect on sales, you need an A/B test: route a predetermined percentage of traffic to each color scheme simultaneously and analyze for a statistically significant difference. An external HTTP(S) load balancer with weighted traffic splitting to two Cloud Run revisions achieves this controlled split. Deploying then rerouting all traffic afterward (B) is a sequential cutover, not a concurrent comparison, so external factors over time confound the sales analysis. Traffic mirroring (C) sends copied requests to the new version for testing but does not serve its responses to real users, so it cannot measure actual user purchasing behavior. A feature flag (D) could work conceptually but lacks the controlled, infrastructure-level percentage splitting and is not the load-balancer-based approach described as the recommended design here.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: Para comparar duas variantes no tráfego de produção ao vivo e medir o efeito delas nas vendas, você precisa de um teste A/B: rotear simultaneamente uma porcentagem predeterminada do tráfego para cada esquema de cores e analisar se há uma diferença estatisticamente significativa. Um external HTTP(S) load balancer com divisão de tráfego ponderada para duas revisões do Cloud Run alcança essa divisão controlada. Implantar e depois redirecionar todo o tráfego em seguida (B) é uma migração sequencial, não uma comparação simultânea, então fatores externos ao longo do tempo distorcem a análise de vendas. O traffic mirroring (C) envia cópias das requisições para a nova versão para teste, mas não entrega as respostas dela a usuários reais, então não consegue medir o comportamento de compra real dos usuários. Uma feature flag (D) poderia funcionar conceitualmente, mas não tem a divisão percentual controlada em nível de infraestrutura e não é a abordagem baseada em load balancer descrita aqui como o design recomendado.

questions.question: You are a lead developer working on a new retail system that runs on Cloud Run and Firestore. A web UI requirement is for the user to be able to browse through all products. A few months after go-live, you notice that Cloud Run instances are terminated with HTTP 500: Container instances are exceeding memory limits errors during busy times. This error coincides with spikes in the number of Firestore queries.You need to prevent Cloud Run from crashing and decrease the number of Firestore queries. You want to use a solution that optimizes system performance. What should you do?

options.text: Modify the query that returns the product list using cursors with limits.
Create a custom index over the products.
Modify the query that returns the product list using integer offsets.
Modify the Cloud Run configuration to increase the memory limits.

questions.correct_text: Modify the query that returns the product list using cursors with limits.
questions.explanation: Loading an entire product collection into memory causes the Cloud Run container to exceed its memory limit, and unbounded queries also drive up Firestore reads. Using query cursors with limits paginates the results, fetching only a small page at a time, which bounds memory usage and reduces the number of documents read per query. Integer offsets (C) still read and discard all skipped documents, so they do not reduce Firestore load and actually cost more. A custom index (B) only speeds up filtering/ordering and does not limit result size, and simply increasing memory (D) treats the symptom rather than the inefficient query pattern.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Carregar uma coleção inteira de produtos na memória faz o container do Cloud Run exceder seu limite de memória, e consultas sem limites também aumentam as leituras do Firestore. Usar query cursors com limites pagina os resultados, buscando apenas uma pequena página por vez, o que limita o uso de memória e reduz o número de documentos lidos por consulta. Offsets inteiros (C) ainda leem e descartam todos os documentos pulados, então não reduzem a carga no Firestore e, na verdade, custam mais. Um índice personalizado (B) só acelera a filtragem/ordenação e não limita o tamanho do resultado, e simplesmente aumentar a memória (D) trata o sintoma, e não o padrão de consulta ineficiente.

questions.question: You are a developer at a large organization. Your team uses Git for source code management (SCM). You want to ensure that your team follows Google-recommended best practices to manage code to drive higher rates of software delivery. Which SCM process should your team use?

options.text: Each developer commits their code to the main branch before each product release, conducts testing, and rolls back if integration issues are detected.
Each group of developers copies the repository, commits their changes to their repository, and merges their code into the main repository before each product release.
Each developer creates a branch for their own work, commits their changes to their branch, and merges their code into the main branch daily.

Each group of developers creates a feature branch from the main branch for their work, commits their changes to their branch, and merges their code into the main branch after the change advisory board approves it.

questions.correct_text: Each developer creates a branch for their own work, commits their changes to their branch, and merges their code into the main branch daily.
questions.explanation: Google's DORA guidance recommends short-lived feature branches created from main, with changes merged back after review/approval, which supports continuous integration while preserving governance such as a change advisory board sign-off. This balances frequent integration with quality gates and is the closest match to recommended practice among the options. Committing directly to main before each release (A) and relying on rollback invites broken builds and integration pain. Forking the whole repository per group (B) creates long-lived divergence and painful merges, the opposite of trunk-friendly flow. Long-lived per-developer branches without coordinated review can also drift, making option D the best described controlled feature-branch workflow.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: A orientação DORA do Google recomenda feature branches de curta duração criadas a partir da main, com as alterações mescladas de volta após revisão/aprovação, o que dá suporte à integração contínua ao mesmo tempo em que preserva a governança, como a aprovação de um change advisory board. Isso equilibra a integração frequente com quality gates e é a opção que mais se aproxima da prática recomendada. Fazer commit diretamente na main antes de cada release (A) e depender de rollback gera builds quebradas e dificuldades de integração. Fazer fork de todo o repositório por grupo (B) cria divergência de longa duração e merges dolorosos, o oposto de um fluxo amigável ao trunk. Branches por desenvolvedor de longa duração sem revisão coordenada também podem se distanciar, tornando a opção D o melhor fluxo controlado de feature branch descrito.

questions.question: You have a web application that publishes messages to Pub/Sub. You plan to build new versions of the application locally and want to quickly test Pub/Sub integration for each new build. How should you configure local testing?

options.text: Install Cloud Code on the integrated development environment (IDE). Navigate to Cloud APIs, and enable Pub/Sub against a valid Google Project ID. When developing locally, configure your application to call pubsub.googleapis.com.

Install the Pub/Sub emulator using gcloud, and start the emulator with a valid Google Project ID. When developing locally, configure your application to use the local emulator with ${gcloud beta emulators pubsub env-init}.
In the Google Cloud console, navigate to the API Library, and enable the Pub/Sub API. When developing locally, configure your application to call pubsub.googleapis.com.

Install the Pub/Sub emulator using gcloud, and start the emulator with a valid Google Project IWhen developing locally, configure your application to use the local emulator by exporting the PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST variable.

questions.correct_text: Install the Pub/Sub emulator using gcloud, and start the emulator with a valid Google Project ID. When developing locally, configure your application to use the local emulator with ${gcloud beta emulators pubsub env-init}.
questions.explanation: For fast, repeatable local testing of Pub/Sub integration, install the Pub/Sub emulator with gcloud and run your application against it. The correct way to point a client library at the emulator is to set the PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST environment variable, which the client libraries automatically detect and use instead of the live service. Options A and C configure the application to call the real pubsub.googleapis.com endpoint, which incurs cost, requires network access, and is not isolated local testing. Option B references a non-existent 'env-init' style invocation for Pub/Sub and does not correctly set PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST, so D is the accurate emulator configuration.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Para testes locais rápidos e repetíveis da integração com Pub/Sub, instale o emulador do Pub/Sub com o gcloud e execute sua aplicação contra ele. A forma correta de apontar uma client library para o emulador é definir a variável de ambiente PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST, que as client libraries detectam automaticamente e usam no lugar do serviço real. As opções A e C configuram a aplicação para chamar o endpoint real pubsub.googleapis.com, o que gera custo, requer acesso de rede e não é um teste local isolado. A opção B faz referência a uma invocação inexistente no estilo 'env-init' para o Pub/Sub e não define corretamente o PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST, portanto D é a configuração correta do emulador.

questions.question: Your ecommerce application receives external requests and forwards them to third-party API services for credit card processing, shipping, and inventory management as shown in the diagram.Your customers are reporting that your application is running slowly at unpredictable times. The application doesn’t report any metrics. You need to determine the cause of the inconsistent performance. What should you do?

options.text: Install the OpenTelemetry library for your respective language, and instrument your application.
Install the Ops Agent inside your container and configure it to gather application metrics.
Modify your application to read and forward the X-Cloud-Trace-Context header when it calls the downstream services.
Enable Managed Service for Prometheus on the Google Kubernetes Engine cluster to gather application metrics.

questions.correct_text: Install the OpenTelemetry library for your respective language, and instrument your application.
questions.explanation: The slowness occurs at unpredictable times across calls to multiple downstream third-party services, and the application emits no telemetry, so you need distributed tracing to see where latency accumulates across the request path. Installing the OpenTelemetry library and instrumenting the application captures spans and metrics that reveal which downstream call is slow, which is the recommended vendor-neutral instrumentation approach. Merely forwarding the X-Cloud-Trace-Context header (C) propagates a trace ID but does not generate or export the spans needed to analyze latency. The Ops Agent (B) and Managed Service for Prometheus (D) gather host or scraped metrics but do not provide the per-request distributed traces required to pinpoint the inconsistent downstream latency.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: A lentidão ocorre em momentos imprevisíveis nas chamadas a múltiplos serviços downstream de terceiros, e a aplicação não emite nenhuma telemetria, então você precisa de distributed tracing para ver onde a latência se acumula ao longo do caminho da requisição. Instalar a biblioteca OpenTelemetry e instrumentar a aplicação captura spans e métricas que revelam qual chamada downstream está lenta, sendo essa a abordagem de instrumentação recomendada e independente de fornecedor. Apenas encaminhar o header X-Cloud-Trace-Context (C) propaga um trace ID, mas não gera nem exporta os spans necessários para analisar a latência. O Ops Agent (B) e o Managed Service for Prometheus (D) coletam métricas de host ou via scraping, mas não fornecem os distributed traces por requisição necessários para identificar a latência inconsistente do downstream.

questions.question: You are developing a new application. You want the application to be triggered only when a given file is updated in your Cloud Storage bucket. Your trigger might change, so your process must support different types of triggers. You want the configuration to be simple so that multiple team members can update the triggers in the future. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Cloud Storage events to be sent to Pub/Sub, and use Pub/Sub events to trigger a Cloud Build job that executes your application.
Create an Eventarc trigger that monitors your Cloud Storage bucket for a specific filename, and set the target as Cloud Run.
Configure a Cloud Function that executes your application and is triggered when an object is updated in Cloud Storage.
Configure a Firebase function that executes your application and is triggered when an object is updated in Cloud Storage.

questions.correct_text: Create an Eventarc trigger that monitors your Cloud Storage bucket for a specific filename, and set the target as Cloud Run.
questions.explanation: Eventarc is the unified, declarative eventing service in Google Cloud, and it can match Cloud Storage events (such as object finalization or update) and route them to targets like Cloud Run. Because the trigger is defined as configuration, team members can easily create, modify, or swap trigger types without rewriting application code, satisfying the requirements for simplicity and flexibility. Option A wiring Cloud Storage to Pub/Sub and then Cloud Build is more complex to maintain and Cloud Build is intended for CI/CD pipelines, not as a general application runtime. Options C and D bind the application logic directly to a single Cloud Storage trigger type, making it harder to support different trigger types in the future, and Firebase functions are aimed at Firebase/mobile use cases rather than this general workload.

questions.question: You are defining your system tests for an application running in Cloud Run in a Google Cloud project. You need to create a testing environment that is isolated from the production environment. You want to fully automate the creation of the testing environment with the least amount of effort and execute automated tests. What should you do?

options.text: Using Cloud Build, execute Terraform scripts to create a new Google Cloud project and a Cloud Run instance of your application in the Google Cloud project.
Using Cloud Build, execute a Terraform script to deploy a new Cloud Run revision in the existing Google Cloud project. Use traffic splitting to send traffic to your test environment.
Using Cloud Build, execute gcloud commands to create a new Google Cloud project and a Cloud Run instance of your application in the Google Cloud project.
Using Cloud Build, execute gcloud commands to deploy a new Cloud Run revision in the existing Google Cloud project. Use traffic splitting to send traffic to your test environment.

questions.correct_text: Using Cloud Build, execute Terraform scripts to create a new Google Cloud project and a Cloud Run instance of your application in the Google Cloud project.
questions.explanation: Creating a brand-new Google Cloud project for the test environment provides true isolation from production, since IAM, quotas, and resources are scoped per project. Using Terraform invoked from Cloud Build gives a fully automated, repeatable, and declarative way to provision the project and Cloud Run service with minimal ongoing effort, and the state can be reused to tear the environment down. Options B and D deploy a new revision in the existing production project and rely on traffic splitting, which does not isolate the test environment and risks exposing test traffic alongside production. Option C uses imperative gcloud commands, which are harder to maintain idempotently than Terraform's declarative infrastructure-as-code approach.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: Criar um projeto totalmente novo no Google Cloud para o ambiente de teste proporciona isolamento real em relação à produção, já que IAM, quotas e recursos têm escopo por projeto. Usar o Terraform invocado a partir do Cloud Build oferece uma forma totalmente automatizada, repetível e declarativa de provisionar o projeto e o serviço do Cloud Run com mínimo esforço contínuo, e o state pode ser reutilizado para destruir o ambiente. As opções B e D implantam uma nova revisão no projeto de produção existente e dependem de traffic splitting, o que não isola o ambiente de teste e arrisca expor o tráfego de teste junto ao de produção. A opção C usa comandos imperativos do gcloud, que são mais difíceis de manter de forma idempotente do que a abordagem declarativa de infraestrutura como código do Terraform.

questions.question: You are a cluster administrator for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Your organization’s clusters are enrolled in a release channel. You need to be informed of relevant events that affect your GKE clusters, such as available upgrades and security bulletins. What should you do?

options.text: Configure cluster notifications to be sent to a Pub/Sub topic.
Execute a scheduled query against the google_cloud_release_notes BigQuery dataset.
Query the GKE API for available versions.
Create an RSS subscription to receive a daily summary of the GKE release notes.

questions.correct_text: Configure cluster notifications to be sent to a Pub/Sub topic.
questions.explanation: GKE cluster notifications can be configured to publish messages to a Pub/Sub topic, delivering structured events such as available upgrades, security bulletins, and other release-channel-relevant information automatically. This is the recommended, event-driven mechanism that lets you subscribe and react programmatically without polling. Querying the GKE API for versions (C) requires manual polling and does not surface security bulletins. RSS subscriptions (D) and BigQuery release-notes queries (B) are general informational sources that are not cluster-specific and are not the integrated notification channel for your enrolled clusters.

questions.explanation_pt: As notificações de cluster do GKE podem ser configuradas para publicar mensagens em um tópico do Pub/Sub, entregando automaticamente eventos estruturados como upgrades disponíveis, boletins de segurança e outras informações relevantes do release channel. Esse é o mecanismo recomendado, orientado a eventos, que permite inscrever-se e reagir de forma programática sem precisar fazer polling. Consultar a API do GKE em busca de versões (C) exige polling manual e não expõe boletins de segurança. Assinaturas RSS (D) e consultas a release notes no BigQuery (B) são fontes de informação genéricas, que não são específicas do cluster e não constituem o canal de notificação integrado para os clusters em que você está inscrito.

questions.question: You need to containerize a web application that will be hosted on Google Cloud behind a global load balancer with SSL certificates. You don’t have the time to develop authentication at the application level, and you want to offload SSL encryption and management from your application. You want to configure the architecture using managed services where possible. What should you do?

options.text: Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and deploy an NGINX Ingress Controller to handle authentication.
Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and deploy cert-manager to manage SSL certificates.
Host the application on Compute Engine, and configure Cloud Endpoints for your application.
Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) with Cloud Load Balancing and Google-managed certificates.

questions.correct_text: Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) with Cloud Load Balancing and Google-managed certificates.
questions.explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) provides application-level authentication without writing any auth code, and when combined with an external HTTP(S) load balancer using Google-managed SSL certificates, SSL termination and certificate lifecycle are fully offloaded to managed Google Cloud services. Hosting the containerized app on GKE behind this setup satisfies all requirements. Options A and B (NGINX Ingress Controller or cert-manager) require you to deploy and operate authentication/certificate tooling yourself, which is more effort and less managed. Cloud Endpoints (C) is an API management gateway and does not provide turnkey end-user authentication plus managed SSL offload in the way IAP with managed certificates does.

questions.question: You manage a system that runs on stateless Compute Engine VMs and Cloud Run instances. Cloud Run is connected to a VPC, and the ingress setting is set to Internal. You want to schedule tasks on Cloud Run. You create a service account and grant it the roles/run.invoker Identity and Access Management (IAM) role. When you create a schedule and test it, a 403 Permission Denied error is returned in Cloud Logging. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the service account the roles/run.developer IAM role.
Configure a cron job on the Compute Engine VMs to trigger Cloud Run on schedule.
Change the Cloud Run ingress setting to 'Internal and Cloud Load Balancing.'
Use Cloud Scheduler with Pub/Sub to invoke Cloud Run.

questions.correct_text: Use Cloud Scheduler with Pub/Sub to invoke Cloud Run.
questions.explanation: Because the Cloud Run service has ingress set to Internal, it only accepts traffic originating from inside the VPC or from internal sources; Cloud Scheduler's direct HTTP target call comes from outside the VPC and is rejected, producing the 403 even though the service account has roles/run.invoker. Routing the trigger through Pub/Sub solves this: Cloud Scheduler publishes to a topic on schedule, and a Pub/Sub push subscription (or Eventarc) delivers the message to the Cloud Run service via an internal path that satisfies the Internal ingress restriction. Granting roles/run.developer (A) only adds management permissions and does not change why the request is blocked. Using a cron job on the VMs (B) abandons the managed scheduling requirement and is fragile. Changing ingress to 'Internal and Cloud Load Balancing' (C) still does not admit Cloud Scheduler's direct external call without an internal load balancer fronting it, so the 403 persists.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Como o serviço do Cloud Run está com o ingress definido como Internal, ele só aceita tráfego originado de dentro da VPC ou de fontes internas; a chamada HTTP direta de destino do Cloud Scheduler vem de fora da VPC e é rejeitada, produzindo o 403 mesmo que a service account tenha o papel roles/run.invoker. Roteamento do gatilho através do Pub/Sub resolve isso: o Cloud Scheduler publica em um tópico conforme o agendamento, e uma push subscription do Pub/Sub (ou o Eventarc) entrega a mensagem ao serviço do Cloud Run por um caminho interno que satisfaz a restrição de ingress Internal. Conceder roles/run.developer (A) apenas adiciona permissões de gerenciamento e não muda o motivo pelo qual a requisição é bloqueada. Usar um cron job nas VMs (B) abandona o requisito de agendamento gerenciado e é frágil. Alterar o ingress para 'Internal and Cloud Load Balancing' (C) ainda não admite a chamada externa direta do Cloud Scheduler sem um internal load balancer à frente dele, então o 403 persiste.

questions.question: You work on an application that relies on Cloud Spanner as its main datastore. New application features have occasionally caused performance regressions. You want to prevent performance issues by running an automated performance test with Cloud Build for each commit made. If multiple commits are made at the same time, the tests might run concurrently. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new project with a random name for every build. Load the required data. Delete the project after the test is run.
Create a new Cloud Spanner instance for every build. Load the required data. Delete the Cloud Spanner instance after the test is run.
Create a project with a Cloud Spanner instance and the required data. Adjust the Cloud Build build file to automatically restore the data to its previous state after the test is run.
Start the Cloud Spanner emulator locally. Load the required data. Shut down the emulator after the test is run.

questions.correct_text: Create a new Cloud Spanner instance for every build. Load the required data. Delete the Cloud Spanner instance after the test is run.
questions.explanation: Concurrent Cloud Build runs require fully isolated Spanner data so tests do not interfere with each other, and creating a dedicated Cloud Spanner instance per build, loading data, then deleting it gives clean isolation without the overhead of provisioning whole projects. Creating a new project per build (A) is far heavier, slower, and harder to manage quota and cleanup for than spinning up a single instance. Restoring shared data after each test (C) breaks under concurrency because simultaneous builds would corrupt each other's state on the same instance. The Cloud Spanner emulator (D) does not faithfully reproduce production performance characteristics, so it cannot validate performance regressions, which is the entire purpose of the test.

questions.question: Your company's security team uses Identity and Access Management (IAM) to track which users have access to which resources. You need to create a version control system that can integrate with your security team's processes. You want your solution to support fast release cycles and frequent merges to your main branch to minimize merge conflicts. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Source Repositories repository, and use trunk-based development.
Create a Cloud Source Repositories repository, and use feature-based development.
Create a GitHub repository, mirror it to a Cloud Source Repositories repository, and use trunk-based development.
Create a GitHub repository, mirror it to a Cloud Source Repositories repository, and use feature-based development.

questions.correct_text: Create a Cloud Source Repositories repository, and use trunk-based development.
questions.explanation: Trunk-based development is the branching model designed for fast release cycles and frequent small merges to the main branch, which minimizes long-lived branches and the merge conflicts they cause. Cloud Source Repositories integrates natively with Google Cloud IAM, so the security team can track and control access to repositories directly, satisfying the requirement to integrate with their IAM-based processes. Feature-based (long-lived feature branch) development (B and D) encourages larger, less frequent merges and more conflicts, the opposite of the stated goal. Mirroring a GitHub repository (C and D) adds an external system whose access is not governed by Google Cloud IAM, weakening the security team's tracking; using Cloud Source Repositories directly keeps access control within IAM.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: O trunk-based development é o modelo de branching projetado para ciclos de release rápidos e merges pequenos e frequentes na branch principal, o que minimiza branches de longa duração e os conflitos de merge que elas causam. O Cloud Source Repositories integra-se nativamente com o Google Cloud IAM, então a equipe de segurança pode rastrear e controlar o acesso aos repositórios diretamente, atendendo ao requisito de integração com seus processos baseados em IAM. O desenvolvimento baseado em features (branches de feature de longa duração) (B e D) incentiva merges maiores e menos frequentes e mais conflitos, o oposto do objetivo declarado. Espelhar um repositório do GitHub (C e D) adiciona um sistema externo cujo acesso não é governado pelo Google Cloud IAM, enfraquecendo o rastreamento da equipe de segurança; usar o Cloud Source Repositories diretamente mantém o controle de acesso dentro do IAM.

questions.question: You recently developed an application that monitors a large number of stock prices. You need to configure Pub/Sub to receive messages and update the current stock price in an in-memory database. A downstream service needs the most up-to-date prices in the in-memory database to perform stock trading transactions. Each message contains three pieces or information:• Stock symbol• Stock price• Timestamp for the updateHow should you set up your Pub/Sub subscription?

options.text: Create a push subscription with exactly-once delivery enabled.
Create a pull subscription with both ordering and exactly-once delivery turned off.
Create a pull subscription with ordering enabled, using the stock symbol as the ordering key.
Create a push subscription with both ordering and exactly-once delivery turned off.

questions.correct_text: Create a pull subscription with ordering enabled, using the stock symbol as the ordering key.
questions.explanation: Because the downstream service needs the most up-to-date price per stock, messages for a given symbol must be processed in the order they were sent; a pull subscription with message ordering enabled using the stock symbol as the ordering key guarantees ordered delivery within each symbol while still allowing parallelism across symbols. Pull is appropriate for an application that maintains its own in-memory database and controls its consumption rate. Disabling ordering (B and D) risks applying an older price after a newer one, corrupting the current value. Exactly-once delivery (A) is not the core requirement here and a push subscription gives the consumer less control; ordering is what actually protects correctness, so the ordered pull subscription keyed on the symbol is the best fit.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: Como o serviço downstream precisa do preço mais atualizado por ação, as mensagens de um determinado símbolo devem ser processadas na ordem em que foram enviadas; uma pull subscription com message ordering habilitado, usando o símbolo da ação como ordering key, garante a entrega ordenada dentro de cada símbolo, ao mesmo tempo em que permite paralelismo entre símbolos diferentes. O modelo pull é apropriado para uma aplicação que mantém seu próprio banco de dados em memória e controla a taxa de consumo. Desabilitar o ordenamento (B e D) corre o risco de aplicar um preço mais antigo depois de um mais recente, corrompendo o valor atual. A entrega exactly-once (A) não é o requisito central aqui, e uma push subscription dá menos controle ao consumidor; o ordenamento é o que realmente protege a correção, então a pull subscription ordenada com chave no símbolo é a melhor opção.

questions.question: You are a developer at a social media company. The company runs their social media website on-premises and uses MySQL as a backend to store user profiles and user posts. Your company plans to migrate to Google Cloud, and your learn will migrate user profile information to Firestore. You are tasked with designing the Firestore collections. What should you do?

options.text: Create one root collection for user profiles, and create one root collection for user posts.
Create one root collection for user profiles, and create one subcollection for each user's posts.
Create one root collection for user profiles, and store each user's post as a nested list in the user profile document.
Create one root collection for user posts, and create one subcollection for each user's profile.

questions.correct_text: Create one root collection for user profiles, and create one subcollection for each user's posts.
questions.explanation: In Firestore, the one-to-many relationship between a user and that user's posts is best modeled with a root collection of user profile documents and a subcollection of posts under each profile document; subcollections scale without bloating the parent document and allow efficient, paginated queries of a single user's posts. Two unrelated root collections (A) loses the natural hierarchy and makes it harder to query a user's posts together. Storing posts as a nested list inside the profile document (C) hits Firestore's 1 MiB document size limit and forces rewrites of the whole document on every new post, which does not scale. Putting profiles as subcollections under posts (D) inverts the natural ownership relationship and is illogical, since a profile owns many posts rather than the reverse.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: No Firestore, o relacionamento um-para-muitos entre um usuário e os posts desse usuário é melhor modelado com uma coleção raiz de documentos de perfil de usuário e uma subcoleção de posts sob cada documento de perfil; subcoleções escalam sem inchar o documento pai e permitem consultas eficientes e paginadas dos posts de um único usuário. Duas coleções raiz não relacionadas (A) perde a hierarquia natural e dificulta consultar os posts de um usuário em conjunto. Armazenar os posts como uma lista aninhada dentro do documento de perfil (C) atinge o limite de tamanho de documento de 1 MiB do Firestore e força reescritas do documento inteiro a cada novo post, o que não escala. Colocar os perfis como subcoleções sob os posts (D) inverte o relacionamento natural de propriedade e é ilógico, já que um perfil possui muitos posts, e não o contrário.

questions.question: Your team recently deployed an application on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You are monitoring your application and want to be alerted when the average memory consumption of your containers is under 20% or above 80%. How should you configure the alerts?

options.text: Create a Cloud Function that consumes the Monitoring API. Create a schedule to trigger the Cloud Function hourly and alert you if the average memory consumption is outside the defined range.
In Cloud Monitoring, create an alerting policy to notify you if the average memory consumption is outside the defined range.
Create a Cloud Function that runs on a schedule, executes kubectl top on all the workloads on the cluster, and sends an email alert if the average memory consumption is outside the defined range.
Write a script that pulls the memory consumption of the instance at the OS level and sends an email alert if the average memory consumption is outside the defined range.

questions.correct_text: In Cloud Monitoring, create an alerting policy to notify you if the average memory consumption is outside the defined range.
questions.explanation: Cloud Monitoring natively collects GKE container metrics, including memory utilization, through the built-in metrics agent. The correct approach is to create an alerting policy directly in Cloud Monitoring that triggers a notification when average memory consumption falls outside the 20% to 80% range, which is the purpose-built, managed feature for this need. Option A using a scheduled Cloud Function polling the Monitoring API hourly is unnecessary custom work and adds latency and complexity. Options C and D reinvent monitoring by running kubectl top or OS-level scripts, which are fragile, do not scale, and duplicate what Cloud Monitoring already provides automatically.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Monitoring coleta nativamente as métricas de containers do GKE, incluindo utilização de memória, por meio do agente de métricas integrado. A abordagem correta é criar uma alerting policy diretamente no Cloud Monitoring que dispara uma notificação quando o consumo médio de memória sai da faixa de 20% a 80%, que é o recurso gerenciado e dedicado para essa necessidade. A opção A, que usa uma Cloud Function agendada consultando a Monitoring API a cada hora, é um trabalho personalizado desnecessário e adiciona latência e complexidade. As opções C e D reinventam o monitoramento executando kubectl top ou scripts no nível do SO, que são frágeis, não escalam e duplicam o que o Cloud Monitoring já fornece automaticamente.

questions.question: You manage a microservice-based ecommerce platform on Google Cloud that sends confirmation emails to a third-party email service provider using a Cloud Function. Your company just launched a marketing campaign, and some customers are reporting that they have not received order confirmation emails. You discover that the services triggering the Cloud Function are receiving HTTP 500 errors. You need to change the way emails are handled to minimize email loss. What should you do?

options.text: Increase the Cloud Function's timeout to nine minutes.
Configure the sender application to publish the outgoing emails in a message to a Pub/Sub topic. Update the Cloud Function configuration to consume the Pub/Sub queue.

Configure the sender application to write emails to Memorystore and then trigger the Cloud Function. When the function is triggered, it reads the email details from Memorystore and sends them to the email service.
Configure the sender application to retry the execution of the Cloud Function every one second if a request fails.

questions.correct_text: Configure the sender application to publish the outgoing emails in a message to a Pub/Sub topic. Update the Cloud Function configuration to consume the Pub/Sub queue.
questions.explanation: The HTTP 500 errors indicate that the synchronous call to the Cloud Function (and the downstream email provider) is failing, and because the request is synchronous those emails are lost. Decoupling the sender from the Cloud Function with a Pub/Sub topic provides durable, asynchronous message buffering with automatic retries and dead-lettering, so emails are retained and retried until successfully processed, minimizing loss. Increasing the timeout (A) does not address transient failures or buffering. Memorystore (C) is an in-memory cache that is not durable and is the wrong tool for guaranteed message delivery. A tight one-second retry loop (D) can overwhelm the failing service and still loses messages if the function or service stays down.

questions.explanation_pt: Os erros HTTP 500 indicam que a chamada síncrona à Cloud Function (e ao provedor de e-mail downstream) está falhando, e como a requisição é síncrona esses e-mails são perdidos. Desacoplar o remetente da Cloud Function com um tópico do Pub/Sub fornece um buffer de mensagens durável e assíncrono, com retentativas automáticas e dead-lettering, de modo que os e-mails são retidos e reprocessados até serem processados com sucesso, minimizando a perda. Aumentar o timeout (A) não resolve falhas transitórias nem o buffering. O Memorystore (C) é um cache em memória que não é durável e é a ferramenta errada para entrega garantida de mensagens. Um loop de retentativa apertado de um segundo (D) pode sobrecarregar o serviço que está falhando e ainda perde mensagens se a função ou o serviço continuar indisponível.

questions.question: Your team has created an application that is hosted on a Google Kubemetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You need to connect the application to a legacy REST service that is deployed in two GKE clusters in two different regions. You want to connect your application to the legacy service in a way that is resilient and requires the fewest number of steps. You also want to be able to run probe-based health checks on the legacy service on a separate port. How should you set up the connection? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Traffic Director with a sidecar proxy to connect the application to the service.
Set up a proxyless Traffic Director configuration for the application.
Configure the legacy service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the sidecar proxy.
Configure the legacy service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the application.
Configure the legacy service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the Traffic Director control plane.

questions.correct_text: Use Traffic Director with a sidecar proxy to connect the application to the service. | Configure the legacy service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the sidecar proxy.
questions.explanation: Traffic Director (Cloud Service Mesh) provides managed, resilient global service routing, and using it with an Envoy sidecar proxy lets the application connect to the multi-region legacy REST service with health checking and traffic management handled by the mesh, requiring the fewest steps. With the sidecar deployment model, health-check probes to the legacy service originate from the sidecar proxy, so the legacy service's firewall must be configured to allow health checks coming from the sidecar proxy (C), including the separate probe port. A proxyless configuration (B) would not provide the sidecar-based probing described and is less suitable here. Allowing health checks from the application (D) or directly from the Traffic Director control plane (E) is incorrect because the data-plane health checks are issued by the sidecar Envoy proxy.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: O Traffic Director (Cloud Service Mesh) fornece roteamento de serviço global gerenciado e resiliente, e usá-lo com um proxy sidecar Envoy permite que a aplicação se conecte ao serviço REST legado multirregião com health checking e gerenciamento de tráfego tratados pela mesh, exigindo o menor número de passos. Com o modelo de implantação por sidecar, as sondagens de health-check ao serviço legado se originam do proxy sidecar, então o firewall do serviço legado deve ser configurado para permitir health checks vindos do proxy sidecar (C), incluindo a porta de probe separada. Uma configuração proxyless (B) não forneceria a sondagem baseada em sidecar descrita e é menos adequada aqui. Permitir health checks vindos da aplicação (D) ou diretamente do control plane do Traffic Director (E) está incorreto, porque os health checks do data-plane são emitidos pelo proxy sidecar Envoy.

questions.question: You are developing a flower ordering application. Currently you have three microservices:• Order Service (receives the orders)• Order Fulfillment Service (processes the orders)• Notification Service (notifies the customer when the order is filled)You need to determine how the services will communicate with each other. You want incoming orders to be processed quickly and you need to collect order information for fulfillment. You also want to make sure orders are not lost between your services and are able to communicate asynchronously. How should the requests be processed?
questions.explanation: For loosely coupled microservices that must communicate asynchronously, process incoming orders quickly, and guarantee no message loss, Pub/Sub is the appropriate Google Cloud messaging service. Publishers (Order Service) write events to topics, and subscribers (Order Fulfillment and Notification Services) consume them independently with at-least-once delivery and durable storage, so orders are not lost if a downstream service is temporarily unavailable. This decoupling lets each service scale and fail independently while still capturing order information for fulfillment. Synchronous request/response patterns such as direct REST calls would tightly couple the services and risk losing orders if a consumer is down.

questions.explanation_pt: Para microsserviços fracamente acoplados que precisam se comunicar de forma assíncrona, processar pedidos recebidos rapidamente e garantir que nenhuma mensagem seja perdida, o Pub/Sub é o serviço de mensageria apropriado do Google Cloud. Os publishers (Order Service) gravam eventos em topics, e os subscribers (Order Fulfillment e Notification Services) os consomem de forma independente com entrega at-least-once e armazenamento durável, de modo que os pedidos não são perdidos se um serviço downstream estiver temporariamente indisponível. Esse desacoplamento permite que cada serviço escale e falhe de forma independente enquanto ainda captura as informações dos pedidos para o atendimento. Padrões síncronos de requisição/resposta, como chamadas REST diretas, acoplariam fortemente os serviços e correriam o risco de perder pedidos se um consumidor estivesse fora do ar.

questions.question: You recently deployed an application to GKE where Pods are writing files to a Compute Engine persistent disk. You have created a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) and a PersistentVolume (PV) object on Kubernetes for the disk, and you reference the PVC in the deployment manifest file.You recently expanded the size of the persistent disk because the application has used up almost all of the disk space. You have logged on to one of the Pods, and you notice that the disk expansion is not visible in the container file system. What should you do?

options.text: Set the spec.capacity.storage value of the PV object to match the size of the persistent disk. Apply the updated configuration by using kubectl.

Recreate the application Pods by running the kubectl delete deployment DEPLOYMENT_NAME && kubectl apply deployment.yaml command, where the DEPLOYMENT_NAME parameter is the name of your deployment and deployment.yaml is its manifest file.
Set the spec.resources.requests.storage value of the PVC object to match the size of the persistent disk. Apply the updated configuration by using kubectl.
In the Pod, resize the disk partition to the maximum value by using the fdisk or parted utility.

questions.correct_text: Set the spec.resources.requests.storage value of the PVC object to match the size of the persistent disk. Apply the updated configuration by using kubectl.
questions.explanation: In GKE, the size of a PersistentVolume backed by a Compute Engine persistent disk is driven by the PersistentVolumeClaim. To grow the volume after expanding the underlying disk, you edit the PVC's spec.resources.requests.storage to the new size and apply it; if the StorageClass allows volume expansion, Kubernetes resizes the volume and the filesystem so the new capacity becomes visible in the container. Editing the PV's spec.capacity.storage directly (A) is not the supported expansion path and does not trigger the filesystem grow. Deleting and recreating the deployment (B) does not change the requested storage size. Manually running fdisk or parted inside the Pod (D) is unsupported, dangerous, and bypasses Kubernetes' managed resize workflow.

topics.exam_domain_name: Configurar aplicações cloud-native para deployment

questions.explanation_pt: No GKE, o tamanho de um PersistentVolume baseado em um persistent disk do Compute Engine é definido pelo PersistentVolumeClaim. Para aumentar o volume após expandir o disco subjacente, você edita o spec.resources.requests.storage do PVC para o novo tamanho e o aplica; se a StorageClass permitir a expansão de volume, o Kubernetes redimensiona o volume e o filesystem, de modo que a nova capacidade fique visível no container. Editar diretamente o spec.capacity.storage do PV (A) não é o caminho de expansão suportado e não dispara o crescimento do filesystem. Excluir e recriar o deployment (B) não altera o tamanho de armazenamento solicitado. Executar manualmente fdisk ou parted dentro do Pod (D) não é suportado, é perigoso e ignora o fluxo de redimensionamento gerenciado do Kubernetes.

questions.question: You work for an ecommerce company. You are designing a new Orders API that will be exposed through Apigee. In your Apigee organization, you created two new environments named orders-test and orders-prod. You plan to use unique URLs named test.lnk-42.com/api/v1/orders and Ink-42.com/api/v1/orders for each environment. You need to ensure that each environment only uses the assigned URL. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Attach orders-test and orders-prod to the orders environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment.
1. Attach orders-test and orders-prod to the orders environment group.2. Add each hostname to the orders environment group.
1. Attach orders-test to the test environment group, and attach orders-prod to the production environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment.
1. Attach orders-test to the test environment group, and attach orders-prod to the production environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment group.

questions.correct_text: 1. Attach orders-test to the test environment group, and attach orders-prod to the production environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment group.
questions.explanation: In Apigee X, hostnames (custom domains) are configured on environment groups, not on individual environments, and environments are attached to environment groups to route traffic. To give each environment a distinct URL, you attach orders-test and orders-prod to separate environment groups (test and production) and assign the appropriate hostname to each environment group. This ensures each environment is reachable only through its assigned URL. Options that attach both environments to a single group (A, B) cannot isolate hostnames per environment, and option C incorrectly adds hostnames to environments rather than to environment groups.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: No Apigee X, os hostnames (domínios personalizados) são configurados em environment groups, e não em environments individuais, e os environments são anexados a environment groups para rotear o tráfego. Para dar a cada environment uma URL distinta, você anexa orders-test e orders-prod a environment groups separados (test e production) e atribui o hostname apropriado a cada environment group. Isso garante que cada environment seja acessível somente por meio de sua URL atribuída. As opções que anexam ambos os environments a um único group (A, B) não conseguem isolar os hostnames por environment, e a opção C adiciona incorretamente os hostnames aos environments em vez de aos environment groups.

questions.question: You are developing an application that uses microservices architecture that includes Cloud Run, Bigtable, and Pub/Sub. You want to conduct the testing and debugging process as quickly as possible to create a minimally viable product with minimal cost. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Shell Editor and Cloud Shell to deploy the application, and test the functionality by using the Google Cloud console in the project.
Use emulators to test the functionality of cloud resources locally, and deploy the code to your Google Cloud project.
Use Cloud Build to create a pipeline, and add the unit testing stage and the manual approval stage. Deploy the code to your Google Cloud project.
Use Cloud Code to develop, deploy, and test microservices resources. Use Cloud Logging to review the resource logs.

questions.correct_text: Use emulators to test the functionality of cloud resources locally, and deploy the code to your Google Cloud project.
questions.explanation: Google provides local emulators for services such as Bigtable and Pub/Sub, letting you test and debug application functionality on your workstation without provisioning or paying for live cloud resources, which gives the fastest iteration loop at minimal cost for an MVP. After validating locally with emulators, you deploy the code to your Google Cloud project. Deploying everything to the project and testing in the console (A) and running a Cloud Build pipeline with manual approval (C) incur cloud costs and are slower for rapid debugging. Cloud Code (D) improves the developer experience but still typically relies on deployed cloud resources, whereas emulators best satisfy the speed-and-low-cost requirement.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O Google fornece emuladores locais para serviços como o Bigtable e o Pub/Sub, permitindo testar e depurar a funcionalidade da aplicação na sua workstation sem provisionar ou pagar por recursos de nuvem em produção, o que oferece o ciclo de iteração mais rápido com custo mínimo para um MVP. Após validar localmente com os emuladores, você implanta o código no seu projeto do Google Cloud. Implantar tudo no projeto e testar no console (A) e executar um pipeline do Cloud Build com aprovação manual (C) geram custos de nuvem e são mais lentos para depuração rápida. O Cloud Code (D) melhora a experiência do desenvolvedor, mas ainda costuma depender de recursos de nuvem implantados, enquanto os emuladores atendem melhor ao requisito de rapidez e baixo custo.

questions.question: You are a lead developer at an organization that recently integrated several Google Cloud services. These services are located within Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) environments that are secured with VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect endpoints. Developers across your organization use different operating systems, development frameworks, and integrated development environments (IDEs). You need to recommend a developer environment that will ensure consistency in the developer process and improve the overall developer experience. You want this solution to:• Enforce consistent security controls.• Have access to Google Cloud resources and applications within the VPC.• Allow the installation of custom tools and utilities on the development environments.What solution should you recommend?

options.text: Use Cloud Workstations, and allow developers to create their own custom images.
Use Cloud Workstations with preconfigured base images. For custom tools and utilities, use custom images that are rebuilt weekly.
Use the Cloud Code extension with the IDEs that are used across the organization. Configure Cloud VPN to enable VPC access.
Use the Cloud Code extension with the IDEs that are used across the organization. Use Identity-Aware Proxy to enable access to the services in the VPC.

questions.correct_text: Use Cloud Workstations with preconfigured base images. For custom tools and utilities, use custom images that are rebuilt weekly.
questions.explanation: Cloud Workstations provides fully managed, secure, browser- or IDE-accessible development environments that run inside your VPC, so they can reach Google Cloud resources protected by VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect while enforcing consistent, centrally managed security controls regardless of the developer's local OS. Using preconfigured base images standardizes the environment, and adding custom images that are rebuilt weekly lets teams install custom tools and utilities while keeping the images patched and under organizational control, which is why B is correct. Option A also uses Cloud Workstations but letting each developer freely build their own images undermines the required consistency and centralized security governance. Options C and D rely on the Cloud Code IDE extension running on each developer's own machine, which does not standardize the environment or enforce consistent security controls, and neither Cloud VPN nor IAP gives the same controlled in-VPC workstation experience that the requirements demand.

topics.exam_domain_name: Construir e testar aplicações

questions.explanation_pt: O Cloud Workstations fornece ambientes de desenvolvimento totalmente gerenciados, seguros e acessíveis via navegador ou IDE, que rodam dentro da sua VPC, de modo que podem acessar recursos do Google Cloud protegidos por VPC Service Controls e Private Service Connect enquanto aplicam controles de segurança consistentes e gerenciados de forma centralizada, independentemente do SO local do desenvolvedor. Usar imagens base pré-configuradas padroniza o ambiente, e adicionar imagens personalizadas que são reconstruídas semanalmente permite que as equipes instalem ferramentas e utilitários personalizados mantendo as imagens atualizadas com patches e sob controle organizacional, e é por isso que B está correta. A opção A também usa o Cloud Workstations, mas permitir que cada desenvolvedor crie livremente suas próprias imagens prejudica a consistência exigida e a governança de segurança centralizada. As opções C e D dependem da extensão do IDE Cloud Code rodando na máquina de cada desenvolvedor, o que não padroniza o ambiente nem aplica controles de segurança consistentes, e nem o Cloud VPN nem o IAP oferecem a mesma experiência controlada de workstation dentro da VPC que os requisitos exigem.

questions.question: You are preparing to conduct a load test on your Cloud Run service by using JMeter. You need to orchestrate the steps and services to use for an effective load test and analysis. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Install JMeter on your local machine, create a log sink to BigQuery, and use Looker to analyze the results.
Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to a Cloud Storage bucket, and use Looker Studio to analyze the results.
Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to a Cloud Storage bucket, and use Looker to analyze the results.
Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to BigQuery, and use Looker Studio to analyze the results.

questions.correct_text: Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to BigQuery, and use Looker Studio to analyze the results.
questions.explanation: For load testing a Cloud Run service, the recommended approach is to run the load generator (JMeter) on a Compute Engine instance so it has stable, high-bandwidth network capacity rather than depending on a local machine, which is why options on a Compute Engine instance are preferred over A. To analyze large volumes of load-test logs effectively, you route the logs via a log sink to BigQuery for scalable querying and then visualize results with Looker Studio, which natively connects to BigQuery and is the appropriate free reporting tool here. Option D matches all of these: Compute Engine plus JMeter, a log sink to BigQuery, and Looker Studio. Options B and C send logs only to a Cloud Storage bucket, which is not directly queryable for analysis, and option C additionally specifies Looker (the enterprise BI platform) rather than Looker Studio.

Para analisar grandes volumes de logs de teste de carga de forma eficaz, você roteia os logs por um log sink para o BigQuery, permitindo consultas escaláveis, e então visualiza os resultados com o Looker Studio, que se conecta nativamente ao BigQuery e é a ferramenta de relatórios gratuita apropriada neste caso. questions.question: You are designing a Node.js-based mobile news feed application that stores data on Google Cloud. You need to select the application's database. You want the database to have zonal resiliency out of the box, low latency responses, ACID compliance, an optional middle tier, semi-structured data storage, and network-partition-tolerant and offline-mode client libraries. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Firestore and use the Firestore client library in the app.
Configure Bigtable and use the Bigtable client in the app.
Configure Cloud SQL and use the Google Client Library for Cloud SQL in the app.
Configure BigQuery and use the BigQuery REST API in the app.

questions.correct_text: Configure Firestore and use the Firestore client library in the app.
questions.explanation: Firestore is the right choice because it natively provides zonal/multi-zone resiliency out of the box, low-latency reads and writes, ACID transactions, semi-structured (document) data storage, and mobile/web client libraries that support offline mode and are tolerant of network partitions, all of which the news feed app requires. It also fits a Node.js mobile application with an optional middle tier through its server and client SDKs. Bigtable (B) is a wide-column NoSQL store optimized for very high throughput analytics and time series, lacks multi-row ACID transactions, and has no offline mobile client libraries. Cloud SQL (C) is a relational database without offline-capable mobile client libraries, and BigQuery (D) is an analytical data warehouse, not a low-latency transactional operational database for a mobile feed.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Firestore é a escolha certa porque oferece nativamente resiliência zonal/multi-zona pronta para uso, leituras e gravações de baixa latência, transações ACID, armazenamento de dados semiestruturados (documentos) e bibliotecas de cliente para mobile/web que suportam modo offline e são tolerantes a partições de rede — tudo o que o app de feed de notícias exige. Ele também se adapta bem a uma aplicação mobile em Node.js com uma camada intermediária opcional, por meio de seus SDKs de servidor e de cliente. O Bigtable (B) é um armazenamento NoSQL de colunas largas otimizado para análises de altíssima taxa de transferência e séries temporais, não possui transações ACID de múltiplas linhas e não tem bibliotecas de cliente mobile com suporte offline. O Cloud SQL (C) é um banco de dados relacional sem bibliotecas de cliente mobile com capacidade offline, e o BigQuery (D) é um data warehouse analítico, não um banco de dados operacional transacional de baixa latência para um feed mobile.

questions.question: You are developing an application component to capture user behavior data and stream the data to BigQuery. You plan to use the BigQuery Storage Write API. You need to ensure that the data that arrives in BigQuery does not have any duplicates. You want to use the simplest operational method to achieve this. What should you do?

options.text: Create a write stream in the default type.
Create a write stream in the committed type.
Configure a Kafka cluster. Use a primary universally unique identifier (UUID) for duplicate messages.
Configure a Pub/Sub topic. Use Cloud Functions to subscribe to the topic and remove any duplicates.

questions.correct_text: Create a write stream in the committed type.
questions.explanation: The BigQuery Storage Write API offers different stream types, and the committed type writes records that are immediately available for query while also supporting exactly-once delivery semantics through stream offsets, which lets the client deduplicate writes simply by tracking offsets, making B the simplest operational way to avoid duplicates. The default stream (A) provides at-least-once semantics and does not give the offset-based exactly-once guarantee, so duplicates can occur. Introducing a Kafka cluster (C) or a Pub/Sub topic with Cloud Functions deduplication (D) adds substantial extra infrastructure and operational complexity, which contradicts the requirement for the simplest method when the Write API itself can provide deduplication.

topics.exam_domain_name: Integrar aplicações com serviços do Google Cloud

questions.explanation_pt: A BigQuery Storage Write API oferece diferentes tipos de stream, e o tipo committed grava registros que ficam imediatamente disponíveis para consulta, ao mesmo tempo em que oferece semântica de entrega exactly-once por meio de stream offsets, o que permite ao cliente deduplicar gravações simplesmente rastreando os offsets, tornando B a maneira operacional mais simples de evitar duplicatas. O default stream (A) oferece semântica at-least-once e não fornece a garantia de exactly-once baseada em offsets, portanto duplicatas podem ocorrer. Introduzir um cluster Kafka (C) ou um tópico do Pub/Sub com deduplicação via Cloud Functions (D) adiciona infraestrutura extra substancial e complexidade operacional, o que contradiz o requisito do método mais simples, já que a própria Write API pode fornecer a deduplicação.

questions.question: You maintain a popular mobile game deployed on Google Cloud services that include Firebase, Firestore, and Cloud Functions. Recently, the game experienced a surge in usage, and the application encountered HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED errors when accessing the Firestore API. The application has now stabilized. You want to quickly fix this issue because your company has a marketing campaign next week and you expect another surge in usage. What should you do?

options.text: Request a quota increase, and modify the application code to retry the Firestore API call with fixed backoff.
Request a quota increase, and modify the application code to retry the Firestore API call with exponential backoff.
Optimize database queries to reduce read/write operations, and modify the application code to retry the Firestore API call with fixed backoff.
Optimize database queries to reduce read/write operations, and modify the application code to retry the Firestore API call with exponential backoff.

questions.correct_text: Optimize database queries to reduce read/write operations, and modify the application code to retry the Firestore API call with exponential backoff.
questions.explanation: HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED errors indicate the application is hitting Firestore limits, so the durable fix combines reducing load by optimizing queries to lower read/write operations with resilient client behavior using exponential backoff (ideally with jitter) on retries, which is Google's recommended retry strategy and prevents retry storms during the next surge, making D correct. Exponential backoff is preferred over fixed backoff because fixed-interval retries from many clients can synchronize and re-overwhelm the service, which rules out options A and C that use fixed backoff. While requesting a quota increase (A and B) can help, simply retrying without optimizing the underlying query load does not address the root cause of excessive operations, so optimizing queries plus exponential backoff is the most effective and recommended combination.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: Erros HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED indicam que a aplicação está atingindo os limites do Firestore, então a correção duradoura combina a redução de carga otimizando as consultas para diminuir as operações de leitura/gravação com um comportamento resiliente do cliente usando exponential backoff (idealmente com jitter) nas novas tentativas, que é a estratégia de retry recomendada pelo Google e evita tempestades de retentativas durante o próximo pico, tornando D correta. O exponential backoff é preferível ao fixed backoff porque novas tentativas em intervalo fixo de muitos clientes podem se sincronizar e sobrecarregar novamente o serviço, o que descarta as opções A e C, que usam fixed backoff. Embora solicitar um aumento de cota (A e B) possa ajudar, simplesmente retentar sem otimizar a carga de consultas subjacente não resolve a causa raiz do excesso de operações, portanto otimizar as consultas mais exponential backoff é a combinação mais eficaz e recomendada.

questions.question: You are developing a mobile application that allows users to create and manage to-do lists. Your application has the following requirements:• Store and synchronize data between different mobile devices.• Support offline access.• Provide real-time updates on each user's device.You need to implement a database solution while minimizing operational effort. Which approach should you use?

options.text: Create a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance. Implement a data model to store to-do list information. Create indexes for the most heavily and frequently used queries.
Create a Bigtable instance. Design a database schema to avoid hotspots when writing data. Use a Bigtable change stream to capture data changes.
Use Firestore as the database. Configure Firestore offline persistence to cache a copy of the Firestore data. Listen to document changes to update applications whenever there are document changes.
Implement a SQLite database on each user's device. Use a scheduled job to synchronize each device database with a copy stored in Cloud Storage.

questions.correct_text: Use Firestore as the database. Configure Firestore offline persistence to cache a copy of the Firestore data. Listen to document changes to update applications whenever there are document changes.
questions.explanation: Firestore is the ideal managed solution because it natively provides cross-device data synchronization, offline persistence (a local cache that automatically syncs when connectivity returns), and real-time listeners that push document changes to clients instantly. This satisfies all three requirements while minimizing operational effort, since Firestore is fully serverless and requires no instance management. Cloud SQL for MySQL (A) offers no built-in offline caching or real-time client updates, so the app developer would have to build synchronization manually. Bigtable (B) is a wide-column store for large analytical/time-series workloads and lacks offline mobile SDK support and real-time client listeners. A SQLite plus Cloud Storage scheduled job (D) adds significant custom code, is not real-time, and conflicts can occur during sync.

topics.exam_domain_name: Projetar apps cloud-native escaláveis, seguras e confiáveis

questions.explanation_pt: O Firestore é a solução gerenciada ideal porque oferece nativamente sincronização de dados entre dispositivos, persistência offline (um cache local que sincroniza automaticamente quando a conectividade retorna) e real-time listeners que enviam alterações de documentos aos clientes instantaneamente. Isso atende a todos os três requisitos enquanto minimiza o esforço operacional, já que o Firestore é totalmente serverless e não exige gerenciamento de instâncias. O Cloud SQL for MySQL (A) não oferece cache offline integrado nem atualizações de cliente em tempo real, então o desenvolvedor do app teria que construir a sincronização manualmente. O Bigtable (B) é um armazenamento de colunas largas para grandes cargas analíticas/de séries temporais e não tem suporte a SDK mobile offline nem real-time listeners de cliente. Uma solução com SQLite mais job agendado do Cloud Storage (D) adiciona código personalizado significativo, não é em tempo real e podem ocorrer conflitos durante a sincronização.

questions.question: You manage an application deployed on GKE clusters across multiple environments. You are using Cloud Build to run user acceptance testing (UAT) tests. You have integrated Cloud Build with Artifact Analysis, and enabled the Binary Authorization API in all Google Cloud projects hosting your environments. You want only container images that have passed certain automated UAT tests to be deployed to the production environment. You have already created an attestor. What should you do next?

options.text: After the UAT phase, sign the attestation with a key stored as a Kubernetes secret. Add a GKE cluster-specific rule in Binary Authorization for the UAT Google Cloud project.
After the UAT phase, sign the attestation with a key stored as a Kubernetes secret. Add a GKE cluster-specific rule in Binary Authorization for the production Google Cloud project policy.
After the UAT phase, sign the attestation with a key stored in Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Add a default rule in Binary Authorization for the UAT Google Cloud project.

After the UAT phase, sign the attestation with a key stored in Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Add a GKE cluster-specific rule in Binary Authorization for the production Google Cloud project policy.

questions.correct_text: After the UAT phase, sign the attestation with a key stored in Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Add a GKE cluster-specific rule in Binary Authorization for the production Google Cloud project policy.
questions.explanation: To gate production deployments, the attestation must be signed with a securely managed key and Binary Authorization must enforce the rule in the production project, since that is where the policy controls what GKE can run. Storing the signing key in Cloud KMS is the recommended secure practice over a Kubernetes secret, which is only base64-encoded and accessible within the cluster. The rule must be applied to the production project's policy (not the UAT project) because the goal is to block unattested images specifically from production. Options A and B store the key insecurely as a Kubernetes secret, and C applies the rule to the UAT project, which would not protect production.
